english_sentences: But one must triturate the metallic drugs in the most acrid vinegar, as old as possible and thinnest in consistency, avoiding thickness of consistency; and it is better that the trituration of the drugs take place [611] in the summer sun.

Some of the metallic substances do not even need to be pounded or sifted, since they are easily dissolved by the vinegar, as chalcitis and misy; but some require both to be pounded and sifted, like the scale of copper.

Now when I first prepared the drug, I also put arsenic (arrhenikon) into it, but afterwards it seemed to me superfluous; for it appeared to me that the drug would be sufficiently composed by means of the scale of copper, the misy and the chalcitis.
In the first composition I also mixed in burnt verdigris (ios), for I suspected the unburnt of biting beyond what is appropriate.

Afterwards, however, I also put in a little unburnt, small in relation to the proportion of the others; and so too with chalcitis: if I put it in raw, I mixed in a very small quantity, but if burnt, a quantity equal to the misy and the scale of copper.
And of all the preparations I both expected and found by experience to be best the one in which the scale of copper was in the greatest quantity, burnt chalcitis second, and then misy.

beads.greek: λειούσθω δ’ οὖν, ὡς ἔφην, ἐν ἡλίῳ θέρους ὥρᾳ πολλαῖς ﻿ [612] ἐφεξῆς ἡμέραις ἅττ’ ἄν μίξεις φάρμακα δι’ ὄξους δριμυτάτου.
beads.english: So then, as I said, let whatever drugs you are going to mix be triturated in the sun in the summer season for many [612] successive days, in the most acrid vinegar.

beads.greek: ὅσῳ γὰρ ἐν πλείονι χρόνῳ λειωθῆ, τοσούτῳ γίγνεται λεπτομερέστερα καὶ διὰ τοῦτο χρησιμώτερα πρὸς τὰς στενὰς τρώσεις, ὡς ἐπί γε τῶν γεγυμνωμένων νεύρων φυλάττεσθαι χρὴ τὰ λίαν λεπτομερῆ τε καὶ διαβρωτικά.
beads.english: For the longer the time over which they are triturated, the more fine-particled they become and for this reason the more useful for narrow wounds, whereas in the case of exposed nerves at least one must guard against those that are excessively fine-particled and corrosive.

beads.greek: διὰ τοῦτο δὲ οἱ εἰρημένοι τροχίσκοι πᾶσι τοῖς τοιούτοις χρήσιμοι, προσειλήφασι γάρ τινα καὶ τῶν στυφόντων.
beads.english: For this reason the aforementioned trochisks are useful in all such cases, for they have taken on in addition some of the astringent substances as well.

beads.greek: ἔνδοξοι δ’ αὐτῶν εἰσὶν ὅ τε τοῦ Ἄνδρωνος καὶ ὁ τοῦ Πολυείδους καὶ ὁ τοῦ Πασίωνος.
beads.english: Renowned among them are that of Andron, that of Polyeides and that of Pasion.

beads.greek: ἔστι δὲ καὶ ἄλλος τις τέταρτος καὶ πέμπτος, οἷς ἐγὼ συνήθως χρῶμαι, τούτων ἰσχυρότερος.
beads.english: There is also another, a fourth and a fifth, which I habitually use, stronger than these.

beads.greek: ῥηθήσονται δ’ αὐτῶν αἱ ἀκριβεῖς συμμετρίαι προήκοντος τοῦ λόγου.
beads.english: Their exact proportions will be stated as the discourse proceeds.

beads.greek: νυνὶ μέντοι τοσοῦτον εἰρήσθω περὶ τῆς χρήσεως αὐτῶν, ὡς χρὴ λειωθέντας αὐτοὺς ξηροὺς μετὰ ταῦτα πάλιν ἐπιβαλόντα σίραιον οὕτως λειοῦν, ἄχρι τοῦ γλοιῶδές τε γενέσθαι τὸ φάρμακον καὶ λεῖον ὁμαλῶς.
beads.english: For now, however, let only this much be said about their use: that one must, once they have been triturated dry, thereafter again add siraion and triturate them in this way, until the drug becomes glutinous and evenly smooth.

beads.greek: ὀνομάζουσι δὲ νῦν καὶ σίραιον τοῦτο παρ’ ἡμῖν ἅπαντες, ἕψημα τοῦ γλεύκους ἑψομένου γινόμενον.
beads.english: Nowadays everyone among us also calls this siraion, the boiled-down must (hepsema) that is produced when the must is boiled.

beads.greek: ἔστω δὲ καὶ τοῦτο μηδὲν οἰνῶδες ἔχον.
beads.english: And let this too have nothing winy about it.

greek_sentences: λειούσθω δ’ οὖν, ὡς ἔφην, ἐν ἡλίῳ θέρους ὥρᾳ πολλαῖς ﻿ [612] ἐφεξῆς ἡμέραις ἅττ’ ἄν μίξεις φάρμακα δι’ ὄξους δριμυτάτου.

ὅσῳ γὰρ ἐν πλείονι χρόνῳ λειωθῆ, τοσούτῳ γίγνεται λεπτομερέστερα καὶ διὰ τοῦτο χρησιμώτερα πρὸς τὰς στενὰς τρώσεις, ὡς ἐπί γε τῶν γεγυμνωμένων νεύρων φυλάττεσθαι χρὴ τὰ λίαν λεπτομερῆ τε καὶ διαβρωτικά.
διὰ τοῦτο δὲ οἱ εἰρημένοι τροχίσκοι πᾶσι τοῖς τοιούτοις χρήσιμοι, προσειλήφασι γάρ τινα καὶ τῶν στυφόντων.
ἔνδοξοι δ’ αὐτῶν εἰσὶν ὅ τε τοῦ Ἄνδρωνος καὶ ὁ τοῦ Πολυείδους καὶ ὁ τοῦ Πασίωνος.
ἔστι δὲ καὶ ἄλλος τις τέταρτος καὶ πέμπτος, οἷς ἐγὼ συνήθως χρῶμαι, τούτων ἰσχυρότερος.
ῥηθήσονται δ’ αὐτῶν αἱ ἀκριβεῖς συμμετρίαι προήκοντος τοῦ λόγου.
νυνὶ μέντοι τοσοῦτον εἰρήσθω περὶ τῆς χρήσεως αὐτῶν, ὡς χρὴ λειωθέντας αὐτοὺς ξηροὺς μετὰ ταῦτα πάλιν ἐπιβαλόντα σίραιον οὕτως λειοῦν, ἄχρι τοῦ γλοιῶδές τε γενέσθαι τὸ φάρμακον καὶ λεῖον ὁμαλῶς.
ὀνομάζουσι δὲ νῦν καὶ σίραιον τοῦτο παρ’ ἡμῖν ἅπαντες, ἕψημα τοῦ γλεύκους ἑψομένου γινόμενον.
ἔστω δὲ καὶ τοῦτο μηδὲν οἰνῶδες ἔχον.
english_sentences: So then, as I said, let whatever drugs you are going to mix be triturated in the sun in the summer season for many [612] successive days, in the most acrid vinegar.

For the longer the time over which they are triturated, the more fine-particled they become and for this reason the more useful for narrow wounds, whereas in the case of exposed nerves at least one must guard against those that are excessively fine-particled and corrosive.
For this reason the aforementioned trochisks are useful in all such cases, for they have taken on in addition some of the astringent substances as well.
Renowned among them are that of Andron, that of Polyeides and that of Pasion.
There is also another, a fourth and a fifth, which I habitually use, stronger than these.
Their exact proportions will be stated as the discourse proceeds.

For now, however, let only this much be said about their use: that one must, once they have been triturated dry, thereafter again add siraion and triturate them in this way, until the drug becomes glutinous and evenly smooth.
Nowadays everyone among us also calls this siraion, the boiled-down must (hepsema) that is produced when the must is boiled.
And let this too have nothing winy about it.

beads.greek: γίγνεται δὲ καὶ τοιοῦτον μήτε ἐξ αὐστηρῶν σταφυλῶν ὄντος τοῦ γλεύκους, [613] ἀλλ’ ὡς ἔνι μάλιστα γλυκειῶν, μήτε ἐκ τοῦ πρώτου ῥέοντος, ἀλλ’ ἐκ τοῦ τελευταίου.
beads.english: And it becomes such when the must is neither from austere grapes, [613] but from grapes as sweet as possible, nor from what flows first, but from what flows last.

beads.greek: εἰ μὲν οὖν εἴη τὸ γλεῦκος τοιοῦτον, ἕψειν αὐτὸ χρὴ μέχρις ἂν ἥμισυ λειφθῇ τοῦ κατὰ τὴν ἀρχὴν ἐμβληθέντος· εἰ δὲ μὴ τοιοῦτον, μέχρι τοῦ τὸ τρίτον ἀπολειφθῆναι καθεψητέον ἐστί.
beads.english: If, then, the must is of this kind, one must boil it until half of what was put in at the beginning is left; but if it is not of this kind, it must be boiled down until a third is left.

beads.greek: τοιούτῳ μὲν ἑψήματι διαλύειν χρὴ τοὺς τροχίσκους, ὥστε μελιτώδη σύστασιν ἔχοντας ἀναληφθέντας μοτοῖς, ἐπιτίθεσθαι τοῖς γεγυμνωμένοις νεύροις καὶ μάλιστα τοὺς μετριωτέρους αὐτῶν, ὁποῖός ἐστιν ὁ τοῦ Πολυείδους, καὶ πολὺ δὴ μᾶλλον, ἐὰν ἁπαλόσαρκον ᾖ τὸ σῶμα, καθ’ ὃ καὶ τελέως ἀποχωρεῖν ἀσφαλέστερόν ἐστι τῆς τῶν τροχίσκων χρήσεως, ἑτέροις χρώμενον φαρμάκοις, ὑπὲρ ὧν ἤδη τε προείρηται καὶ αὖθις εἰρήσεται.
beads.english: With boiled-down must (hepsema) of this kind one must dissolve the troches, so that, having a honey-like consistency and taken up on lint plugs, they are applied to the exposed nerves—and especially the more moderate of them, such as that of Polyeides, and indeed much more so if the body is soft-fleshed, in which case it is also safer to withdraw entirely from the use of the troches, employing other drugs, about which something has already been said before and will be said again.

greek_sentences: γίγνεται δὲ καὶ τοιοῦτον μήτε ἐξ αὐστηρῶν σταφυλῶν ὄντος τοῦ γλεύκους, [613] ἀλλ’ ὡς ἔνι μάλιστα γλυκειῶν, μήτε ἐκ τοῦ πρώτου ῥέοντος, ἀλλ’ ἐκ τοῦ τελευταίου.
εἰ μὲν οὖν εἴη τὸ γλεῦκος τοιοῦτον, ἕψειν αὐτὸ χρὴ μέχρις ἂν ἥμισυ λειφθῇ τοῦ κατὰ τὴν ἀρχὴν ἐμβληθέντος· εἰ δὲ μὴ τοιοῦτον, μέχρι τοῦ τὸ τρίτον ἀπολειφθῆναι καθεψητέον ἐστί.

english_sentences: And it becomes such when the must is neither from austere grapes, [613] but from grapes as sweet as possible, nor from what flows first, but from what flows last.
If, then, the must is of this kind, one must boil it until half of what was put in at the beginning is left; but if it is not of this kind, it must be boiled down until a third is left.

With boiled-down must (hepsema) of this kind one must dissolve the troches, so that, having a honey-like consistency and taken up on lint plugs, they are applied to the exposed nerves—and especially the more moderate of them, such as that of Polyeides, and indeed much more so if the body is soft-fleshed, in which case it is also safer to withdraw entirely from the use of the troches, employing other drugs, about which something has already been said before and will be said again.

beads.greek: σκεπασθέντος δὲ τοῦ γεγυμνωμένου νεύρου τοῖς μοτοῖς ἔξωθεν ἐπιβλητέον ἕν τι τῶν πρὸς τὰς στενὰς τρώσεις ἁρμοττόντων, ὧν ἐστι τέτταρα γένη, τουτὶ μὲν ἓν τὸ διὰ τῶν μεταλλικῶν, ὑπὲρ οὗ πρόκειται λέγειν, ἕτερον δὲ τὸ διὰ τῶν ὀπῶν, ἐν οἶς ἐστι καὶ τὸ δι’ εὐφορβίου, καὶ τρίτον τὸ διὰ τῆς κόπρου τῶν περιστερῶν, καὶ τέταρτον, ὃ καλῶ τὸ πρᾷον, ᾧ καὶ πρὸς τὰ τελέως γεγυμνωμένα νεῦρα τῶν [614] ἁπαλοσάρκων σωμάτων χρῶμαι.
beads.english: Once the laid-bare nerve has been covered with the lint-plugs, one must apply on the outside one of the drugs suited to narrow wounds, of which there are four kinds: this one, the drug made of metallic substances, about which it is proposed to speak; another, the drug made of juices, among which is also the one made with euphorbium; a third, the drug made of pigeons' dung; and a fourth, which I call the mild one, which I use also for the completely laid-bare nerves of [614] soft-fleshed bodies.

beads.greek: τούτων τῶν τεττάρων ἕν τι περιβάλλειν χρὴ παντὶ τῷ πεπονθότι μορίῳ συνεπιλαμβάνοντα πολὺ καὶ τῶν ὑγιεινῶν μερῶν καὶ μάλιστα τῶν ὑπερκειμένων, οἷς καὶ τὴν κατάντλησιν ποιεῖσθαι χρὴ δὶς τῆς ἡμέρας ἢ τρὶς, ἐὰν ἐπείγῃ.
beads.english: One of these four must be placed around the whole affected part, taking in also a good deal of the healthy parts, and especially those lying above, on which one must also perform the affusion twice a day, or three times, if it is urgent.

beads.greek: καὶ μέντοι καὶ τῆς νυκτὸς ἐνίοτε τῶν μὲν μοτῶν ἐπικειμένων κατὰ τοῦ γεγυμνωμένου νεύρου, τοῦ δ’ ἐπιβεβλημένου κατ’ αὐτῶν ἔξωθεν αἰρομένου.
beads.english: And indeed sometimes also at night, the lint-plugs remaining in place upon the laid-bare nerve, while the drug applied over them from outside is removed.

beads.greek: παμπόλλης δ’ οὔσης διαφορᾶς τῶν ἀνθρωπίνων σωμάτων κατά τε τὰς ἐξ ἀρχῆς αὐτῶν κράσεις καὶ τὰς τῶν ἡλικιῶν μεταβολὰς, ἔτι τε πρὸς τούτοις τὰ ἐπιτηδεύματα τὸ συντιθέμενον φάρμακον ἀδύνατον ἅπασιν ἁρμόττειν.
beads.english: But since there is a very great difference among human bodies both in respect of their original mixtures and the changes of the ages of life, and further, in addition to these, their pursuits, it is impossible for the compounded drug to be fitting for all.

beads.greek: ἔστω τοίνυν διὰ τοῦτό σοι δύο παρεσκευασμένα, τὸ μὲν ἕτερον ἰσχυρότερον τῶν ὁμογενῶν, τὸ δὲ ἕτερον πρᾳότερον, ἃ μιγνὺς ἀλλήλοις ἐπὶ τῆς χρείας, ἐργάσῃ πάμπολλα τὰ μεταξὺ παρὰ τὸ ποσὸν τῆς μίξεως.
beads.english: Therefore, on this account, let there be two prepared for you, the one stronger among those of the same kind, the other milder; mixing these with one another at the time of use, you will produce very many intermediate drugs according to the quantity of the mixture.

beads.greek: ἐὰν γὰρ ἴσον ἑκατέρου μίξῃς, ἔσται σοι τὸ μιχθὲν ἀκριβῶς ἀμφοῖν μέσον. ἐὰν δὲ θατέρου πλέον, ἐπὶ τοσοῦτον ἀποκεχωρηκὸς τοῦ μέσου πρὸς ἐκεῖνο τῶν ἄκρων, ἐφ’ ὅσον ἡ μίξις ὑπερέσχεν.
beads.english: For if you mix an equal amount of each, the mixture will be for you exactly the mean between both; but if more of one, it will have departed from the mean towards that one of the extremes to the degree that the mixture exceeded.

παμπόλλης δ’ οὔσης διαφορᾶς τῶν ἀνθρωπίνων σωμάτων κατά τε τὰς ἐξ ἀρχῆς αὐτῶν κράσεις καὶ τὰς τῶν ἡλικιῶν μεταβολὰς, ἔτι τε πρὸς τούτοις τὰ ἐπιτηδεύματα τὸ συντιθέμενον φάρμακον ἀδύνατον ἅπασιν ἁρμόττειν.

ἐὰν γὰρ ἴσον ἑκατέρου μίξῃς, ἔσται σοι τὸ μιχθὲν ἀκριβῶς ἀμφοῖν μέσον.
ἐὰν δὲ θατέρου πλέον, ἐπὶ τοσοῦτον ἀποκεχωρηκὸς τοῦ μέσου πρὸς ἐκεῖνο τῶν ἄκρων, ἐφ’ ὅσον ἡ μίξις ὑπερέσχεν.
english_sentences: Once the laid-bare nerve has been covered with the lint-plugs, one must apply on the outside one of the drugs suited to narrow wounds, of which there are four kinds: this one, the drug made of metallic substances, about which it is proposed to speak; another, the drug made of juices, among which is also the one made with euphorbium; a third, the drug made of pigeons' dung; and a fourth, which I call the mild one, which I use also for the completely laid-bare nerves of [614] soft-fleshed bodies.

One of these four must be placed around the whole affected part, taking in also a good deal of the healthy parts, and especially those lying above, on which one must also perform the affusion twice a day, or three times, if it is urgent.
And indeed sometimes also at night, the lint-plugs remaining in place upon the laid-bare nerve, while the drug applied over them from outside is removed.

But since there is a very great difference among human bodies both in respect of their original mixtures and the changes of the ages of life, and further, in addition to these, their pursuits, it is impossible for the compounded drug to be fitting for all.

Therefore, on this account, let there be two prepared for you, the one stronger among those of the same kind, the other milder; mixing these with one another at the time of use, you will produce very many intermediate drugs according to the quantity of the mixture.

For if you mix an equal amount of each, the mixture will be for you exactly the mean between both; but if more of one, it will have departed from the mean towards that one of the extremes to the degree that the mixture exceeded.

beads.greek: ἔστω τοίνυν τὸ μὲν ἰσχυρότατον [615] τῶν μεταλλικῶν ἐκ τούτων συγκείμενον· ἓν μὲν ἐχέτω μέρος τῆς ὠμῆς χαλκίτεως, δύο δὲ τοῦ μίσυος ὡσαύτως ὠμοῦ, τρία δὲ τῆς τοῦ χαλκοῦ λεπίδος· τὸ δ’ ἀσθενέστατον, ἓν μὲν ὡσαύτως μίσυός τε καὶ χαλκίτεως, ἀλλὰ κεκαυμένων ἀμφοτέρων, τῆς δὲ λεπίδος τέτταρα.
beads.english: Let, then, the strongest [615] of the metallic ones be composed of these: let it have one part of raw chalcitis, two of misy, likewise raw, and three of scale of copper; and the weakest, likewise one of misy and of chalcitis, but both burnt, and four of the scale.

beads.greek: καὶ μέντοι καὶ μέσον ἀμφοῖν, ᾧ κέχρημαι πολλάκις, ἔστω τοιόνδε. μίσυος καὶ χαλκίτεως καὶ ἰοῦ, κεκαυμένων ἁπάντων ἓν ἑκάστου μέρος, τῆς δὲ λεπίδος τοῦ χαλκοῦ μέρη τρία.
beads.english: And indeed let the one intermediate between both, which I have often used, be as follows: of misy and chalcitis and verdigris, all burnt, one part of each, and of scale of copper three parts.

beads.greek: τούτοις οὖν ὡς προείρηκα λειωθεῖσι μιγνύσθω κηροῦ κατὰ μὲν τὸ ἰσχυρότατον τὸ διπλάσιον, κατὰ δὲ τὸ ἀσθενέστατον δύο καὶ ἥμισυ μέρη, κατὰ δὲ τὸ μέσον ὃ μεταξὺ τούτων ἐστὶ μέρη δύο καὶ τέταρτον οἷον ἐπὶ τοῦ πρώτου γεγραμμένου τῶν τριῶν, ὅπερ ἰσχυρότατον ἔφην εἶναι, τὰ πάντα μέρη γίγνεται τὸν ἀριθμὸν ἐκ μίσυος καὶ χαλκίτεως καὶ λεπίδος ἀθροιζόμενα ἕξ.
beads.english: To these, then, ground fine as I have said before, let wax be mixed: in the case of the strongest, double; in the case of the weakest, two and a half parts; and in the case of the middle one, which lies between these, two parts and a quarter. For example, in the case of the first of the three written down, which I said was the strongest, the total parts assembled from misy and chalcitis and scale come to six in number.

beads.greek: τούτοις οὖν ἐπιβαλεῖς κηροῦ μέρη ιβ΄.
beads.english: To these, then, you will add twelve parts of wax.

beads.greek: κατὰ δὲ τὸ ἀσθενέστατον, ἐὰν ἓξ ᾖ μέρη τῶν μεταλλικῶν, μέρη ιβ΄. βάλλῃς κηροῦ, τὸ μεταξὺ δὲ ἐπὶ τοῦ μέσου.
beads.english: And in the case of the weakest, if there are six parts of the metallic substances, you would put in twelve parts of wax, and in the case of the middle one the amount between.

beads.greek: μεταξὺ δ’ ἔτι τῶν ὀκτωκαίδεκα καὶ δώδεκα τὰ πέντε καὶ δέκα.
beads.english: And again, between eighteen and twelve lies fifteen.

beads.greek: ὑποθῇς τὸ ἓν εἶναι μέρος ἁπάντων δηλονότι, τοσαύτας [616] βάλλῃς δραχμὰς, ὅσα περ τὰ μέρη, ἐάν τε οὐγγίαν ἢ λίτραν, οὕτω γὰρ εἴθισται παρὰ τοῖς Ῥωμαίοις ὀνομάζεσθαι, τοσαύτας οὐγγίας ἢ λίτρας.
beads.english: you posit the one part to be one drachma—of all the ingredients, clearly—you put in as many [616] drachmas as there are parts; and if an ounce or a litra (for so it is customary among the Romans to name them), as many ounces or litras.

beads.greek: ἔστι δὲ παρ’ αὐτοῖς μέτρον, ᾧ τὸ ἔλαιον μετροῦσιν ἐντετμημένον γραμμαῖς διαιρούσαις τὸ σύμπαν εἰς μέρη ιβ΄. καὶ καλεῖται μὲν τὸ ὅλον μέτρον ὑπ’ αὐτῶν λίτρα, τὸ δωδέκατον δ’ αὐτῆς οὐγγία.
beads.english: There is among them a measure, with which they measure oil, incised with lines that divide the whole into twelve parts; and the whole measure is called by them a litra, and the twelfth part of it an ounce.

beads.greek: τὰ μὲν οὖν μεταλλικὰ καὶ ὁ κηρὸς ἐπὶ ζυγοῦ δι’ ἑτέρας οὐγγίας ἵσταται, τὸ δ’ ἔλαιον τῷ κέρατι μετρεῖται.
beads.english: The metallic substances and the wax, then, are weighed on a balance by means of a different ounce, whereas the oil is measured by the horn.

beads.greek: βαλλέσθω τοίνυν εἰς τὰ προειρημένα φάρμακα πάντα κατὰ τὴν ἀναλογίαν τοῦ κηροῦ τὸ ἔλαιον, ἐν ἅπασιν αὐτοῖς τὸ ἥμισυ πλεονάζον, ὥστε ἐὰν ὁ κηρὸς ᾖ γο η΄. τὸ ἔλαιον βάλλεται γο ιβ΄.
beads.english: Let the oil, therefore, be put into all the aforesaid drugs in proportion to the wax, exceeding it by half in all of them, so that if the wax is 8 ounces, the oil put in is 12 ounces, that is, the whole litra.

beads.greek: τουτέστιν ὅλην τὴν λίτραν. ἔστω δὲ τὸ ἔλαιον ὅμοιον τῷ Σαβίνῳ λεπτομερές τε καὶ στύψεως ἥκιστα μετέχον.
beads.english: And let the oil be like the Sabine, fine-particled and partaking least of astringency; and it is better if it is also old.

beads.greek: ἄμεινον δ’ εἰ καὶ παλαιὸν εἴη. τὸ δ’ ὠμοτριβὲς ὀνομαζόμενον καὶ τὸ μετὰ θαλλῶν ἐλαίας ἐσκευασμένον οὐκ ἐπιτήδειον.
beads.english: But the oil called omotribes (of unripe olives) and that prepared with olive shoots are not suitable.

And let the oil be like the Sabine, fine-particled and partaking least of astringency; and it is better if it is also old.
But the oil called omotribes (of unripe olives) and that prepared with olive shoots are not suitable.

beads.greek: ἅπασι δὲ τοῖς εἰρημένοις φαρμάκοις, ὅταν ἐν τῇ θυείᾳ τὰ μεταλλικὰ πλείοσιν ἡμέραις τριφθῇ μετ’ ὄξους, ἐπεμβαλλέσθω λιβανωτὸς ὁ λευκότατός τε καὶ λιπαρὸς, ﻿ [617] εἶτα πάλιν ἅμα τοῖς μεταλλικοῖς λειούσθω τινὰς ἡμέρας, πρὶν τὴν κηρωτὴν αὐτοῖς ἐπιμίγνυσθαι.
beads.english: To all the drugs mentioned, when the metallic substances have been triturated in the mortar for several days with vinegar, let frankincense—the whitest and oily kind—be added in, [617] and then let it again be ground fine together with the metallic substances for some days, before the cerate is mixed in with them.

beads.greek: ὅσον δ’ ἂν ἐξ ἁπάντων τῶν μεταλλικῶν ἀθροίζηται πλῆθος, τούτου τὸ ἥμισυ μέρος ὁ λιβανωτὸς ἐχέτω.
beads.english: Whatever quantity is gathered from all the metallic substances together, let the frankincense amount to half of that.

beads.greek: εἰ δὲ μαλακώτερον ἐθέλοις ποιῆσαι τὸ φάρμακον, ἐμβάλλειν πλέον ἢ κατὰ τὸ ἥμισυ, καθάπερ εἰ καὶ δριμύτερον, ἔλαττον ἢ τὸ ἥμισυ.
beads.english: But if you should wish to make the drug softer, put in more than the half, just as, if you wish it sharper, less than the half.

beads.greek: καὶ μέντοι καὶ τηκομένῳ τῷ κηρῷ μετὰ τοῦ ἐλαίου τῶν εἰρημένων ῥητινῶν τινος ἐπιβάλλειν ἔξεστιν, εἰδότος σου δριμύτερον μὲν αὐτὸ γενέσθαι τῆς στροβιλίνης ἐμβληθείσης, μαλακώτερον δὲ τῆς τερμινθίνης, μέσον δ’ ἀμφοῖν τῆς ἐλατίνης.
beads.english: Moreover, it is also possible to add some one of the aforementioned resins to the wax while it is being melted with the oil, you being aware that the drug becomes sharper when strobilos (pine-cone) resin is put in, softer when terebinth is, and intermediate between the two when fir resin is.

beads.greek: ἐκ δὲ τοῦ γένους τῶν ῥητινῶν ἐστι καὶ ἡ λάριξ ὀνομαζομένη τοὐπίπαν μὲν ὑγροτέρα τῶν προειρημένων οὖσα, παραπλησία δὲ κατὰ τὴν σύστασιν τῇ ὑγρᾷ πευκίνῃ, ἣν ἀντὶ τῆς τερμινθίνης πιπράσκουσεν οἱ ῥωποπῶλαι τοῖς οὐκ εἰδόσι δίακρίνειν αὐτάς.
beads.english: Of the class of resins is also the so-called larix, which is on the whole moister than those previously mentioned, and similar in consistency to the liquid pine resin, which the dealers in sundries sell in place of terebinth to those who do not know how to distinguish them.

beads.greek: ἔστι δ’ ἡ τοιαύτη ῥητίνη καὶ τῇ ὀσμῇ καὶ τῇ γεύσει καὶ τῇ δυνάμει δριμυτέρα τῆς τερμινθίνης.
beads.english: Such a resin is sharper than terebinth in smell, in taste and in power.

beads.greek: ταύτῃ τε οὖν τῇ ῥητίνῃ καὶ τῇ τερμινθίνῃ παραπλησίαν ἔχει δύναμιν ἡ λάριξ ὀνομαζομένη, λεπτομερεστέρα δ’ αὐτῶν ἐστι καὶ διαφορητικωτέρα.
beads.english: The so-called larix, then, has a power similar to this resin and to terebinth, but it is finer in parts than they and more discutient.

greek_sentences: ἅπασι δὲ τοῖς εἰρημένοις φαρμάκοις, ὅταν ἐν τῇ θυείᾳ τὰ μεταλλικὰ πλείοσιν ἡμέραις τριφθῇ μετ’ ὄξους, ἐπεμβαλλέσθω λιβανωτὸς ὁ λευκότατός τε καὶ λιπαρὸς, ﻿ [617] εἶτα πάλιν ἅμα τοῖς μεταλλικοῖς λειούσθω τινὰς ἡμέρας, πρὶν τὴν κηρωτὴν αὐτοῖς ἐπιμίγνυσθαι.

english_sentences: To all the drugs mentioned, when the metallic substances have been triturated in the mortar for several days with vinegar, let frankincense—the whitest and oily kind—be added in, [617] and then let it again be ground fine together with the metallic substances for some days, before the cerate is mixed in with them.

But if you should wish to make the drug softer, put in more than the half, just as, if you wish it sharper, less than the half.

Such a resin is sharper than terebinth in smell, in taste and in power.
The so-called larix, then, has a power similar to this resin and to terebinth, but it is finer in parts than they and more discutient.

beads.greek: μίξεις οὖν τῷ κηρῷ τῶν εἰρημένων ῥητινῶν [618] βουλόμενος ἐμπλαστρῶδες γενέσθαι τὸ φάρμακον ἕκτον μέρος, ὡς ἐὰν τοῦ κηροῦ βάλῃς λίτραν α΄.
beads.english: You will therefore mix with the wax, if you wish the drug to become plaster-like, a sixth part of the resins [618] mentioned, so that if you put in one pound of wax, you will put in two ounces of the resin; but if it should be very liquid, it will suffice to mix in even one alone.

beads.greek: τῆς ῥητίνης ἐμβαλεῖς γο β΄. εἰ δ’ εἴη λίαν ὑγρὰ, καὶ μίαν ἀρκέσει μόνην μῖξαι.
beads.english: If, however, you are not concerned that the drug become plaster-like, there will be no great need to mix the resin into it.

beads.greek: μὴ φροντίζων μέντοι τοῦ γενέσθαι τό φάρμακον ἐμπλαστρῶδες, οὐ πάνυ τι δεήσει τὴν ῥητίνην μιγνύναι αὐτῷ. καὶ χαλβάνης δὲ μίγνυε πάντως, ἔνθα μέντοι πρόκειται πρᾳότατον ἐργάσασθαι τὸ φάρμακον, ἴσον τῷ κατὰ τὸν λιβανωτὸν σταθμῷ.
beads.english: And mix in galbanum too, by all means: where, however, it is proposed to make the drug as mild as possible, in an amount equal to the weight of the frankincense; where stronger, half of it; and for the mean between both, the amount intermediate between the equal and the half, as for instance, if the drachms of frankincense were four, you will put in two of galbanum if you wish the drug to remain strong, four if mild, and three for the middle.

beads.greek: ἔνθα δ’ ἰσχυρότερον, τὸ ἥμισυ. κατὰ δὲ τὸ μέσον ἀμφοῖν, τὸ μεταξὺ τοῦ τ’ ἴσου καὶ τοῦ ἡμίσεως, οἷον εἰ τέτταρες εἶεν αἱ τοῦ λιβανωτοῦ δραχμαὶ, δύο μὲν ἐμβαλεῖς τῆς χαλβάνης ἰσχυρὸν διαμεῖναι τὸ φάρμακον βουλόμενος, πρᾷον δὲ τέσσαρας, τρεῖς δὲ μέσον.
beads.english: For just as it has something soft and pain-relieving, so too it has something septic.

beads.greek: ὥσπερ γὰρ ἔχει τι μαλακὸν καὶ ἀνώδυνον, οὕτω καὶ σηπτικόν.
beads.english: And this belongs also to most of the emollients.

beads.greek: τοῦτο δὲ ὑπάρχει καὶ τοῖς πλείστοις τῶν μαλακτικῶν. διὸ καὶ γεγυμνωμένῳ τῷ νεύρῳ προσφέροντός σου τὸ φάρμακον οὐ πάνυ τι μεμίχθαι χρὴ τὴν χαλβάνην, ἄνευ δὲ γυμνώσεως οὐ σμικρῶς ἡ μίξις αὐτῆς, εἰς ἀνωδυνίαν συντελοῦσα.
beads.english: Therefore, when you are applying the drug to a nerve that has been laid bare, the galbanum should not be mixed in to any great extent; but without denudation its admixture is of no small account, contributing to freedom from pain.

τοῦτο δὲ ὑπάρχει καὶ τοῖς πλείστοις τῶν μαλακτικῶν.

beads.greek: καὶ τοίνυν ἔνεστοί σοι καὶ τοιοῦτον φάρμακον ἔχειν ἕτοιμον ἐπὶ τῶν εὐαισθήτων τε καὶ ἁπαλοσάρκων καὶ κακοχύμων, ἐν ᾧ πλέον [619] ἐστὶ τῆς χαλβάνης.
beads.english: And so it is possible for you to have ready also a drug of this sort, for use on bodies that are highly sensitive, soft-fleshed and full of bad humours, in which there is more [619] galbanum.

beads.greek: ἅπαντα γὰρ τὰ μεταλλικὰ τραχυντικά τ’ ἐστὶ καὶ ὀδυνηρά. καὶ τῶν ὑγρῶν ὄξος.
beads.english: For all the metallic substances are roughening and painful, and, among liquids, vinegar.

beads.greek: εἰκότως οὖν τὰ δι’ αὐτῶν σκευαζόμενα φάρμακα τραχέα τε φαίνεται καὶ ὀδυνηρά. καὶ διὰ τοῦτο αὐτοῖς ἐπιτήδειός ἐστιν ἥ τε δι’ ἐλαίου κατάντλησις ἥ τε μίξις τῆς χαλβάνης ὁμοίως.
beads.english: It is reasonable, then, that the drugs prepared from them appear rough and painful; and for this reason affusion with oil is suited to them, and likewise the admixture of galbanum.

beads.greek: ἔστι δ’ οὐδὲν ἧττον χαλβάνης ἀνώδυνον τὸ λεπτομερὲς στέαρ.
beads.english: Fine-particled fat, moreover, is no less pain-relieving than galbanum.

beads.greek: ἔχειν οὖν ἀξιῶ σέ τι καὶ διὰ τούτων ἐσκευασμένον ἕτερον φάρμακον, ὃ μιγνύναι δυνήσῃ τῷ διὰ τῶν μεταλλικῶν, ἐπί τε τῶν εἰρημένων σωμάτων, ὅσα τε ἄλλα τραχέος τε καὶ ὀδυνηροῦ τοῦ φαρμάκου λάβῃ ποτὲ αἴσθησιν.

beads.greek: ἐκλέγεσθαι δὲ καὶ τούτων ὅσα λεπτομερέστερα, τοιαῦτα δ’ ἐστὶ τά τε τῶν ἀγρίων ζώων καὶ μάλιστα λέοντός τε καὶ παρδάλεως καὶ ὑαίνης καὶ ἄρκτου, τά τε τῶν πτηνῶν καὶ μάλιστα τῶν χηνῶν.
beads.english: Of these fats too one should select those that are finer in parts; such are those of wild animals, and especially of the lion, the leopard, the hyena and the bear, and those of birds, and especially of geese.

beads.greek: εἰ δὲ μὴ παρείη τοῦτο, τῶν ἀγροίκων ἀλεκτρυόνων τε καὶ ἀλεκτορίδων.
beads.english: If this is not at hand, that of country cocks and hens.

beads.greek: οὕτω δὲ καὶ τὸ τῶν ἀγροίκων χηνῶν στέαρ προαιρεῖσθαι. τῶν γὰρ ἐν ταῖς πόλεσι τρεφομένων ζώων, ὡς ἂν ἀργῶν κατακεκλεισμένων, ὑγρότερόν τέ ἐστι καὶ παχυμερέστερον τὸ στέαρ.
beads.english: In the same way one should also prefer the fat of country geese; for the fat of animals reared in cities, inasmuch as they are shut up in idleness, is moister and coarser in parts.

For all the metallic substances are roughening and painful, and, among liquids, vinegar.
It is reasonable, then, that the drugs prepared from them appear rough and painful; and for this reason affusion with oil is suited to them, and likewise the admixture of galbanum.

I think it right, therefore, that you also have another drug, prepared from these as well, which you will be able to mix with the one made from the metallic substances, both in the case of the bodies just mentioned and in whatever other cases there is ever a sensation of the drug being rough and painful.

If this is not at hand, that of country cocks and hens.
In the same way one should also prefer the fat of country geese; for the fat of animals reared in cities, inasmuch as they are shut up in idleness, is moister and coarser in parts.

beads.greek: ὅταν δ’ ἡ σύστασις τοῦ φαρμάκου κηρωτοειδὴς [620] ᾖ, μιγνύσθω κηροῦ τὸ τρίτον ἢ τέταρτον ἢ, εἰ λίαν ὑγρὸν εἶναί σοι φαίνοιτο τὸ στέαρ, ἐγχωρεῖ καὶ τὸ ἥμισυ τοῦ κηροῦ μῖξαι, ὥσπερ γε εἰ καὶ ξηρὸν εἴη, τὸ τέταρτον. εἰ δὲ μέσος ἔχει, τὸ τρίτον.
beads.english: But when the consistency of the drug is to be cerate-like, [620] let a third or a fourth part of wax be mixed in; or, if the fat should seem to you to be exceedingly moist, it is permissible to mix in even half as much wax, just as, if it should be dry, a fourth; and if it is in a middle state, a third.

beads.greek: εἰς πολλὰ δὲ χρήσιμος ἡμῖν ἡ τοιαύτη κηρωτὴ μέλλουσα γενήσεσθαι διὰ στεάτων ὀνομαζέσθω.
beads.english: Since such a cerate is going to be useful to us for many purposes, let it be named the cerate of fats.

beads.greek: [Περὶ τοῦ δι’ εὐφορβίου συντιθεμένου φαρμάκου.] Λέλεκταί μοι καὶ πρόσθεν ὡς ἀπολείπεται πάμπολυ τοῦ νέου τὸ παλαιὸν εὐφόρβιον.
beads.english: [On the drug compounded with euphorbium.] It has been stated by me also earlier that old euphorbium falls very far short of the new.

beads.greek: ἂν μὲν οὖν αὐτοετὲς ᾖ, καὶ τοῦ Κυρηναίου μᾶλλον ὀποῦ θερμαίνει καὶ μάλιστα τοῦ νῦν, ἐξ ὅτου δι’ ὕδατος ἀρδεύσεως αὐξάνουσί τε τὰ φυτὰ καὶ πρὸς πλῆθος ὀποῦ γενέσεως παρασκευάζουσι μετ’ ἐνιαυτὸν γὰρ ἕνα θερμὸν ἱκανῶς ἐστι, λείπεται δὲ ἤδη συχνῷ τοῦ προσφάτου.
beads.english: If, then, it is of the same year, it heats even more than the Cyrenaic juice, and especially more than that of the present day, ever since they have been making the plants grow by watering with water and preparing them for an abundant production of juice; for after one year it is sufficiently hot, but already falls considerably short of the fresh.

beads.greek: δυοῖν δὲ ἐτῶν γενόμενον, ἔτι δὴ καὶ πλέον ἀπολείπεται τοῦ νέου, καθάπερ γε τριῶν ἢ τεττάρων ἔτι μᾶλλον.
beads.english: When it has become two years old, it falls still further short of the new, just as at three or four it falls short still more.

beads.greek: εἰ δέ τι τούτων χρονιώτερον εἴη, παντάπασιν ἡ δύναμις αὐτοῦ καταλύεται.
beads.english: And if it should be of longer standing than these, its power is entirely dissolved.

beads.greek: γνωριεῖς δ’, ὡς ἔφην, ὅπως ἔχει χρόνου καὶ δυνάμεως, εἴς τε τὴν χρόαν ἀφορῶν αὐτοῦ καὶ τὴν σύστασιν.
beads.english: You will recognise, as I said, how it stands with respect to age and power by looking at its colour and its consistency.

εἰ δὲ μέσος ἔχει, τὸ τρίτον.
εἰς πολλὰ δὲ χρήσιμος ἡμῖν ἡ τοιαύτη κηρωτὴ μέλλουσα γενήσεσθαι διὰ στεάτων ὀνομαζέσθω.
[Περὶ τοῦ δι’ εὐφορβίου συντιθεμένου φαρμάκου.] Λέλεκταί μοι καὶ πρόσθεν ὡς ἀπολείπεται πάμπολυ τοῦ νέου τὸ παλαιὸν εὐφόρβιον.

ἂν μὲν οὖν αὐτοετὲς ᾖ, καὶ τοῦ Κυρηναίου μᾶλλον ὀποῦ θερμαίνει καὶ μάλιστα τοῦ νῦν, ἐξ ὅτου δι’ ὕδατος ἀρδεύσεως αὐξάνουσί τε τὰ φυτὰ καὶ πρὸς πλῆθος ὀποῦ γενέσεως παρασκευάζουσι μετ’ ἐνιαυτὸν γὰρ ἕνα θερμὸν ἱκανῶς ἐστι, λείπεται δὲ ἤδη συχνῷ τοῦ προσφάτου.
δυοῖν δὲ ἐτῶν γενόμενον, ἔτι δὴ καὶ πλέον ἀπολείπεται τοῦ νέου, καθάπερ γε τριῶν ἢ τεττάρων ἔτι μᾶλλον.
εἰ δέ τι τούτων χρονιώτερον εἴη, παντάπασιν ἡ δύναμις αὐτοῦ καταλύεται.
γνωριεῖς δ’, ὡς ἔφην, ὅπως ἔχει χρόνου καὶ δυνάμεως, εἴς τε τὴν χρόαν ἀφορῶν αὐτοῦ καὶ τὴν σύστασιν.
english_sentences: But when the consistency of the drug is to be cerate-like, [620] let a third or a fourth part of wax be mixed in; or, if the fat should seem to you to be exceedingly moist, it is permissible to mix in even half as much wax, just as, if it should be dry, a fourth; and if it is in a middle state, a third.
Since such a cerate is going to be useful to us for many purposes, let it be named the cerate of fats.
[On the drug compounded with euphorbium.] It has been stated by me also earlier that old euphorbium falls very far short of the new.

If, then, it is of the same year, it heats even more than the Cyrenaic juice, and especially more than that of the present day, ever since they have been making the plants grow by watering with water and preparing them for an abundant production of juice; for after one year it is sufficiently hot, but already falls considerably short of the fresh.
When it has become two years old, it falls still further short of the new, just as at three or four it falls short still more.
And if it should be of longer standing than these, its power is entirely dissolved.
You will recognise, as I said, how it stands with respect to age and power by looking at its colour and its consistency.

beads.greek: τῇ μὲν γὰρ χρόᾳ ξανθότερον καὶ ὠχρότερον [621] φαίνεται τοῦ νέου τὸ παλαιὸν, τῇ συστάσει δὲ σκληρόν τε καὶ ξηρότερον.
beads.english: For in colour the old appears yellower and paler [621] than the new, and in consistency hard and drier.

beads.greek: εἰ μέντοι γευόμενος ἐθέλοις διακρίνειν, οὐ στοχαστικὴν, ἀλλὰ βεβαίαν ἕξεις τὴν διάγνωσιν· αὐτοῦ.
beads.english: If, however, you should wish to distinguish it by tasting, you will have a diagnosis of it that is not conjectural but certain.

beads.greek: ὃ δὲ ἔφην αὐτοσχεδιάσαι δι’ αὐτοῦ χρίσμα θερμαντικὸν, ἀκριβέστατά σοι δηλώσει τὴν δύναμιν τοῦ φαρμάκου.
beads.english: And the heating unguent which I said one should improvise from it will show you most precisely the power of the drug.

beads.greek: σύγκειται δὲ κατὰ τήνδε τὴν συμμετρίαν. ἓν μέν ἐστι μέρος τοῦ εὐφορβίου, τρία δὲ τοῦ κηροῦ, τοῦ δὲ ἐλαίου ιβ΄.
beads.english: It is composed according to the following proportion: one part is of euphorbium, three of wax, and of oil twelve.

beads.greek: τριπλάσιον μὲν εἶναι χρὴ τοῦ εὐφορβίου τὸν κηρόν. αὐτοῦ δὲ πάλιν τοῦ κηροῦ τετραπλάσιον τὸ ἔλαιον.
beads.english: The wax must be three times the euphorbium, and the oil in turn four times the wax itself.

beads.greek: ὅταν οὖν οὕτω συνθῇς τὸ φάρμακον, ἀνατρίψας τι μέρος αὐτῷ δυνήσῃ γνῶναι σαφῶς ὁπόσην δύναμιν ἔχει. μάλιστα δὲ ἐν τῷ βαλανείῳ καταφανὲς γίγνεται.
beads.english: When, then, you have compounded the drug in this way, by rubbing some part with it you will be able to know clearly how great a power it has.

beads.greek: δάκνονται γὰρ καὶ ὑπὸ τοῦ ἀέρος μὲν, ἀλλ’ ἔτι καὶ μᾶλλον ὑπὸ τοῦ ὕδατος ἰσχυρῶς, ὅταν ᾖ θερμὸν καὶ νέον καὶ ἰσχυρὸν τὸ εὐφόρβιον.
beads.english: And it becomes most evident in the bath; for people are stung strongly, by the air indeed, but still more by the water, when the euphorbium is hot and new and strong.

beads.greek: ἐὰν μὲν οὖν ἔχῃς τοιοῦτον καὶ αὐτὸ τοῦτο τὸ εἰρημένον χρῖσμα, θαῤῥῶν ἐπιτίθει τοῖς νύγμασιν, ἐφ’ ὧν εὐλαβῇ μύσαι τὸ στόμιον.
beads.english: If, then, you have euphorbium of this kind and this very unguent that has been described, apply it confidently to punctures in which you are wary that the mouth may close.

greek_sentences: τῇ μὲν γὰρ χρόᾳ ξανθότερον καὶ ὠχρότερον [621] φαίνεται τοῦ νέου τὸ παλαιὸν, τῇ συστάσει δὲ σκληρόν τε καὶ ξηρότερον.
εἰ μέντοι γευόμενος ἐθέλοις διακρίνειν, οὐ στοχαστικὴν, ἀλλὰ βεβαίαν ἕξεις τὴν διάγνωσιν· αὐτοῦ.
ὃ δὲ ἔφην αὐτοσχεδιάσαι δι’ αὐτοῦ χρίσμα θερμαντικὸν, ἀκριβέστατά σοι δηλώσει τὴν δύναμιν τοῦ φαρμάκου.
σύγκειται δὲ κατὰ τήνδε τὴν συμμετρίαν.
ἓν μέν ἐστι μέρος τοῦ εὐφορβίου, τρία δὲ τοῦ κηροῦ, τοῦ δὲ ἐλαίου ιβ΄.
τριπλάσιον μὲν εἶναι χρὴ τοῦ εὐφορβίου τὸν κηρόν.
αὐτοῦ δὲ πάλιν τοῦ κηροῦ τετραπλάσιον τὸ ἔλαιον.
ὅταν οὖν οὕτω συνθῇς τὸ φάρμακον, ἀνατρίψας τι μέρος αὐτῷ δυνήσῃ γνῶναι σαφῶς ὁπόσην δύναμιν ἔχει.
μάλιστα δὲ ἐν τῷ βαλανείῳ καταφανὲς γίγνεται.
δάκνονται γὰρ καὶ ὑπὸ τοῦ ἀέρος μὲν, ἀλλ’ ἔτι καὶ μᾶλλον ὑπὸ τοῦ ὕδατος ἰσχυρῶς, ὅταν ᾖ θερμὸν καὶ νέον καὶ ἰσχυρὸν τὸ εὐφόρβιον.
ἐὰν μὲν οὖν ἔχῃς τοιοῦτον καὶ αὐτὸ τοῦτο τὸ εἰρημένον χρῖσμα, θαῤῥῶν ἐπιτίθει τοῖς νύγμασιν, ἐφ’ ὧν εὐλαβῇ μύσαι τὸ στόμιον.
english_sentences: For in colour the old appears yellower and paler [621] than the new, and in consistency hard and drier.
If, however, you should wish to distinguish it by tasting, you will have a diagnosis of it that is not conjectural but certain.
And the heating unguent which I said one should improvise from it will show you most precisely the power of the drug.
It is composed according to the following proportion: one part is of euphorbium, three of wax, and of oil twelve.
The wax must be three times the euphorbium, and the oil in turn four times the wax itself.
When, then, you have compounded the drug in this way, by rubbing some part with it you will be able to know clearly how great a power it has.
And it becomes most evident in the bath; for people are stung strongly, by the air indeed, but still more by the water, when the euphorbium is hot and new and strong.
If, then, you have euphorbium of this kind and this very unguent that has been described, apply it confidently to punctures in which you are wary that the mouth may close.

beads.greek: ἐὰν δὲ ἀσθενέστερον ᾖ, προστίθει τῷ σταθμῷ τοῦ εὐφορβίου κατὰ τὴν ἀναλογίαν τῆς ἀσθενείας, ἐνίοτε μὲν ἓν ἥμισυ μέρος ﻿ [622] ἐμβάλλων, ἔστι δ’ ὅτε δύο, καὶ ποτὲ ἴσον τῷ κηρῷ καὶ πλεῖον, ἐὰν λίαν ᾖ παλαιόν.
beads.english: But if it is weaker, add to the weight of the euphorbium in proportion to its weakness, sometimes putting in one and a half parts, [622] sometimes two, and at times an amount equal to the wax, and even more, if it is very old.

beads.greek: ἥ γε μὴν πρώτη χρῆσις ἐπὶ τοῦ νενυγμένου τὸ νεῦρον ἢ τὸν τένοντα ποδηγήσει σε πρὸς τὴν δευτέραν.
beads.english: The first application, at any rate, upon one who has been punctured in the nerve or the tendon will guide you toward the second.

beads.greek: ἐὰν μὲν γὰρ αὐτός τε ὁ τετρωμένος φησὶ δεδῆχθαι, σοί τ’ αὐτῷ φαίνηται τὰ περὶ τὸ νύγμα θερμὰ καὶ αὐτὸ τὸ νύγμα πλέον ἢ δεῖ ἐπῃρμένον, ὑποφλεγμαῖνόν τε τοῖς χείλεσιν, ἤτοι γε ἐκλύσεις τοῦ φαρμάκου τὴν δύναμιν ἐλαίου μίξει πλέονος ἢ συνθεὶς ἄλλο κατὰ προτέραν συμμετρίαν ἢ δι’ εὐφορβίου παλαιοτέρου σύμμετρον οὕτως ἐργάσῃ.
beads.english: For if the wounded man himself says that he feels a biting, and to you yourself the parts around the puncture appear hot and the puncture itself raised more than it should be and somewhat inflamed at its lips, then either you will relax the power of the drug by the admixture of more oil, or, compounding another according to the former proportion or by means of older euphorbium, you will in this way make it well-proportioned.

beads.greek: ἐὰν δὲ τὰ ἐναντία τῶν εἰρημένων παρῇ, παραυξήσεις τοῦ φαρμάκου τὴν δύναμιν.
beads.english: But if the opposites of what has been said are present, you will increase the power of the drug.

beads.greek: ἐὰν δὲ συμμέτρως ἔχειν ἅπαντα φαίνηται, φυλάξεις.
beads.english: And if everything appears to be in due measure, you will keep it as it is.

beads.greek: ἡ μὲν οὖν τριπλάσιον ἔχουσα τὸν κηρὸν τοῦ εὐφορβίου σύνθεσις ἰσχυροτάτη τῶν ἄλλων ἐστὶν, ὅταν γε, ὡς εἴρηται, νέον ᾖ τὸ εὐφόρβιον· ἡ δὲ πενταπλάσιον ἀσθενεστάτη, μέση δ’ ἀμφοῖν ἡ τετραπλάσιον ἔχουσα τὸν κηρὸν τοῦ εὐφορβίου.
beads.english: The composition, then, which has the wax triple the euphorbium is the strongest of all, provided that, as has been said, the euphorbium is fresh; that which has it fivefold is the weakest, and intermediate between both is the one which has the wax fourfold the euphorbium.

greek_sentences: ἐὰν δὲ ἀσθενέστερον ᾖ, προστίθει τῷ σταθμῷ τοῦ εὐφορβίου κατὰ τὴν ἀναλογίαν τῆς ἀσθενείας, ἐνίοτε μὲν ἓν ἥμισυ μέρος ﻿ [622] ἐμβάλλων, ἔστι δ’ ὅτε δύο, καὶ ποτὲ ἴσον τῷ κηρῷ καὶ πλεῖον, ἐὰν λίαν ᾖ παλαιόν.
ἥ γε μὴν πρώτη χρῆσις ἐπὶ τοῦ νενυγμένου τὸ νεῦρον ἢ τὸν τένοντα ποδηγήσει σε πρὸς τὴν δευτέραν.

ἐὰν μὲν γὰρ αὐτός τε ὁ τετρωμένος φησὶ δεδῆχθαι, σοί τ’ αὐτῷ φαίνηται τὰ περὶ τὸ νύγμα θερμὰ καὶ αὐτὸ τὸ νύγμα πλέον ἢ δεῖ ἐπῃρμένον, ὑποφλεγμαῖνόν τε τοῖς χείλεσιν, ἤτοι γε ἐκλύσεις τοῦ φαρμάκου τὴν δύναμιν ἐλαίου μίξει πλέονος ἢ συνθεὶς ἄλλο κατὰ προτέραν συμμετρίαν ἢ δι’ εὐφορβίου παλαιοτέρου σύμμετρον οὕτως ἐργάσῃ.
ἐὰν δὲ τὰ ἐναντία τῶν εἰρημένων παρῇ, παραυξήσεις τοῦ φαρμάκου τὴν δύναμιν.
ἐὰν δὲ συμμέτρως ἔχειν ἅπαντα φαίνηται, φυλάξεις.

ἡ μὲν οὖν τριπλάσιον ἔχουσα τὸν κηρὸν τοῦ εὐφορβίου σύνθεσις ἰσχυροτάτη τῶν ἄλλων ἐστὶν, ὅταν γε, ὡς εἴρηται, νέον ᾖ τὸ εὐφόρβιον· ἡ δὲ πενταπλάσιον ἀσθενεστάτη, μέση δ’ ἀμφοῖν ἡ τετραπλάσιον ἔχουσα τὸν κηρὸν τοῦ εὐφορβίου.
english_sentences: But if it is weaker, add to the weight of the euphorbium in proportion to its weakness, sometimes putting in one and a half parts, [622] sometimes two, and at times an amount equal to the wax, and even more, if it is very old.
The first application, at any rate, upon one who has been punctured in the nerve or the tendon will guide you toward the second.

For if the wounded man himself says that he feels a biting, and to you yourself the parts around the puncture appear hot and the puncture itself raised more than it should be and somewhat inflamed at its lips, then either you will relax the power of the drug by the admixture of more oil, or, compounding another according to the former proportion or by means of older euphorbium, you will in this way make it well-proportioned.
But if the opposites of what has been said are present, you will increase the power of the drug.
And if everything appears to be in due measure, you will keep it as it is.

The composition, then, which has the wax triple the euphorbium is the strongest of all, provided that, as has been said, the euphorbium is fresh; that which has it fivefold is the weakest, and intermediate between both is the one which has the wax fourfold the euphorbium.

beads.greek: τὸ δὲ ἔλαιον εἰ μὲν οἷα τὰ καλούμενα πρὸς τῶν ἰατρῶν ἄκοπα χρίσματα βούλοιο ποιῆσαι, τετραπλάσιον ἐμβαλεῖς τοῦ κηροῦ· εἰ δ’ οἵαν ἐπὶ τῶν καταγμάτων [623] τὴν ὑγρὰν κηρωτὴν ἐργαζόμεθα διπλάσιον· εἰ δὲ καὶ ξηρὸς καὶ ἀλιπὴς ὁ κηρὸς εἴη, καὶ πλέον τοῦ διπλασίου.
beads.english: As for the oil: if you wish to make such things as the unguents called by physicians akopa, you will put in four times the amount of the wax; but if such as the liquid cerate which we prepare for fractures, [623] double; and if the wax should be both dry and fat-free, even more than double.

beads.greek: τοὐπίπαν δ’ ἀρκέσει προσθεῖναι μέρους ἑνὸς τὸ ἥμισυ τῷ διπλασίῳ, ὡς γενέσθαι τὸ πᾶν μέτρον τοῦ κηροῦ δυοῖν καὶ ἡμίσεων μερῶν.
beads.english: For the most part it will suffice to add half of one part to the double, so that the whole measure in relation to the wax comes to two and a half parts.

beads.greek: ἐμπλαστρῶδες δὲ ποιῆσαι βουληθεὶς τὸ φάρμακον τῷ κηρῷ μίξεις τὸ ἴσον ἔλαιον. ἐὰν δὲ τὸ περιέχον ᾖ σύμμετρον κατὰ θερμότητα, ὅ τε κηρὸς παλαιὸς καὶ αὐχμηρὸς τό τε περιέχον ψυχρὸν, ὀλίγῳ πλέον, ὥσπερ γε καὶ ἐὰν ὅ τε κηρὸς ᾖ λιπαρὸς τό τε περιέχον θερμὸν, ἔλαττον ὀλίγῳ.
beads.english: But if you wish to make the drug plaster-like, you will mix with the wax an equal amount of oil, provided the surrounding air is moderate in respect of heat; but if the wax is old and parched and the surrounding air cold, a little more, just as also, if the wax is fatty and the surrounding air hot, a little less.

beads.greek: τὸ δ’ ὀλίγον τοῦτο δωδέκατόν ἐστι μέρος ἐφ’ ἑκάτερα τοῦ μέσου.
beads.english: And this "little" is a twelfth part on either side of the mean.

beads.greek: καὶ γὰρ καὶ ἕνδεκα καὶ δεκατρεῖς ἐλαίου οὐγγίας ποτὲ ἔμιξα τῇ λίτρᾳ τοῦ κηροῦ κατὰ τὸ ποσὸν τῆς τε συστάσεως αὐτοῦ καὶ τῆς τοῦ περιέχοντος θερμότητός τε καὶ ψύξεως.
beads.english: For indeed I have at times mixed both eleven and thirteen ounces of oil with the pound of wax, according to the degree both of its consistency and of the heat and cold of the surrounding air.

greek_sentences: τὸ δὲ ἔλαιον εἰ μὲν οἷα τὰ καλούμενα πρὸς τῶν ἰατρῶν ἄκοπα χρίσματα βούλοιο ποιῆσαι, τετραπλάσιον ἐμβαλεῖς τοῦ κηροῦ· εἰ δ’ οἵαν ἐπὶ τῶν καταγμάτων [623] τὴν ὑγρὰν κηρωτὴν ἐργαζόμεθα διπλάσιον· εἰ δὲ καὶ ξηρὸς καὶ ἀλιπὴς ὁ κηρὸς εἴη, καὶ πλέον τοῦ διπλασίου.
τοὐπίπαν δ’ ἀρκέσει προσθεῖναι μέρους ἑνὸς τὸ ἥμισυ τῷ διπλασίῳ, ὡς γενέσθαι τὸ πᾶν μέτρον τοῦ κηροῦ δυοῖν καὶ ἡμίσεων μερῶν.
ἐμπλαστρῶδες δὲ ποιῆσαι βουληθεὶς τὸ φάρμακον τῷ κηρῷ μίξεις τὸ ἴσον ἔλαιον.
ἐὰν δὲ τὸ περιέχον ᾖ σύμμετρον κατὰ θερμότητα, ὅ τε κηρὸς παλαιὸς καὶ αὐχμηρὸς τό τε περιέχον ψυχρὸν, ὀλίγῳ πλέον, ὥσπερ γε καὶ ἐὰν ὅ τε κηρὸς ᾖ λιπαρὸς τό τε περιέχον θερμὸν, ἔλαττον ὀλίγῳ.
τὸ δ’ ὀλίγον τοῦτο δωδέκατόν ἐστι μέρος ἐφ’ ἑκάτερα τοῦ μέσου.
καὶ γὰρ καὶ ἕνδεκα καὶ δεκατρεῖς ἐλαίου οὐγγίας ποτὲ ἔμιξα τῇ λίτρᾳ τοῦ κηροῦ κατὰ τὸ ποσὸν τῆς τε συστάσεως αὐτοῦ καὶ τῆς τοῦ περιέχοντος θερμότητός τε καὶ ψύξεως.
english_sentences: As for the oil: if you wish to make such things as the unguents called by physicians akopa, you will put in four times the amount of the wax; but if such as the liquid cerate which we prepare for fractures, [623] double; and if the wax should be both dry and fat-free, even more than double.
For the most part it will suffice to add half of one part to the double, so that the whole measure in relation to the wax comes to two and a half parts.

But if you wish to make the drug plaster-like, you will mix with the wax an equal amount of oil, provided the surrounding air is moderate in respect of heat; but if the wax is old and parched and the surrounding air cold, a little more, just as also, if the wax is fatty and the surrounding air hot, a little less.
And this "little" is a twelfth part on either side of the mean.
For indeed I have at times mixed both eleven and thirteen ounces of oil with the pound of wax, according to the degree both of its consistency and of the heat and cold of the surrounding air.

beads.greek: σπανίως δὲ βραχεῖ πλέον ἢ ἔλαττον· ἵνα δ’ ἐπίδεσιν ἔχῃ καὶ λιπαρότητα καὶ γλισχρότητα καὶ μὴ ψαθυρὸν ᾖ, μηδ’ εὐδιάλυτον μηδ’ εὐαπόπτωτον τοῦ χρωτὸς τὸ σκευασθὲν, ἐπέμιξα ῥητίνης αὐτῷ, μάλιστα μὲν εἰ παρείη τερμινθίνης ἀληθοῦς, εἰ δὲ μὴ, τῆς γε εὐποριστοτάτης, ἣν ὀνομάζουσι [624] φρυκτήν τε καὶ κολοφωνίαν.
beads.english: And rarely a little more or less. But in order that the preparation may have binding quality (ἐπίδεσιν) and fattiness and viscosity, and not be crumbly, nor easily dissolved, nor easily falling off the skin, I mixed into it some resin, preferably, if it were available, genuine terebinth, and if not, at least the most readily procurable kind, which they call [624] 'roasted' (phrykte) and colophony.

beads.greek: ἔστω δ’ ἴσος αὐτῆς ὁ σταθμὸς τῷ κηρῷ.
beads.english: Let its weight be equal to the wax.

beads.greek: φυλάττει γὰρ οἷς ἄν ἐμβληθῇ φαρμάκοις τὴν προϋπάρχουσαν σύστασιν, ὅταν γε καὶ αὕτη συμμέτρως ἔχῃ.
beads.english: For it preserves the pre-existing consistency of whatever drugs it is put into, provided that it too is in a well-proportioned condition.

beads.greek: πρόδηλον γὰρ ὅτι καθάπερ ἐν ἅπασι τοῖς ἄλλοις, οὕτω κᾀν τῇ ῥητίνῃ τὸ μᾶλλον καὶ ἧττόν ἐστιν.
beads.english: For it is evident that, just as in all other things, so too in resin there is the more and the less.

beads.greek: ἐὰν οὖν ποτὲ φαίνηται λιπαρωτέρα τε καὶ ὑγροτέρα, γινώσκειν χρὴ τὴν ἐκ τοῦ κηροῦ τετηκότος ἐλαίῳ γενησομένην κηρωτὴν ἑαυτῆς ὑγροτέραν ἐσομένην.
beads.english: If, then, it ever appears fattier and moister, one must recognise that the cerate which will result from the wax melted in oil will be moister than itself [would otherwise be].

beads.greek: ὅλως δ’ ἐπὶ νευροτρώτων, ὅταν ἁμαρτάνηταί ποτε τῆς ἀκριβοῦς τε καὶ μέσης συστάσεως τῶν ἐμπλαστρωδῶν φαρμάκων, ἐπὶ τὸ μαλακώτερον ἄμεινον ῥέπειν, εἰ καὶ μολῦνον ἔσεσθαι μέλλοι τὸ σκευασθέν.
beads.english: In general, in those wounded in the nerves, whenever one ever misses the exact and middle consistency of the plaster-like drugs, it is better to incline towards the softer, even if the preparation is going to be smearing (μολῦνον).

beads.greek: ὡσαύτως δὲ καὶ ἡ σύμμετρος τῇ συστάσει.
beads.english: And likewise also that which is well-proportioned in consistency.

beads.greek: πίττα δὲ φυλάττει τὴν τῆς κηρωτῆς σύστασιν.
beads.english: And pitch preserves the consistency of the cerate.

beads.greek: ἀρίστη δ’, ὡς ἔφην, εἰς τὴν τοιαύτην μίξιν ἡ λιπαρὰ, καθάπερ γε καὶ ἡ ῥητίνη.
beads.english: The best for such a mixture, as I said, is the fatty kind, just as indeed is also the [fatty] resin.

beads.greek: ἐὰν δ’ ὑγρὰν ἐμβάλλῃς ῥητίνην, ὁποία κατὰ τὴν σύστασίν ἐστιν ἡ τερμινθίνη, τρίτον αὐτῆς μέρος εἶναι τοῦ κηροῦ προσήκει, καὶ αὐτῆς δὲ τῆς τερμινθίνης ἡ νέα πολὺ τῆς παλαιᾶς ἐστιν ὑγροτέρα.
beads.english: But if you put in a liquid resin, such as terebinth is in its consistency, it is fitting that it be a third part of the wax; and of terebinth itself the fresh is much moister than the old.

greek_sentences: σπανίως δὲ βραχεῖ πλέον ἢ ἔλαττον· ἵνα δ’ ἐπίδεσιν ἔχῃ καὶ λιπαρότητα καὶ γλισχρότητα καὶ μὴ ψαθυρὸν ᾖ, μηδ’ εὐδιάλυτον μηδ’ εὐαπόπτωτον τοῦ χρωτὸς τὸ σκευασθὲν, ἐπέμιξα ῥητίνης αὐτῷ, μάλιστα μὲν εἰ παρείη τερμινθίνης ἀληθοῦς, εἰ δὲ μὴ, τῆς γε εὐποριστοτάτης, ἣν ὀνομάζουσι [624] φρυκτήν τε καὶ κολοφωνίαν.
ἔστω δ’ ἴσος αὐτῆς ὁ σταθμὸς τῷ κηρῷ.
φυλάττει γὰρ οἷς ἄν ἐμβληθῇ φαρμάκοις τὴν προϋπάρχουσαν σύστασιν, ὅταν γε καὶ αὕτη συμμέτρως ἔχῃ.
πρόδηλον γὰρ ὅτι καθάπερ ἐν ἅπασι τοῖς ἄλλοις, οὕτω κᾀν τῇ ῥητίνῃ τὸ μᾶλλον καὶ ἧττόν ἐστιν.
ἐὰν οὖν ποτὲ φαίνηται λιπαρωτέρα τε καὶ ὑγροτέρα, γινώσκειν χρὴ τὴν ἐκ τοῦ κηροῦ τετηκότος ἐλαίῳ γενησομένην κηρωτὴν ἑαυτῆς ὑγροτέραν ἐσομένην.
ὅλως δ’ ἐπὶ νευροτρώτων, ὅταν ἁμαρτάνηταί ποτε τῆς ἀκριβοῦς τε καὶ μέσης συστάσεως τῶν ἐμπλαστρωδῶν φαρμάκων, ἐπὶ τὸ μαλακώτερον ἄμεινον ῥέπειν, εἰ καὶ μολῦνον ἔσεσθαι μέλλοι τὸ σκευασθέν.
ὡσαύτως δὲ καὶ ἡ σύμμετρος τῇ συστάσει.
πίττα δὲ φυλάττει τὴν τῆς κηρωτῆς σύστασιν.
ἀρίστη δ’, ὡς ἔφην, εἰς τὴν τοιαύτην μίξιν ἡ λιπαρὰ, καθάπερ γε καὶ ἡ ῥητίνη.
ἐὰν δ’ ὑγρὰν ἐμβάλλῃς ῥητίνην, ὁποία κατὰ τὴν σύστασίν ἐστιν ἡ τερμινθίνη, τρίτον αὐτῆς μέρος εἶναι τοῦ κηροῦ προσήκει, καὶ αὐτῆς δὲ τῆς τερμινθίνης ἡ νέα πολὺ τῆς παλαιᾶς ἐστιν ὑγροτέρα.
english_sentences: And rarely a little more or less.

But in order that the preparation may have binding quality (ἐπίδεσιν) and fattiness and viscosity, and not be crumbly, nor easily dissolved, nor easily falling off the skin, I mixed into it some resin, preferably, if it were available, genuine terebinth, and if not, at least the most readily procurable kind, which they call [624] 'roasted' (phrykte) and colophony.
Let its weight be equal to the wax.
For it preserves the pre-existing consistency of whatever drugs it is put into, provided that it too is in a well-proportioned condition.
For it is evident that, just as in all other things, so too in resin there is the more and the less.
If, then, it ever appears fattier and moister, one must recognise that the cerate which will result from the wax melted in oil will be moister than itself [would otherwise be].

In general, in those wounded in the nerves, whenever one ever misses the exact and middle consistency of the plaster-like drugs, it is better to incline towards the softer, even if the preparation is going to be smearing (μολῦνον).
And likewise also that which is well-proportioned in consistency.
And pitch preserves the consistency of the cerate.
The best for such a mixture, as I said, is the fatty kind, just as indeed is also the [fatty] resin.
But if you put in a liquid resin, such as terebinth is in its consistency, it is fitting that it be a third part of the wax; and of terebinth itself the fresh is much moister than the old.

beads.greek: μέμνησθε τοίνυν ὅπερ ἐπὶ κηροῦ καὶ ῥητίνης ἠκούσατε, [625] τοῦτο ἐπὶ πάντων φυλάττειν. οὐ γὰρ τῶν ξηρῶν καὶ αὐχμηρῶν ἢ διὰ χρόνον ἢ διὰ τὴν ἐξ ἀρχῆς φύσιν, ἀλλὰ τῶν συμμέτρων τῇ συστάσει τοσοῦτον ἑκάστου μικτέον ἐστὶν ἐν τῇ συνθέσει τῶν φαρμάκων, ὅσον ἂν ὑπ’ ἐμοῦ γεγραμμένον εὑρίσκηται.
beads.english: Remember, then, to observe in all cases what you have heard concerning wax and resin, [625] For it is not of things that are dry and parched, whether through time or through their nature from the beginning, but of things of moderate consistency that one must mix, in the composition of the drugs, as much of each as is found written by me.

beads.greek: ἔστω δὴ τὸ συμμέτρως ἔχον δυνάμεώς τε καὶ συστάσεως τοῦ προκειμένου φαρμάκου, κηροῦ μὲν καὶ ῥητίνης φρυκτῆς καὶ ἐλαίου τὸ ἴσον ἔχειν, αὐτοῦ δὲ τοῦ εὐφορβίου τὸ ἕκτον, ὡς εἶναι λίτραν μὲν ἐκείνων ἑκάστου, τοῦ δὲ εὐφορβίου δύο οὐγγίας.
beads.english: Let, then, the form of the drug before us that is moderate in both power and consistency be one that has equal amounts of wax, roasted (phrykte) resin and oil, and a sixth part of euphorbium itself, so that there is a litra of each of those, but two ounces of euphorbium.

beads.greek: εἰ δὲ μαλακώτερον αὐτὸ ποιῆσαι βουληθείημεν, ἀρκεῖ τὸ ὄγδοον μέρος ἐμβάλλειν τοῦ εὐφορβίου, τουτέστιν γο α΄. καὶ ἡμίσειαν, ἐπὶ τοῦ νέου καὶ θερμοτάτου, καθότι προεῖπον εὐφορβίου τῆς συμμετρίας ταύτης ὡρισμένης, ὡς ἐάν γε παλαιότερον ᾖ, καὶ διὰ τοῦτο ἀσθενέστερον, εἴρηται πρόσθεν ὡς πλέον εἶναι προσήκει τοῦτο τῆς τῶν ἄλλων ἀναλογίας.
beads.english: If, however, we should wish to make it softer, it suffices to put in an eighth part of euphorbium, that is, one ounce and a half—this proportion being defined, as I said before, for euphorbium that is fresh and hottest; since if it is older, and on that account weaker, it has been said earlier that this ought to be more than the proportion of the others.

beads.greek: εἰ δὲ μὴ μόνης ῥητίνης, ἀλλὰ καὶ πίττης ἐμβάλλειν ἐθελήσαιμεν, ἡμίλιτρον ἑκατέρας μίξομεν, ὡς εἶναι ἴσον τὸν σταθμὸν τῷ κηρῷ.
beads.english: And if we should wish to put in not resin alone but also pitch, we shall mix in half a litra of each, so that the weight is equal to the wax.

beads.greek: πολὺ δὲ κάλλιόν ἐστι τὸ φάρμακον, ἐὰν ἀντὶ τῆς ῥητίνης τε καὶ πίττης πρόπολιν μίξῃ τις ἴσην τῷ κηρῷ.
beads.english: But the drug is far better if, in place of the resin and pitch, one mixes in propolis equal to the wax.

greek_sentences: μέμνησθε τοίνυν ὅπερ ἐπὶ κηροῦ καὶ ῥητίνης ἠκούσατε, [625] τοῦτο ἐπὶ πάντων φυλάττειν.

οὐ γὰρ τῶν ξηρῶν καὶ αὐχμηρῶν ἢ διὰ χρόνον ἢ διὰ τὴν ἐξ ἀρχῆς φύσιν, ἀλλὰ τῶν συμμέτρων τῇ συστάσει τοσοῦτον ἑκάστου μικτέον ἐστὶν ἐν τῇ συνθέσει τῶν φαρμάκων, ὅσον ἂν ὑπ’ ἐμοῦ γεγραμμένον εὑρίσκηται.

ἔστω δὴ τὸ συμμέτρως ἔχον δυνάμεώς τε καὶ συστάσεως τοῦ προκειμένου φαρμάκου, κηροῦ μὲν καὶ ῥητίνης φρυκτῆς καὶ ἐλαίου τὸ ἴσον ἔχειν, αὐτοῦ δὲ τοῦ εὐφορβίου τὸ ἕκτον, ὡς εἶναι λίτραν μὲν ἐκείνων ἑκάστου, τοῦ δὲ εὐφορβίου δύο οὐγγίας.
εἰ δὲ μαλακώτερον αὐτὸ ποιῆσαι βουληθείημεν, ἀρκεῖ τὸ ὄγδοον μέρος ἐμβάλλειν τοῦ εὐφορβίου, τουτέστιν γο α΄.

καὶ ἡμίσειαν, ἐπὶ τοῦ νέου καὶ θερμοτάτου, καθότι προεῖπον εὐφορβίου τῆς συμμετρίας ταύτης ὡρισμένης, ὡς ἐάν γε παλαιότερον ᾖ, καὶ διὰ τοῦτο ἀσθενέστερον, εἴρηται πρόσθεν ὡς πλέον εἶναι προσήκει τοῦτο τῆς τῶν ἄλλων ἀναλογίας.
εἰ δὲ μὴ μόνης ῥητίνης, ἀλλὰ καὶ πίττης ἐμβάλλειν ἐθελήσαιμεν, ἡμίλιτρον ἑκατέρας μίξομεν, ὡς εἶναι ἴσον τὸν σταθμὸν τῷ κηρῷ.
πολὺ δὲ κάλλιόν ἐστι τὸ φάρμακον, ἐὰν ἀντὶ τῆς ῥητίνης τε καὶ πίττης πρόπολιν μίξῃ τις ἴσην τῷ κηρῷ.
english_sentences: Remember, then, to observe in all cases what you have heard concerning wax and resin, [625] For it is not of things that are dry and parched, whether through time or through their nature from the beginning, but of things of moderate consistency that one must mix, in the composition of the drugs, as much of each as is found written by me.

Let, then, the form of the drug before us that is moderate in both power and consistency be one that has equal amounts of wax, roasted (phrykte) resin and oil, and a sixth part of euphorbium itself, so that there is a litra of each of those, but two ounces of euphorbium.

If, however, we should wish to make it softer, it suffices to put in an eighth part of euphorbium, that is, one ounce and a half—this proportion being defined, as I said before, for euphorbium that is fresh and hottest; since if it is older, and on that account weaker, it has been said earlier that this ought to be more than the proportion of the others.
And if we should wish to put in not resin alone but also pitch, we shall mix in half a litra of each, so that the weight is equal to the wax.
But the drug is far better if, in place of the resin and pitch, one mixes in propolis equal to the wax.

beads.greek: τὸ λιπαρὸν δ’ οὐκ ἐχούσης [626] αὐτῆς ὁμοίως ταῖς ῥητίναις, ἐὰν μὲν ἀνεπίδετον ἐθελήσωμεν εἷναι τὸ φάρμακον, ἐμβαλοῦμεν τῆς τερμινθίνης ἢ τῆς λάρικος ὀνομαζομένης ἢ καὶ τῆς συγκομιστῆς πευκίνης.
beads.english: But since it [626] does not have oiliness in the same way as the resins, if we wish the drug to be one that needs no bandaging (ἀνεπίδετον), we shall add some terebinth resin, or the resin called larch, or also the unrefined (συγκομιστή) pine resin.

beads.greek: ὀνομάζω δὲ συγκομιστὴν μὲν ἣν ἐν τοῖς γλωσσοκομείοις τε καὶ κεραμείοις κομίζουσι, ξύλα τε πολλὰ καὶ λιθώδη σώματα καθ’ ἑαυτὴν ἔχουσαν.
beads.english: I call 'unrefined' that which they transport in cases (γλωσσοκόμεια) and earthenware vessels, which has in it many pieces of wood and stony bodies.

beads.greek: ἐὰν δὲ τήξας αὐτὴν διηθήσῃς, καθαρὰ τότε γίνεται, ὁμοίως αὐτῇ τῇ κολοφωνίᾳ καὶ φρυκτῇ καλουμένῃ.
beads.english: But if you melt it and strain it, it then becomes pure, just like the Colophonian resin itself and the so-called roasted (phrykte) resin.

beads.greek: καὶ τῶν αὐτοῤῥύτων δὲ καλουμένων ῥητινῶν ἐγχωρεῖ μιγνύναι.
beads.english: It is also possible to mix in some of the so-called self-flowing (αὐτόρρυτοι) resins.

beads.greek: καλοῦσι δ’ αὐτὰς ἐν Λακεδαίμονι μὲν καί τισιν ἄλλοις χωρίοις πρωτοῤῥύτους, ἐν Κιλικίᾳ δὲ καπνέλαιον ὀνομάζουσι τὴν τοιαύτην ῥητίνην, ἁπασῶν τῶν ὑγρῶν ῥητινῶν ὑγροτέραν τε καὶ θερμοτέραν καὶ λεπτομερεστέραν οὖσαν, ὥσθ’ αὕτη μὲν συντελέσει τῇ τοῦ συντιθεμένου φαρμάκου δυνάμει, καὶ μάλιστ’ αὐτὴν ἐμβάλλειν προσήκει, ὅταν ἄτονον ᾖ τὸ εὐφόρ βιον.
beads.english: In Lacedaemon and in certain other places they call these 'first-flowing' (πρωτόρρυτοι), while in Cilicia they name such a resin kapnelaion (smoke-oil); it is moister, hotter and of finer parts than all the liquid resins, so that this one will contribute to the power of the drug being compounded, and it is especially fitting to add it when the euphorbium is weak.

beads.greek: ἔστι δὲ καὶ τῶν ἄλλων ῥητινῶν εὐωδεστέρα, καθάπερ ἡ τερμινθίνη καὶ ἡ ἐλατίνη.
beads.english: It is also more fragrant than the other resins, as are the terebinth and the fir resin.

beads.greek: λέλεκται δ’ ἔμπροσθεν ὅτι θερμοτέρα ἐστὶ τῆς τερμινθίνης ἡ ἐλατίνη, ταύτης δὲ ἡ στροβιλίνη.
beads.english: And it has been said earlier that the fir resin is hotter than the terebinth, and the strobilos (pine-cone) resin hotter than this.

greek_sentences: τὸ λιπαρὸν δ’ οὐκ ἐχούσης [626] αὐτῆς ὁμοίως ταῖς ῥητίναις, ἐὰν μὲν ἀνεπίδετον ἐθελήσωμεν εἷναι τὸ φάρμακον, ἐμβαλοῦμεν τῆς τερμινθίνης ἢ τῆς λάρικος ὀνομαζομένης ἢ καὶ τῆς συγκομιστῆς πευκίνης.
ὀνομάζω δὲ συγκομιστὴν μὲν ἣν ἐν τοῖς γλωσσοκομείοις τε καὶ κεραμείοις κομίζουσι, ξύλα τε πολλὰ καὶ λιθώδη σώματα καθ’ ἑαυτὴν ἔχουσαν.
ἐὰν δὲ τήξας αὐτὴν διηθήσῃς, καθαρὰ τότε γίνεται, ὁμοίως αὐτῇ τῇ κολοφωνίᾳ καὶ φρυκτῇ καλουμένῃ.
καὶ τῶν αὐτοῤῥύτων δὲ καλουμένων ῥητινῶν ἐγχωρεῖ μιγνύναι.

καλοῦσι δ’ αὐτὰς ἐν Λακεδαίμονι μὲν καί τισιν ἄλλοις χωρίοις πρωτοῤῥύτους, ἐν Κιλικίᾳ δὲ καπνέλαιον ὀνομάζουσι τὴν τοιαύτην ῥητίνην, ἁπασῶν τῶν ὑγρῶν ῥητινῶν ὑγροτέραν τε καὶ θερμοτέραν καὶ λεπτομερεστέραν οὖσαν, ὥσθ’ αὕτη μὲν συντελέσει τῇ τοῦ συντιθεμένου φαρμάκου δυνάμει, καὶ μάλιστ’ αὐτὴν ἐμβάλλειν προσήκει, ὅταν ἄτονον ᾖ τὸ εὐφόρ βιον.
ἔστι δὲ καὶ τῶν ἄλλων ῥητινῶν εὐωδεστέρα, καθάπερ ἡ τερμινθίνη καὶ ἡ ἐλατίνη.
λέλεκται δ’ ἔμπροσθεν ὅτι θερμοτέρα ἐστὶ τῆς τερμινθίνης ἡ ἐλατίνη, ταύτης δὲ ἡ στροβιλίνη.
english_sentences: But since it [626] does not have oiliness in the same way as the resins, if we wish the drug to be one that needs no bandaging (ἀνεπίδετον), we shall add some terebinth resin, or the resin called larch, or also the unrefined (συγκομιστή) pine resin.
I call 'unrefined' that which they transport in cases (γλωσσοκόμεια) and earthenware vessels, which has in it many pieces of wood and stony bodies.
But if you melt it and strain it, it then becomes pure, just like the Colophonian resin itself and the so-called roasted (phrykte) resin.
It is also possible to mix in some of the so-called self-flowing (αὐτόρρυτοι) resins.

In Lacedaemon and in certain other places they call these 'first-flowing' (πρωτόρρυτοι), while in Cilicia they name such a resin kapnelaion (smoke-oil); it is moister, hotter and of finer parts than all the liquid resins, so that this one will contribute to the power of the drug being compounded, and it is especially fitting to add it when the euphorbium is weak.
It is also more fragrant than the other resins, as are the terebinth and the fir resin.
And it has been said earlier that the fir resin is hotter than the terebinth, and the strobilos (pine-cone) resin hotter than this.

beads.greek: διαφέρει δὲ τῶν εἰρημένων ῥητινῶν ﻿ [627] τό τε στροβίλινον ὀνομαζόμενον φύσημα καὶ τὸ πιτύϊνον, ξηρὸν καὶ ἀλιπὲς καὶ αὐχμηρὸν ἑκάτερον ἐν τάχει γιγνόμενον, ὡς ἐν ὅλμῳ τε κόπτεσθαι καὶ διαττᾶσθαι κοσκίνῳ.
beads.english: Different from the resins mentioned are the so-called physēma (φύσημα) of the stone-pine and that of the pitys-pine, each of which quickly becomes dry, free of fat and parched, so that it is pounded in a mortar and sifted through a sieve.

beads.greek: διὰ τοῦτ’ οὖν ἄχρηστα μέν ἐστι ταῦτα πρὸς τὴν τοῦ προκειμένου σύνθεσιν φαρμάκου, συνεχέστατα δ’ ἐχρησάμην, ὅταν ᾖ τὸ εὐφόρβιον αὐτοετές.
beads.english: For this reason, then, these are useless for the composition of the drug before us; but I have used [it] most frequently whenever the euphorbium is of the same year.

beads.greek: τῇ δὲ συνθέσει τοῦ ἐλαίου καὶ τοῦ κηροῦ καὶ τῆς φρυκτῆς ῥητίνης ἑκάστου λίτραν μίαν, ἡμίλιτρον δὲ τῆς λιπαρᾶς πίσσης.
beads.english: For the composition, [I take] of oil and of wax and of roasted resin one litra of each, and half a litra of fatty pitch.

beads.greek: καὶ τούτοις τακεῖσιν εὐφορβίου μίγνυμι δύο οὐγγίας· εἰ δ’ ἀσθενέστερον εἴη, τρεῖς· εἰ δὲ τερμινθίνην ἐθέλοις μίξαι τῷ κηρῷ, μόνην· εἰς σύμμετρον αὐξήσεις τοῦ φαρμάκου σύστασιν, ἐὰν τριπλάσιος ὁ κηρὸς ᾖ, τῆς τερμινθίνης ὑγρᾶς καὶ νέας οὔσης.
beads.english: And to these, once melted, I mix two ounces of euphorbium; if it should be weaker, three. If you should wish to mix terebinth alone with the wax, you will bring the drug to a well-proportioned consistency if the wax is threefold, the terebinth being moist and fresh.

beads.greek: ἐξηρασμένης δ’ ὑπὸ χρόνου μίξεις ἐλαίου τὸ ἥμισυ τοῦ σταθμοῦ τῆς τερμινθίνης.
beads.english: But if it has been dried out by time, you will mix in oil, half the weight of the terebinth.

beads.greek: ὅλον δὲ τοῦτο τὸ ἐκ τῶν τριῶν μιχθὲν, τοῦ τ’ ἐλαίου λέγω καὶ τοῦ κηροῦ καὶ τῆς τερμινθίνης, ὅταν γένηται λίτρας μίας καὶ ἡμισείας τοῦ εὐφορβίου τοῦ αὐτοετοῦς προσλήψεται μίαν οὐγγίαν· εἰ δὲ μὴ τοιοῦτον εἴη, μίαν καὶ ἡμίσειαν.
beads.english: And this whole mixture made from the three—I mean the oil and the wax and the terebinth—when it amounts to one and a half litrai, will take in addition one ounce of euphorbium of the same year; if it is not such, one and a half.

beads.greek: ἐξ ὧν γ’ ἔμπροσθεν εἷπον ἤδη πολλάκις, ἔνεστιν ἡμῖν τὸ εὐφόρβιον αὔξειν ἀνάλογον τῷ χρόνῳ.
beads.english: On the basis of what I have already said many times before, it is possible for us to increase the euphorbium in proportion to its age.

greek_sentences: διαφέρει δὲ τῶν εἰρημένων ῥητινῶν ﻿ [627] τό τε στροβίλινον ὀνομαζόμενον φύσημα καὶ τὸ πιτύϊνον, ξηρὸν καὶ ἀλιπὲς καὶ αὐχμηρὸν ἑκάτερον ἐν τάχει γιγνόμενον, ὡς ἐν ὅλμῳ τε κόπτεσθαι καὶ διαττᾶσθαι κοσκίνῳ.
διὰ τοῦτ’ οὖν ἄχρηστα μέν ἐστι ταῦτα πρὸς τὴν τοῦ προκειμένου σύνθεσιν φαρμάκου, συνεχέστατα δ’ ἐχρησάμην, ὅταν ᾖ τὸ εὐφόρβιον αὐτοετές.
τῇ δὲ συνθέσει τοῦ ἐλαίου καὶ τοῦ κηροῦ καὶ τῆς φρυκτῆς ῥητίνης ἑκάστου λίτραν μίαν, ἡμίλιτρον δὲ τῆς λιπαρᾶς πίσσης.

καὶ τούτοις τακεῖσιν εὐφορβίου μίγνυμι δύο οὐγγίας· εἰ δ’ ἀσθενέστερον εἴη, τρεῖς· εἰ δὲ τερμινθίνην ἐθέλοις μίξαι τῷ κηρῷ, μόνην· εἰς σύμμετρον αὐξήσεις τοῦ φαρμάκου σύστασιν, ἐὰν τριπλάσιος ὁ κηρὸς ᾖ, τῆς τερμινθίνης ὑγρᾶς καὶ νέας οὔσης.
ἐξηρασμένης δ’ ὑπὸ χρόνου μίξεις ἐλαίου τὸ ἥμισυ τοῦ σταθμοῦ τῆς τερμινθίνης.

ὅλον δὲ τοῦτο τὸ ἐκ τῶν τριῶν μιχθὲν, τοῦ τ’ ἐλαίου λέγω καὶ τοῦ κηροῦ καὶ τῆς τερμινθίνης, ὅταν γένηται λίτρας μίας καὶ ἡμισείας τοῦ εὐφορβίου τοῦ αὐτοετοῦς προσλήψεται μίαν οὐγγίαν· εἰ δὲ μὴ τοιοῦτον εἴη, μίαν καὶ ἡμίσειαν.
ἐξ ὧν γ’ ἔμπροσθεν εἷπον ἤδη πολλάκις, ἔνεστιν ἡμῖν τὸ εὐφόρβιον αὔξειν ἀνάλογον τῷ χρόνῳ.
english_sentences: Different from the resins mentioned are the so-called physēma (φύσημα) of the stone-pine and that of the pitys-pine, each of which quickly becomes dry, free of fat and parched, so that it is pounded in a mortar and sifted through a sieve.
For this reason, then, these are useless for the composition of the drug before us; but I have used [it] most frequently whenever the euphorbium is of the same year.
For the composition, [I take] of oil and of wax and of roasted resin one litra of each, and half a litra of fatty pitch.
And to these, once melted, I mix two ounces of euphorbium; if it should be weaker, three.
If you should wish to mix terebinth alone with the wax, you will bring the drug to a well-proportioned consistency if the wax is threefold, the terebinth being moist and fresh.
But if it has been dried out by time, you will mix in oil, half the weight of the terebinth.

And this whole mixture made from the three—I mean the oil and the wax and the terebinth—when it amounts to one and a half litrai, will take in addition one ounce of euphorbium of the same year; if it is not such, one and a half.
On the basis of what I have already said many times before, it is possible for us to increase the euphorbium in proportion to its age.

beads.greek: καὶ [628] μέντοι κᾂν ἐπιτεθὲν τῷ τετρωμένῳ τὸ φάρμακον ἐν τῇ πρώτῃ χρήσει φαίνηταί πως ἀσθενέστερον, ἔνεστιν ἐλαίῳ τὸ εὐφόρβιον λειώσαντα μιγνύειν αὐτὸ τῷ ἐμπλαστρώδει φαρμάκῳ προμεμαλαγμένῳ κατὰ τὰ χεῖρας, οὕτως γὰρ ποιούντων, ἑτοίμως ἑνοῦται.
beads.english: And [628] indeed, even if the drug, when applied to the wounded person at its first use, appears somewhat weaker, it is possible, after triturating the euphorbium with oil, to mix it with the plaster-like drug that has been previously softened in the hands; for when one does so, it readily unites.

beads.greek: κατ’ αὐτὴν δὲ τὴν πρώτην σύνθεσιν τοῦ φαρμάκου κάλλιόν ἐστιν τὴν κηρωτὴν ἐξυσμένην, ἰδίᾳ προκατασκευάσαντα μιγνύειν οὕτω τῷ λελειωμένῳ μετὰ τοῦ ἐλαίου εὐφορβίῳ.
beads.english: But in the very first compounding of the drug it is better to prepare the cerate separately beforehand, scraped, and thus to mix it with the euphorbium that has been triturated together with the oil.

beads.greek: καταχυθέντων γὰρ αὐτοῦ τῶν τετηκότων ἐν τῇ θυείᾳ, αἱ καλούμεναι πολλάκις ἐγκηρίδες γίγνονται καὶ μάλισθ’ ὅταν ᾖ τὸ περιέχον ψυχρόν.
beads.english: For when the melted ingredients are poured over it in the mortar, the so-called enkerides (lumps of wax) often form, and especially when the surrounding air is cold.

beads.greek: ὕδατος δὲ βάλλειν τηκομένῳ τῷ κηρῷ μετὰ τῆς ῥητίνης οὐκ ἀναγκαῖον, ὡς ἐγὼ κατ’ ἀρχὰς ἐποίουν ἐπιμιγνὺς αὐτῷ τοσοῦτον, ὅσον ἔμελλεν ἀναλίσκεσθαι κατ’ αὐτὴν τὴν ἕψησιν.
beads.english: And it is not necessary to add water to the wax as it is being melted together with the resin, as I used to do at the beginning, mixing in with it as much as was going to be consumed during the boiling itself.

beads.greek: [Τὸ διὰ τῶν τηκτῶν συντιθέμενον φάρμακον.] Τηκτὰ καλῶ φάρμακα τά τε διὰ πυρὸς ὁμιλίας τηκόμενα καὶ τὰ δι’ ὑγρῶν τινῶν, οἷον ὕδατος, ὄξους, οἴνου.
beads.english: [The drug compounded from meltable substances.] I call meltable drugs both those that are melted through contact with fire and those melted by means of certain liquids, such as water, vinegar, wine.

greek_sentences: καὶ [628] μέντοι κᾂν ἐπιτεθὲν τῷ τετρωμένῳ τὸ φάρμακον ἐν τῇ πρώτῃ χρήσει φαίνηταί πως ἀσθενέστερον, ἔνεστιν ἐλαίῳ τὸ εὐφόρβιον λειώσαντα μιγνύειν αὐτὸ τῷ ἐμπλαστρώδει φαρμάκῳ προμεμαλαγμένῳ κατὰ τὰ χεῖρας, οὕτως γὰρ ποιούντων, ἑτοίμως ἑνοῦται.
κατ’ αὐτὴν δὲ τὴν πρώτην σύνθεσιν τοῦ φαρμάκου κάλλιόν ἐστιν τὴν κηρωτὴν ἐξυσμένην, ἰδίᾳ προκατασκευάσαντα μιγνύειν οὕτω τῷ λελειωμένῳ μετὰ τοῦ ἐλαίου εὐφορβίῳ.
καταχυθέντων γὰρ αὐτοῦ τῶν τετηκότων ἐν τῇ θυείᾳ, αἱ καλούμεναι πολλάκις ἐγκηρίδες γίγνονται καὶ μάλισθ’ ὅταν ᾖ τὸ περιέχον ψυχρόν.
ὕδατος δὲ βάλλειν τηκομένῳ τῷ κηρῷ μετὰ τῆς ῥητίνης οὐκ ἀναγκαῖον, ὡς ἐγὼ κατ’ ἀρχὰς ἐποίουν ἐπιμιγνὺς αὐτῷ τοσοῦτον, ὅσον ἔμελλεν ἀναλίσκεσθαι κατ’ αὐτὴν τὴν ἕψησιν.
[Τὸ διὰ τῶν τηκτῶν συντιθέμενον φάρμακον.] Τηκτὰ καλῶ φάρμακα τά τε διὰ πυρὸς ὁμιλίας τηκόμενα καὶ τὰ δι’ ὑγρῶν τινῶν, οἷον ὕδατος, ὄξους, οἴνου.
english_sentences: And [628] indeed, even if the drug, when applied to the wounded person at its first use, appears somewhat weaker, it is possible, after triturating the euphorbium with oil, to mix it with the plaster-like drug that has been previously softened in the hands; for when one does so, it readily unites.
But in the very first compounding of the drug it is better to prepare the cerate separately beforehand, scraped, and thus to mix it with the euphorbium that has been triturated together with the oil.
For when the melted ingredients are poured over it in the mortar, the so-called enkerides (lumps of wax) often form, and especially when the surrounding air is cold.

And it is not necessary to add water to the wax as it is being melted together with the resin, as I used to do at the beginning, mixing in with it as much as was going to be consumed during the boiling itself.
[The drug compounded from meltable substances.] I call meltable drugs both those that are melted through contact with fire and those melted by means of certain liquids, such as water, vinegar, wine.

beads.greek: δι’ ὄξους μὲν οὖν τήκεται πυρὸς χωρὶς ἀμμωνιακὸν θυμίαμα καὶ σαγαπηνὸς ὀπὸς, ὅτε τοῦ πάνακος ὁμοίως, ὃν ἐν συνθέτῳ [629] προσηγορίᾳ καλοῦσιν ὀποπάνακα.
beads.english: Now by means of vinegar, without fire, there are dissolved ammoniac incense and the juice of sagapenum, and likewise that of panax, which they call in a compound [629] appellation opopanax.

beads.greek: διὰ πυρὸς δὲ πρόπολις, κηρὸς, ῥητίνη, λάδανον, στέαρ, χαλβάνη.
beads.english: By means of fire: propolis, wax, resin, ladanum, fat, galbanum.

beads.greek: βέλ τιον δὲ ταύτην ἐπὶ διπλοῦ σκεύους τήκειν.
beads.english: It is better, however, to melt this last in a double vessel.

beads.greek: ὀνομάζομεν δὲ οὕτως, ὅταν ἐν κακκάβῃ θερμὸν ὕδωρ ἐχούσῃ σκεῦος ἕτερον ἐνίσταται μετὰ τῶν τηκτῶν ἔχον καὶ τὴν χαλβάνην, ὑποκαιομένης τῆς κακκάβης.
beads.english: We so name it when, in a cauldron holding hot water, another vessel is set, containing, together with the meltable substances, the galbanum too, while the cauldron is heated from beneath.

beads.greek: ἔστω δέ σοι καὶ τοιοῦτον ἐσκευασμένον τι φάρμακον, ἕν μὲν πάντως, ἄμεινον δὲ καὶ δύο.
beads.english: Let you also have some such drug prepared, one in any case, but better two.

beads.greek: ἔσται δ’ αὐτῶν τὸ μὲν ἰσχυρότερον τοιόνδε.
beads.english: Of these the stronger will be as follows.

beads.greek: ὀποπάνακα διαλύσας ὄξει λείωσον ἐπὶ πλέον, εἶτα τήξας ἐπὶ πυρὸς πρόπολίν τε καὶ χαλβάνην καὶ ῥητίνην τερμινθίνην μῖξον τῷ ὀποπάνακι.
beads.english: Having dissolved opopanax in vinegar, triturate it thoroughly; then, having melted over fire propolis and galbanum and terebinth resin, mix them with the opopanax.

beads.greek: τῶν μὲν οὖν ἄλλων ἑκάστου μέρος ἕν ἔστω, τῆς δὲ προπόλεως ἕξ νέας τε καὶ λιπαρᾶς οὔσης.
beads.english: Of each of the others let there be one part, but of propolis six, provided it is fresh and oily.

beads.greek: εἰ δὲ ξηρὰ καὶ παλαιὰ τύχοι, βέλτιον μὲν μηδ’ ὅλως χρῆσθαι τῇ τοιαύτῃ· εἰ δὲ ἀποροίης τῆς ἑτέρας, δύο μέρη μίξεις οὐχ ἕν.
beads.english: If it should happen to be dry and old, it is better not to use such at all; but if you are without the other kind, you will mix in two parts, not one.

beads.greek: εἰ δὲ μὴ παρείη σοι πρόπολις, ἀντ’ αὐτῆς ἔμβαλλε λιπαρὰν πίτταν, οἵα ἐστὶν ἥ τε Βρυτία καὶ ἡ ἐκ τῶν κατὰ τὸν Πόντον χωρίων κομιζομένη λιπαρά τε ἅμα καὶ εὐώδης, ἣν εἰς τὸ μέλαν ἀμαράκινον ἐμβάλλουσιν ὁποῖον ἔμπροσθεν ἅπαν ἐσκευάζετο.
beads.english: And if propolis is not available to you, put in its place oily pitch, such as the Bruttian is, and that brought from the regions about Pontus, which is at once oily and fragrant, and which they put into the black amaracine unguent, such as formerly all of it used to be prepared.

greek_sentences: δι’ ὄξους μὲν οὖν τήκεται πυρὸς χωρὶς ἀμμωνιακὸν θυμίαμα καὶ σαγαπηνὸς ὀπὸς, ὅτε τοῦ πάνακος ὁμοίως, ὃν ἐν συνθέτῳ [629] προσηγορίᾳ καλοῦσιν ὀποπάνακα.
διὰ πυρὸς δὲ πρόπολις, κηρὸς, ῥητίνη, λάδανον, στέαρ, χαλβάνη.
βέλ τιον δὲ ταύτην ἐπὶ διπλοῦ σκεύους τήκειν.
ὀνομάζομεν δὲ οὕτως, ὅταν ἐν κακκάβῃ θερμὸν ὕδωρ ἐχούσῃ σκεῦος ἕτερον ἐνίσταται μετὰ τῶν τηκτῶν ἔχον καὶ τὴν χαλβάνην, ὑποκαιομένης τῆς κακκάβης.
ἔστω δέ σοι καὶ τοιοῦτον ἐσκευασμένον τι φάρμακον, ἕν μὲν πάντως, ἄμεινον δὲ καὶ δύο.
ἔσται δ’ αὐτῶν τὸ μὲν ἰσχυρότερον τοιόνδε.
ὀποπάνακα διαλύσας ὄξει λείωσον ἐπὶ πλέον, εἶτα τήξας ἐπὶ πυρὸς πρόπολίν τε καὶ χαλβάνην καὶ ῥητίνην τερμινθίνην μῖξον τῷ ὀποπάνακι.
τῶν μὲν οὖν ἄλλων ἑκάστου μέρος ἕν ἔστω, τῆς δὲ προπόλεως ἕξ νέας τε καὶ λιπαρᾶς οὔσης.
εἰ δὲ ξηρὰ καὶ παλαιὰ τύχοι, βέλτιον μὲν μηδ’ ὅλως χρῆσθαι τῇ τοιαύτῃ· εἰ δὲ ἀποροίης τῆς ἑτέρας, δύο μέρη μίξεις οὐχ ἕν.

εἰ δὲ μὴ παρείη σοι πρόπολις, ἀντ’ αὐτῆς ἔμβαλλε λιπαρὰν πίτταν, οἵα ἐστὶν ἥ τε Βρυτία καὶ ἡ ἐκ τῶν κατὰ τὸν Πόντον χωρίων κομιζομένη λιπαρά τε ἅμα καὶ εὐώδης, ἣν εἰς τὸ μέλαν ἀμαράκινον ἐμβάλλουσιν ὁποῖον ἔμπροσθεν ἅπαν ἐσκευάζετο.
english_sentences: Now by means of vinegar, without fire, there are dissolved ammoniac incense and the juice of sagapenum, and likewise that of panax, which they call in a compound [629] appellation opopanax.
By means of fire: propolis, wax, resin, ladanum, fat, galbanum.
It is better, however, to melt this last in a double vessel.
We so name it when, in a cauldron holding hot water, another vessel is set, containing, together with the meltable substances, the galbanum too, while the cauldron is heated from beneath.
Let you also have some such drug prepared, one in any case, but better two.
Of these the stronger will be as follows.
Having dissolved opopanax in vinegar, triturate it thoroughly; then, having melted over fire propolis and galbanum and terebinth resin, mix them with the opopanax.
Of each of the others let there be one part, but of propolis six, provided it is fresh and oily.
If it should happen to be dry and old, it is better not to use such at all; but if you are without the other kind, you will mix in two parts, not one.

And if propolis is not available to you, put in its place oily pitch, such as the Bruttian is, and that brought from the regions about Pontus, which is at once oily and fragrant, and which they put into the black amaracine unguent, such as formerly all of it used to be prepared.

beads.greek: [630] νυνὶ γὰρ καὶ χωρὶς αὐτῆς ὑπόλευκον ἀμαράκινον συντιθέασιν.
beads.english: [630] For nowadays they compose a whitish amaracine even without it.

beads.greek: εἰ δὲ καὶ τῆς τοιαύτης ἀποροίης, τῇ ἄλλῃ χρῶ, μετὰ τοῦ καὶ τὴν τερμινθίνην ὡς εἴρηται διπλασιάζειν.
beads.english: But if you lack this kind too, use the other, while also doubling the terebinth, as has been said.

beads.greek: ἐγὼ δέ ποτε καὶ μόνον ἐπέθηκα τὸ διὰ τῆς λιπαρᾶς πίττης φάρμακον, ᾧ καὶ πρὸς τοὺς λυσσοδήκτους χρῶμαι.
beads.english: I myself have on occasion also applied on its own the drug made with the oily pitch, which I also use for those bitten by rabid dogs.

beads.greek: μόνην γὰρ τοῦτο τὴν λιπαρὰν ἔχει πίτταν ἡψημένην ἐν ὄξει δριμεῖ κατὰ συμμετρίαν τοιάνδε. ξέστης εἷς Ῥωμαϊκὸς τοῦ ὄξους, μία δὲ λίτρα τῆς πίττης, τοῦ δ’ ὀποπάνακος τὸ τέταρτον μέρος τῆς λίτρας, ὅπερ ἐστὶν γο γ΄.
beads.english: For this contains only the oily pitch, boiled in acrid vinegar, according to the following proportion: one Roman sextarius of the vinegar, one litra of the pitch, and of the opopanax a fourth part of a litra, which is three ounces.

beads.greek: τοῦτο τὸ φάρμακον οὐκ ἐᾷ τῶν λυσσοδήκτων συνουλωθῆναι τὸ ἕλκος.
beads.english: This drug does not allow the wound of those bitten by rabid dogs to cicatrize.

beads.greek: ἐπιτήδειον δ’ ἐστὶ καὶ τοῖς νενυγμένοις νευρῶδές τι μόριον, οὐκ ἐῶν μύσαι τὸ στόμιον τοῦ νύγματος.
beads.english: It is also suitable for those who have been punctured in some sinewy part, since it does not allow the mouth of the puncture to close.

beads.greek: ἀλλ’ ἐπεὶ σκληρόν ἐστιν, ἐπὶ μόνων τῶν σκληρῶν σωμάτων αὐτῷ χρηστέον, ὁποῖα τά τε τῶν σκαπανέων εἰσὶ καὶ θεριστῶν.
beads.english: But since it is hard, it is to be used only on hard bodies, such as those of diggers and reapers.

greek_sentences: [630] νυνὶ γὰρ καὶ χωρὶς αὐτῆς ὑπόλευκον ἀμαράκινον συντιθέασιν.
εἰ δὲ καὶ τῆς τοιαύτης ἀποροίης, τῇ ἄλλῃ χρῶ, μετὰ τοῦ καὶ τὴν τερμινθίνην ὡς εἴρηται διπλασιάζειν.
ἐγὼ δέ ποτε καὶ μόνον ἐπέθηκα τὸ διὰ τῆς λιπαρᾶς πίττης φάρμακον, ᾧ καὶ πρὸς τοὺς λυσσοδήκτους χρῶμαι.
μόνην γὰρ τοῦτο τὴν λιπαρὰν ἔχει πίτταν ἡψημένην ἐν ὄξει δριμεῖ κατὰ συμμετρίαν τοιάνδε.
ξέστης εἷς Ῥωμαϊκὸς τοῦ ὄξους, μία δὲ λίτρα τῆς πίττης, τοῦ δ’ ὀποπάνακος τὸ τέταρτον μέρος τῆς λίτρας, ὅπερ ἐστὶν γο γ΄.
τοῦτο τὸ φάρμακον οὐκ ἐᾷ τῶν λυσσοδήκτων συνουλωθῆναι τὸ ἕλκος.
ἐπιτήδειον δ’ ἐστὶ καὶ τοῖς νενυγμένοις νευρῶδές τι μόριον, οὐκ ἐῶν μύσαι τὸ στόμιον τοῦ νύγματος.
ἀλλ’ ἐπεὶ σκληρόν ἐστιν, ἐπὶ μόνων τῶν σκληρῶν σωμάτων αὐτῷ χρηστέον, ὁποῖα τά τε τῶν σκαπανέων εἰσὶ καὶ θεριστῶν.
english_sentences: [630] For nowadays they compose a whitish amaracine even without it.
But if you lack this kind too, use the other, while also doubling the terebinth, as has been said.
I myself have on occasion also applied on its own the drug made with the oily pitch, which I also use for those bitten by rabid dogs.

For this contains only the oily pitch, boiled in acrid vinegar, according to the following proportion: one Roman sextarius of the vinegar, one litra of the pitch, and of the opopanax a fourth part of a litra, which is three ounces.
This drug does not allow the wound of those bitten by rabid dogs to cicatrize.
It is also suitable for those who have been punctured in some sinewy part, since it does not allow the mouth of the puncture to close.
But since it is hard, it is to be used only on hard bodies, such as those of diggers and reapers.

beads.greek: εἰ δὲ μόνον ὑμῶν τινι παρείη τοῦτο, τοῦ νενυγμένου παιδὸς ὄντος ἢ γυναικὸς ἢ ἁπαλοσάρκου τινὸς, ἔνεστι τήκειν αὐτὸ, μετά τινος τῶν διαφορητικῶν μύρων, ἀμαρανίκου τε καὶ ὀποβαλσάμου μάλιστα, δευτέρου δὲ ἰρίνου καὶ κομμαγηνοῦ, μὴ παρόντων [631] δὲ τούτων, λευκίνου τε καὶ σουσίνου καὶ κυπρίνου.
beads.english: But if one of you should have only this at hand, and the person punctured is a child or a woman or someone of soft flesh, it is possible to melt it together with one of the discutient unguents—above all the amaracine (ἀμαρανίκου, presumably ἀμαρακίνου) and opobalsamum, secondarily the iris and the Commagene unguent, and when these are not available, [631] the white-violet, the lily, and henna oil.

beads.greek: καὶ τούτων δ’ ἀπορῶν, ἐλαίῳ τῆξον αὐτὸ παλαιῷ, ἢ εἴπερ ἐν Ἀλεξανδρεία τύχοις ὢν, κικίνῳ τε καὶ ῥαφανίνῳ, ἢ πλεῖστα γὰρ ταῦτα κατ’ ἐκείνην τὴν πόλιν ἐστὶν, ὥσπερ γε καὶ καθ’ ὅλην τὴν Αἴγυπτον.
beads.english: And if you lack these as well, melt it with old oil, or, if you happen to be in Alexandria, with castor oil and radish oil, for these are most abundant in that city, as indeed throughout the whole of Egypt.

beads.greek: οὐ χαλεπῶς δ’ εὐπορούμενον ἐν τοῖς χωρίοις ἐκείνοις ἐστὶ καὶ τὸ σινάπινον ἔλαιον, οὗ καὶ αὐτοῦ μίξας ποτὲ μέρος εὔδηλον ὅτι δριμύτατον ἐργάσῃ φάρμακον ὡς πρὸς τὸ διανοίγειν τὰ μεμυκότα νύγματα.
beads.english: Mustard oil, too, is obtained without difficulty in those regions; and if at some point you mix in a portion of this as well, it is quite clear that you will produce a most pungent drug with respect to opening up punctures that have closed.

beads.greek: πρόδηλον δ’ ἔστιν ἐκ τῶν εἰρημένων, κᾂν σαγαπηνὸν ἀντὶ ὀποπάνακος ἐν θυείᾳ δι’ ὄξους προλειώσας, ἐπιχέοις αὐτῷ τετηκυῖαν ῥητίνην καὶ πρόπολιν καὶ στέαρ τι τῶν δριμυτέρων, ἐκ ταὐτοῦ γένους ἔσται τὸ φάρμακον.
