[Φαιὰ Αἰγυπτία Ἀνδρομάχου.] Ὁ μὲν γὰρ Ἀνδρόμαχος οὕτως ἔγραψε κατὰ λέξιν.
english_sentences: Some of them, however, who wrote down notable drugs of many uses (polychrēsta) — those at least who were more careful — added, in addition to the other things they profess these drugs [890] to do, sometimes that they are beneficial also for those wounded in the nerves, at other times for severings of nerves and muscles, and there are times when they said that they also help punctures or contusions of them.
But you, from what you have learned, are able to recognise before trial whether someone professes things possible or impossible concerning what he has written.
And it is also possible for you, in the case of drugs that have been written down without a statement of what they are naturally able to do, to recognise the conditions on which they are to be used.

So then, in order that I may begin, by way of example, with a certain plaster drug of many uses (polychrēston), written second in order in the pharmacological book of Andromachus which he composed on the drugs applied externally to the body, without his indicating for what it is especially to be used, it is possible for you once again to exercise yourselves in how one must recognise, from the simple drugs written down, the power of the compound.
[The grey Egyptian of Andromachus.] For Andromachus wrote as follows, word for word: The grey Egyptian.
Take litharge, 44 drachms; castor oil, 6 cotylae; wax, 144 drachms; ammoniac incense, 72 drachms; terebinth resin, 36 drachms.

beads.english: of burnt wool [891] 18 drachms; of scale of steel (stomoma) 8 drachms; of scale of copper 8 drachms; of aristolochia 8 drachms; of frankincense 8 drachms; some add myrrh 4 drachms; of opopanax 2 drachms; of sea-water 50 drachms, for the soaking of the wax.
This, then, is the recipe of the drug, which is in truth a good one and of many uses; but he himself omitted to say in which cases it is to be used.

Now if, having first stated the power of each of the simple drugs, as we did in eleven books, and having also written some general method of the composition of drugs, as I did in the book preceding this one, he had proposed such recipes to the others then living for the sake of exercise, so that they might answer for which affections it can be useful, we would truly have praised his teaching.

beads.greek: εἰς ἐμβροχὴν κηροῦ. αὕτη μὲν ἡ γραφὴ τοῦ φαρμάκου καλοῦ καὶ πολυχρήστου κατὰ ἀλήθειαν ὄντος, ἀλλὰ αὐτός γε παρέλιπεν εἰπεῖν ἐπὶ τίνων αὐτῷ χρηστέον.
beads.english: But since he did none of these things, one might find fault with him in every way.

beads.greek: εἰ μὲν οὖν προειρηκὼς ἑκάστου γε τῶν ἁπλῶν φαρμάκων τὴν δύναμιν, ὥσπερ ἡμεῖς ἐποιήσαμεν ἐν ὑπομνήμασιν ἕνδεκα, μέθοδόν τέ τινα γεγραφὼς καθόλου συνθέσεως φαρμάκων, ὡς ἐγὼ κατὰ τὸ πρὸ τοῦδε τοῦ βιβλίου πεποίημαι, προὔβαλλε ζῶσι τοῖς ἑτέροις τοιαύτας γραφὰς ἕνεκα γυμνασίας, ὅπως ἀποκρίνοιντο πρὸς τίνα παθήματα δύναται χρήσιμον ὑπάρχειν, ἐπῃνέσαμεν ὄντως αὐτοῦ τὴν διδασκαλίαν.
ἐπεὶ δ’ οὐδὲν τούτων ἐποίησε, παντοίως ἄν τις αὐτῷ μέμψαιτο. διὰ τοῦτο οὖν εἰκότως αἱ φαρμακίτιδες αὐτοῦ βίβλοι παμπόλλων φαρμάκων ἀρίστων ἔχουσαι συνθέσεις ἠμέληνται τοῖς ἰατροῖς.
beads.english: For this reason, then, his books on drugs, although they contain the compositions of a very great many excellent drugs, have with good reason been neglected by physicians.

greek_sentences: αὕτη μὲν ἡ γραφὴ τοῦ φαρμάκου καλοῦ καὶ πολυχρήστου κατὰ ἀλήθειαν ὄντος, ἀλλὰ αὐτός γε παρέλιπεν εἰπεῖν ἐπὶ τίνων αὐτῷ χρηστέον.

εἰ μὲν οὖν προειρηκὼς ἑκάστου γε τῶν ἁπλῶν φαρμάκων τὴν δύναμιν, ὥσπερ ἡμεῖς ἐποιήσαμεν ἐν ὑπομνήμασιν ἕνδεκα, μέθοδόν τέ τινα γεγραφὼς καθόλου συνθέσεως φαρμάκων, ὡς ἐγὼ κατὰ τὸ πρὸ τοῦδε τοῦ βιβλίου πεποίημαι, προὔβαλλε ζῶσι τοῖς ἑτέροις τοιαύτας γραφὰς ἕνεκα γυμνασίας, ὅπως ἀποκρίνοιντο πρὸς τίνα παθήματα δύναται χρήσιμον ὑπάρχειν, ἐπῃνέσαμεν ὄντως αὐτοῦ τὴν διδασκαλίαν.

But since he did none of these things, one might find fault with him in every way.
For this reason, then, his books on drugs, although they contain the compositions of a very great many excellent drugs, have with good reason been neglected by physicians.

beads.greek: ἐν γὰρ τοῖς χιλίοις εἷς τις δοκεῖ τὸ τέλος ἔχειν τῆς τέχνης, οἱ δ’ ἄλλοι [892] τοῖς ἰδιώταις ὡσαύτως ἀγαπῶσιν, ἐὰν τοῖς σαφῶς γεγραμμένοις φαρμάκοις ὀρθῶς χρῆσθαι δύνωνται.
beads.english: For among a thousand, some one person seems to possess the perfection of the art, while the rest, [892] just like laymen, are content if they are able to use correctly the drugs that have been clearly written up.

beads.greek: καὶ τί δεῖ λέγειν περὶ τῶν τοιούτων ἰατρῶν; ὅπου δὲ καὶ τῶν ἐμπειρικῶν ὀνομαζομένων ἔνιοι καίτοι ἀξιόλογοι διὰ τῶν τῆς τέχνης ἔργων ὀφθέντες, ὅμως ἀγνοεῖν φασιν ᾧτινι λογισμῷ τῶν συνθέτων φαρμάκων ἕκαστον εὕρηται, καὶ τί λέγω λογισμῷ;
beads.english: And why need one speak of such physicians, when even some of those called Empiricists, although they have shown themselves noteworthy through the works of the art, nevertheless say that they do not know by what reasoning each of the compound drugs was discovered—and why do I say 'by what reasoning'?

beads.greek: τὴν ἀρχὴν γὰρ οὐ λογισμῷ φασιν εὑρῆσθαι τῶν τοιούτων οὐδέν.
beads.english: For they say that none of such things was discovered by reasoning at all.

beads.greek: ἄχρηστος οὖν αὐτοῖς ἐστιν ἡ τῆς φαιᾶς ταύτης ἐμπλάστρου γραφὴ, τὸ χρῶμα μόνον ἐν τῷ προγράμματι διδασκούσης χωρὶς τῆς κατὰ δύναμιν ἐπαγγελίας, ἣν ἄμεινον ἦν γεγράφθαι πρὸ τοῦ χρώματος.
beads.english: Useless to them, therefore, is the prescription of this grey plaster, which in its heading teaches only the colour, without the professed virtue in respect of its power, which it would have been better to have written before the colour.

beads.greek: ἐπεὶ τοίνυν ὁ Ἀνδρόμαχος εἰπεῖν παρέλιπε τὴν δύναμιν αὐτῆς, ἡμεῖς εὑρεῖν πειραθῶμεν ἐκ τῆς τῶν μιγνυμένων φαρμάκων ἰδέας τε καὶ δυνάμεως.
beads.english: Since, then, Andromachus omitted to state its power, let us attempt to discover it from the kind and the power of the drugs that are mixed in it.

beads.greek: ἡ μὲν δὴ λιθάργυρος ὅτι τῆς μέσης οὖσα κράσεως ἐν τῷ θερμαίνειν καὶ ψύχειν ἀποκεχώρηκε βραχὺ πρὸς τὸ ξηραίνειν ἐμάθετε.
beads.english: Now you have learned that litharge, being of the middle mixture with respect to heating and cooling, has departed slightly towards drying.

greek_sentences: ἐν γὰρ τοῖς χιλίοις εἷς τις δοκεῖ τὸ τέλος ἔχειν τῆς τέχνης, οἱ δ’ ἄλλοι [892] τοῖς ἰδιώταις ὡσαύτως ἀγαπῶσιν, ἐὰν τοῖς σαφῶς γεγραμμένοις φαρμάκοις ὀρθῶς χρῆσθαι δύνωνται.
καὶ τί δεῖ λέγειν περὶ τῶν τοιούτων ἰατρῶν;
ὅπου δὲ καὶ τῶν ἐμπειρικῶν ὀνομαζομένων ἔνιοι καίτοι ἀξιόλογοι διὰ τῶν τῆς τέχνης ἔργων ὀφθέντες, ὅμως ἀγνοεῖν φασιν ᾧτινι λογισμῷ τῶν συνθέτων φαρμάκων ἕκαστον εὕρηται, καὶ τί λέγω λογισμῷ;
τὴν ἀρχὴν γὰρ οὐ λογισμῷ φασιν εὑρῆσθαι τῶν τοιούτων οὐδέν.
ἄχρηστος οὖν αὐτοῖς ἐστιν ἡ τῆς φαιᾶς ταύτης ἐμπλάστρου γραφὴ, τὸ χρῶμα μόνον ἐν τῷ προγράμματι διδασκούσης χωρὶς τῆς κατὰ δύναμιν ἐπαγγελίας, ἣν ἄμεινον ἦν γεγράφθαι πρὸ τοῦ χρώματος.
ἐπεὶ τοίνυν ὁ Ἀνδρόμαχος εἰπεῖν παρέλιπε τὴν δύναμιν αὐτῆς, ἡμεῖς εὑρεῖν πειραθῶμεν ἐκ τῆς τῶν μιγνυμένων φαρμάκων ἰδέας τε καὶ δυνάμεως.
ἡ μὲν δὴ λιθάργυρος ὅτι τῆς μέσης οὖσα κράσεως ἐν τῷ θερμαίνειν καὶ ψύχειν ἀποκεχώρηκε βραχὺ πρὸς τὸ ξηραίνειν ἐμάθετε.
english_sentences: For among a thousand, some one person seems to possess the perfection of the art, while the rest, [892] just like laymen, are content if they are able to use correctly the drugs that have been clearly written up.

And why need one speak of such physicians, when even some of those called Empiricists, although they have shown themselves noteworthy through the works of the art, nevertheless say that they do not know by what reasoning each of the compound drugs was discovered—and why do I say 'by what reasoning'?
For they say that none of such things was discovered by reasoning at all.

Useless to them, therefore, is the prescription of this grey plaster, which in its heading teaches only the colour, without the professed virtue in respect of its power, which it would have been better to have written before the colour.
Since, then, Andromachus omitted to state its power, let us attempt to discover it from the kind and the power of the drugs that are mixed in it.
Now you have learned that litharge, being of the middle mixture with respect to heating and cooling, has departed slightly towards drying.

beads.greek: καὶ μέντοι καὶ τὴν χρείαν αὐτῆς εἰς τὰς ἐμπλάστρους ἔγνωτε διττὴν ὑπάρχουσαν, εἰ μὲν ἄτηκτος μείνειεν, ὡς ὕλης μόνον, εἰ δὲ τακείη καὶ ὡς ξηραίνειν δυναμένης [893] καὶ μᾶλλον εἰ ἐπὶ πλέον ἑψηθείη. νυνὶ μέντοι ζήτημά ἐστι ἐπὶ πόσον ἑψηθήσεται, κο.
beads.english: And indeed you also know that its use in plasters is twofold: if it remains unmelted, as material only; but if it is melted, also as something able to dry, [893] and the more so if it is boiled for longer.

beads.greek: στ΄. γράψαντος τοῦ Ἀνδρομάχου μίγνυσθαι χρῆναι τοῦ κίκεως, ὅπερ ἐστὶν ἐλαίου κικίνου.
beads.english: Now, however, there is a question as to how far it will be boiled, since Andromachus has written that six cotylae of kiki, which is castor oil, must be mixed in.

beads.greek: πόσων γὰρ οὐγγιῶν τὴν ἐκ τῆς Ῥωμαϊκῆς λίτρας εἶναι βούλεται κοτύλην, οὐκ ἐδήλωσε· καίτοι βέλτιον ἦν ἐν Ῥώμῃ βεβιωκότα λιτρῶν μὲν καὶ ξεστῶν καὶ οὐγγιῶν μεμνῆσθαι, παραλιπεῖν δὲ τὸ τῆς κοτύλης ὄνομα ταῖς ἔξω τῆς Ἰταλίας πόλεσιν Ἑλληνικαῖς ὑπάρχον ἐν χρήσει.
beads.english: For he did not make clear of how many ounces, reckoned from the Roman litra, he wants the cotyle to be; and yet it would have been better for one who had lived in Rome to speak of litrai and xestai and ounces, and to leave aside the name of the cotyle, which is in use in the Greek cities outside Italy.

beads.greek: εἰ μὲν οὖν ἐν ἁπάσαις αὐταῖς ταὐτὸ ἦν ὄνομα τῆς κοτύλης, οὐδὲν ἂν ἦν ζήτημα.
beads.english: Now if the name of the cotyle were the same in all of them, there would be no question.

beads.greek: νυνὶ δὲ ἐπειδὴ παμπόλλη διαφορὰ κατὰ τὸ ποσὸν ἐν αὐταῖς ἐστιν, ἐχρῆν αὐτὸν εἰπεῖν ἤτοι γε ὅτι τὴν Ἀττικὴν λέγω κοτύλην ἢ τὴν Ἀλεξανδρεωτικὴν ἢ τὴν Ἐφεσίαν ἤ τινα ἄλλην.
beads.english: But as it is, since there is a very great difference in quantity among them, he ought to have said either 'I mean the Attic cotyle' or the Alexandrian or the Ephesian or some other.

beads.greek: οἱ μὲν οὖν πλεῖστοι τῶν γραψάντων περὶ μέτρων καὶ σταθμῶν θ΄. φασὶν οὐγγιῶν τῶν ἐκ τῆς Ῥωμαϊκῆς λίτρας τὴν ὑπὸ τῶν ἰατρῶν ἐν τοῖς φαρμακίτισι βιβλίοις γεγραμμένην κοτύλην.
beads.english: Now the majority of those who have written on measures and weights say that the cotyle written of by physicians in the pharmacological books is of nine ounces, of those reckoned from the Roman litra.

beads.greek: ἄλλοι δὲ τὴν τῶν ιβ΄. φασὶν οὐγγιῶν ὑπ’ αὐτῶν λέγεσθαι, καθάπερ ἐν Ῥώμῃ τὴν λίτραν τοῦ ἐλαίου συνήθως ὀνομάζουσιν.
beads.english: But others say that the one of twelve ounces is meant by them, just as in Rome they customarily name the litra of oil.

greek_sentences: καὶ μέντοι καὶ τὴν χρείαν αὐτῆς εἰς τὰς ἐμπλάστρους ἔγνωτε διττὴν ὑπάρχουσαν, εἰ μὲν ἄτηκτος μείνειεν, ὡς ὕλης μόνον, εἰ δὲ τακείη καὶ ὡς ξηραίνειν δυναμένης [893] καὶ μᾶλλον εἰ ἐπὶ πλέον ἑψηθείη.
νυνὶ μέντοι ζήτημά ἐστι ἐπὶ πόσον ἑψηθήσεται, κο.
γράψαντος τοῦ Ἀνδρομάχου μίγνυσθαι χρῆναι τοῦ κίκεως, ὅπερ ἐστὶν ἐλαίου κικίνου.

πόσων γὰρ οὐγγιῶν τὴν ἐκ τῆς Ῥωμαϊκῆς λίτρας εἶναι βούλεται κοτύλην, οὐκ ἐδήλωσε· καίτοι βέλτιον ἦν ἐν Ῥώμῃ βεβιωκότα λιτρῶν μὲν καὶ ξεστῶν καὶ οὐγγιῶν μεμνῆσθαι, παραλιπεῖν δὲ τὸ τῆς κοτύλης ὄνομα ταῖς ἔξω τῆς Ἰταλίας πόλεσιν Ἑλληνικαῖς ὑπάρχον ἐν χρήσει.
εἰ μὲν οὖν ἐν ἁπάσαις αὐταῖς ταὐτὸ ἦν ὄνομα τῆς κοτύλης, οὐδὲν ἂν ἦν ζήτημα.
νυνὶ δὲ ἐπειδὴ παμπόλλη διαφορὰ κατὰ τὸ ποσὸν ἐν αὐταῖς ἐστιν, ἐχρῆν αὐτὸν εἰπεῖν ἤτοι γε ὅτι τὴν Ἀττικὴν λέγω κοτύλην ἢ τὴν Ἀλεξανδρεωτικὴν ἢ τὴν Ἐφεσίαν ἤ τινα ἄλλην.
οἱ μὲν οὖν πλεῖστοι τῶν γραψάντων περὶ μέτρων καὶ σταθμῶν θ΄.
φασὶν οὐγγιῶν τῶν ἐκ τῆς Ῥωμαϊκῆς λίτρας τὴν ὑπὸ τῶν ἰατρῶν ἐν τοῖς φαρμακίτισι βιβλίοις γεγραμμένην κοτύλην.
φασὶν οὐγγιῶν ὑπ’ αὐτῶν λέγεσθαι, καθάπερ ἐν Ῥώμῃ τὴν λίτραν τοῦ ἐλαίου συνήθως ὀνομάζουσιν.
english_sentences: And indeed you also know that its use in plasters is twofold: if it remains unmelted, as material only; but if it is melted, also as something able to dry, [893] and the more so if it is boiled for longer.
Now, however, there is a question as to how far it will be boiled, since Andromachus has written that six cotylae of kiki, which is castor oil, must be mixed in.

For he did not make clear of how many ounces, reckoned from the Roman litra, he wants the cotyle to be; and yet it would have been better for one who had lived in Rome to speak of litrai and xestai and ounces, and to leave aside the name of the cotyle, which is in use in the Greek cities outside Italy.
Now if the name of the cotyle were the same in all of them, there would be no question.
But as it is, since there is a very great difference in quantity among them, he ought to have said either 'I mean the Attic cotyle' or the Alexandrian or the Ephesian or some other.
Now the majority of those who have written on measures and weights say that the cotyle written of by physicians in the pharmacological books is of nine ounces, of those reckoned from the Roman litra.
But others say that the one of twelve ounces is meant by them, just as in Rome they customarily name the litra of oil.

beads.greek: ἤδη δέ τινος ἤκουσα λέγοντος ﻿ [894] γο ιστ΄. Ῥωμαϊκὰς ἔχειν τὴν ἐν ταῖς φαρμακίτισι βίβλοις γεγραμμένην ὑπὸ τῶν ἰατρῶν κοτύλην, οὐ μικρὰ δέ ἐστι διαφορὰ πρὸς τὴν τοῦ φαρμάκου δύναμιν ἢ μεγάλας ἐμβάλλειν ἢ μικρὰς τὰς κοτύλας.
beads.english: But I have already heard someone saying that the kotyle written by the physicians in the pharmacological books [894] has sixteen Roman ounces; and it is no small difference with respect to the power of the drug whether one puts in large kotylai or small ones.

beads.greek: ἐγὼ γοῦν ἐν τῇ Ῥώμῃ τὴν τοῦ ἐλαίου καλουμένην λίτραν, ἣν διὰ τῶν κατατετμημένων κεράτων μετροῦσιν, ἔστησά ποτε βουλόμενος μαθεῖν ὁπόσον ἔχει σταθμὸν τοῦ βάρους.
beads.english: I, at any rate, in Rome once weighed the so-called litra of oil, which they measure by means of the graduated horns, wishing to learn how much weight it has by the balance.

beads.greek: εὗρον δὲ καὶ ταῖς σταθμικαῖς δέκα οὐγγίαις ἴσας τὰς μετρικὰς τοῦ ἐλαίου ιβ΄.
beads.english: And I found that the twelve measure-ounces of oil are equal to ten weight-ounces.

beads.greek: διὸ γράφειν ἐχρῆν ἐπιμελέστερον ἐν ταῖς φαρμακίτισι βίβλοις τοὺς ἰατροὺς, ὁποίας τινὰς κελεύουσι βάλλεσθαι τὰς οὐγγίας ἢ τὰς λίτρας τῶν ὑγρῶν φαρμάκων, πότερα τὰς μετρικὰς ἢ τὰς σταθμικάς.
beads.english: Therefore the physicians ought to write more carefully in the pharmacological books what sort of ounces or litrai of the liquid drugs they order to be put in, whether the measure-ones or the weight-ones.

beads.greek: πρόδηλον γὰρ, ὅτι τῶν ὑγρῶν τούτων σωμάτων, ὥσπερ καὶ τῶν στερεῶν, τὰ μέν ἐστι βαρύτερα, τὰ δὲ κουφότερα.
beads.english: For it is evident that of these liquid bodies, just as of the solid ones, some are heavier and others lighter.

beads.greek: καὶ λέλεκταί μοι κατὰ λόγον ἕτερον ἑκάστου τῶν εἰς τὰ φάρμακα βαλλομένων ὑγρῶν ὁ σταθμὸς, ἀλλὰ νῦν γε τὸ προκείμενον ἀναλάβωμεν.
beads.english: And the weight of each of the liquids put into drugs has been stated by me in another treatise; but now let us resume the matter before us.

beads.greek: τὰς γάρ τοι τρεῖς κοτύλας, εἰ μὲν ἐξ ἐννέα τις οὐγγιῶν μετρικῶν ἑκάστην θείη, τὰς μὲν τρεῖς οὐγγιῶν ἑπτὰ καὶ κ΄. ἐργάσεται.
beads.english: For as to the three kotylai, if one sets each at nine measure-ounces, he will make the three come to twenty-seven ounces.

greek_sentences: ἤδη δέ τινος ἤκουσα λέγοντος ﻿ [894] γο ιστ΄.
Ῥωμαϊκὰς ἔχειν τὴν ἐν ταῖς φαρμακίτισι βίβλοις γεγραμμένην ὑπὸ τῶν ἰατρῶν κοτύλην, οὐ μικρὰ δέ ἐστι διαφορὰ πρὸς τὴν τοῦ φαρμάκου δύναμιν ἢ μεγάλας ἐμβάλλειν ἢ μικρὰς τὰς κοτύλας.
ἐγὼ γοῦν ἐν τῇ Ῥώμῃ τὴν τοῦ ἐλαίου καλουμένην λίτραν, ἣν διὰ τῶν κατατετμημένων κεράτων μετροῦσιν, ἔστησά ποτε βουλόμενος μαθεῖν ὁπόσον ἔχει σταθμὸν τοῦ βάρους.
εὗρον δὲ καὶ ταῖς σταθμικαῖς δέκα οὐγγίαις ἴσας τὰς μετρικὰς τοῦ ἐλαίου ιβ΄.
διὸ γράφειν ἐχρῆν ἐπιμελέστερον ἐν ταῖς φαρμακίτισι βίβλοις τοὺς ἰατροὺς, ὁποίας τινὰς κελεύουσι βάλλεσθαι τὰς οὐγγίας ἢ τὰς λίτρας τῶν ὑγρῶν φαρμάκων, πότερα τὰς μετρικὰς ἢ τὰς σταθμικάς.
πρόδηλον γὰρ, ὅτι τῶν ὑγρῶν τούτων σωμάτων, ὥσπερ καὶ τῶν στερεῶν, τὰ μέν ἐστι βαρύτερα, τὰ δὲ κουφότερα.
καὶ λέλεκταί μοι κατὰ λόγον ἕτερον ἑκάστου τῶν εἰς τὰ φάρμακα βαλλομένων ὑγρῶν ὁ σταθμὸς, ἀλλὰ νῦν γε τὸ προκείμενον ἀναλάβωμεν.
τὰς γάρ τοι τρεῖς κοτύλας, εἰ μὲν ἐξ ἐννέα τις οὐγγιῶν μετρικῶν ἑκάστην θείη, τὰς μὲν τρεῖς οὐγγιῶν ἑπτὰ καὶ κ΄.
english_sentences: But I have already heard someone saying that the kotyle written by the physicians in the pharmacological books [894] has sixteen Roman ounces; and it is no small difference with respect to the power of the drug whether one puts in large kotylai or small ones.
I, at any rate, in Rome once weighed the so-called litra of oil, which they measure by means of the graduated horns, wishing to learn how much weight it has by the balance.
And I found that the twelve measure-ounces of oil are equal to ten weight-ounces.

Therefore the physicians ought to write more carefully in the pharmacological books what sort of ounces or litrai of the liquid drugs they order to be put in, whether the measure-ones or the weight-ones.
For it is evident that of these liquid bodies, just as of the solid ones, some are heavier and others lighter.
And the weight of each of the liquids put into drugs has been stated by me in another treatise; but now let us resume the matter before us.
For as to the three kotylai, if one sets each at nine measure-ounces, he will make the three come to twenty-seven ounces.

beads.greek: τεμνομένης [895] δὲ ἑκάστης αὐτῆς εἰς η΄. δραχμὰς, τὰς δραχμὰς ἕξουσι διακοσίας ιστ΄.
beads.english: and when each of these is divided [895] into 8 drachmas, they will have two hundred and sixteen drachmas.

beads.greek: εἰ δὲ ἐκ τῶν ιβ΄. οὐγγιῶν ἑκάστην κοτύλην ὑπάρχειν ὑπόθοιτο, γενήσονται μὲν στ΄.
beads.english: But if one were to suppose that each kotyle consists of 12 ounces, there will be thirty-six ounces, and 288 drachmas, each ounce being divided into 8 drachmas.

beads.greek: δραχμὰς ἑκάστης οὐγγίας. πεπείραμαι δ’ ἐγὼ πολλάκις ἐν ἐλαίῳ λιθάργυρον ἑψηκὼς τὴν μὲν σύμμετρον αὐτῆς μίξιν ἴσην τῇ σταθμικῇ λίτρᾳ τῆς λιθαργύρου, τῇ μετρικῇ δὲ τοῦ ἐλαίου γίγνεσθαι.
beads.english: I myself have found by experience, having often boiled litharge in oil, that the well-proportioned mixture of it comes about when the weight-litra of litharge is set equal to the measure-litra of oil; and that if one puts in more oil, it being of course boiled for a longer time, it becomes more drying.

beads.greek: εἰ δὲ ἐμβάλλοι τις ἔλαιον πλέον, ἑψομένην τε δηλονότι πλείονι χρόνῳ, ξηραντικωτέραν γίγνεσθαι. ἐπὶ δὲ τῶν λευκῶν ἐμπλάστρων διὰ τὸ χρῶμα μίγνυμεν καὶ τὸ ψιμύθιον τῇ λιθαργύρῳ, τοὐπίπαν ἴσον ἴσῃ κατὰ τὸν σταθμόν.
beads.english: In the case of the white plasters, on account of the colour, we mix white lead too with the litharge, for the most part equal to equal by weight.

beads.greek: ἐμβάλλεται δὲ ἡ κοτύλη τῶν θ΄. οὐγγιῶν, ὡς πρὸς τὴν σταθμικὴν λίτραν τῆς λιθαργύρου, βουλομένοις φυλάττειν τὸ χρῶμα, διὰ τὸ τὴν πλείονα ἕψησιν ἐργάσασθαι μελαντέραν τὴν λιθάργυρον, ἀλλ’ ἧττον ἐχέκολλον γίνεται τὸ φάρμακον, ἐλαίου βληθέντος ὀλίγου.
beads.english: And the kotyle of 9 ounces is put in, in relation to the weight-litra of litharge, by those who wish to preserve the colour, because the longer boiling makes the litharge blacker; but the drug becomes less adhesive when only a little oil has been put in.

greek_sentences: τεμνομένης [895] δὲ ἑκάστης αὐτῆς εἰς η΄.
δραχμὰς, τὰς δραχμὰς ἕξουσι διακοσίας ιστ΄.
οὐγγιῶν ἑκάστην κοτύλην ὑπάρχειν ὑπόθοιτο, γενήσονται μὲν στ΄.
πεπείραμαι δ’ ἐγὼ πολλάκις ἐν ἐλαίῳ λιθάργυρον ἑψηκὼς τὴν μὲν σύμμετρον αὐτῆς μίξιν ἴσην τῇ σταθμικῇ λίτρᾳ τῆς λιθαργύρου, τῇ μετρικῇ δὲ τοῦ ἐλαίου γίγνεσθαι.
εἰ δὲ ἐμβάλλοι τις ἔλαιον πλέον, ἑψομένην τε δηλονότι πλείονι χρόνῳ, ξηραντικωτέραν γίγνεσθαι.
ἐπὶ δὲ τῶν λευκῶν ἐμπλάστρων διὰ τὸ χρῶμα μίγνυμεν καὶ τὸ ψιμύθιον τῇ λιθαργύρῳ, τοὐπίπαν ἴσον ἴσῃ κατὰ τὸν σταθμόν.
ἐμβάλλεται δὲ ἡ κοτύλη τῶν θ΄.

οὐγγιῶν, ὡς πρὸς τὴν σταθμικὴν λίτραν τῆς λιθαργύρου, βουλομένοις φυλάττειν τὸ χρῶμα, διὰ τὸ τὴν πλείονα ἕψησιν ἐργάσασθαι μελαντέραν τὴν λιθάργυρον, ἀλλ’ ἧττον ἐχέκολλον γίνεται τὸ φάρμακον, ἐλαίου βληθέντος ὀλίγου.
english_sentences: and when each of these is divided [895] into 8 drachmas, they will have two hundred and sixteen drachmas.
But if one were to suppose that each kotyle consists of 12 ounces, there will be thirty-six ounces, and 288 drachmas, each ounce being divided into 8 drachmas.

I myself have found by experience, having often boiled litharge in oil, that the well-proportioned mixture of it comes about when the weight-litra of litharge is set equal to the measure-litra of oil; and that if one puts in more oil, it being of course boiled for a longer time, it becomes more drying.
In the case of the white plasters, on account of the colour, we mix white lead too with the litharge, for the most part equal to equal by weight.

And the kotyle of 9 ounces is put in, in relation to the weight-litra of litharge, by those who wish to preserve the colour, because the longer boiling makes the litharge blacker; but the drug becomes less adhesive when only a little oil has been put in.

beads.greek: διό τινες ἔμιξαν ἤτοι τὴν τερμινθίνην ῥητίνην ἢ τὴν κολοφωνίαν καλουμένην τὴν διαυγῆ, καθ’ ὅσον οἷόν τε πειρώμενοι μήτε τὴν χρόαν βλάψαι μήτε τὴν δύναμιν τοῦ φαρμάκου, [896] προσθεῖναί τε τῆς ῥητίνης μίξει τὸ δυσαπόπτωτον αὐτῇ, διὰ τὸ ψαθυρὸν γίνεσθαι τὸ φάρμακον, ἂν ἐν ἐλαίῳ τοσούτῳ τοσοῦτον ἕψηται τῆς λιθαργύρου τε καὶ τοῦ ψιμυθίου.
beads.english: For this reason some have mixed in either terebinth resin or the transparent kind called colophony, trying, as far as possible, to harm neither the colour nor the power of the drug, [896] and to add to it, by the admixture of the resin, the property of not easily falling off, because the drug becomes crumbly if so much of the litharge and of the white lead is boiled in so much oil.

beads.greek: τινὲς δὲ κατὰ τὸν αὐτὸν λόγον ἐνέβαλον ἑψημένῳ τῷ φαρμάκῳ τὸν λευκὸν κηρόν.
beads.english: Others, on the same principle, added white wax to the drug once it had been boiled.

beads.greek: τῇ μέντοι διπλάσιον ἐχούσῃ τὸ ἔλαιον λιθαργύρῳ, κᾂν μηδὲν ἐπεμβάλλῃς ῥητινῶδες ἢ κηρῶδες, ὑπάρξει τὸ ἐχέκολλον ἐκ τῆς ἑψήσεως, καὶ πολύ γε μᾶλλον, ἐὰν τριπλάσιον μίξῃς τὸ ἔλαιον τῇ λιθαργύρῳ, τουτέστιν ἐὰν τρεῖς μετρικὰς ἐλαίου μίξεις τρισὶ σταθμικαῖς τῆς λιθαργύρου. εἰκὸς οὖν ἐστι τὸν Ἀνδρόμαχον θ΄.
beads.english: To litharge that has double the quantity of oil, however, even if you add nothing resinous or waxy, the adhesive quality will belong as a result of the boiling, and much more so if you mix in triple the oil to the litharge, that is, if you mix three measure-litrai of oil with three weight-litrai of litharge.

beads.greek: τῶν μετρικῶν οὐγγιῶν ἀξιοῦν ἐμβάλλεσθαι τὸ κίκινον ἔλαιον, ὡς γίγνεσθαι τῶν ἕξ κοτυλῶν οὐγγίας νδ΄. μετρικὰς, ὅπερ ἐστὶ ταὐτὸν λίτρας μετρικαῖς Ῥωμαϊκαῖς δ΄.
beads.english: It is likely, then, that Andromachus wants the castor oil to be put in at nine metric ounces [per kotyle], so that the six kotylai come to fifty-four metric ounces, which is the same as four and a half Roman metric litrai.

beads.greek: καὶ S". εὔδηλον δ’ ὅτι μὴ παρόντος ποτὲ ἡμῖν τοῦ κικίνου τὸ παλαιὸν ἔλαιον ἀντ’ αὐτοῦ παραληψόμεθα.
beads.english: And it is quite clear that, if at some time castor oil is not available to us, we shall take old oil in its place.

greek_sentences: διό τινες ἔμιξαν ἤτοι τὴν τερμινθίνην ῥητίνην ἢ τὴν κολοφωνίαν καλουμένην τὴν διαυγῆ, καθ’ ὅσον οἷόν τε πειρώμενοι μήτε τὴν χρόαν βλάψαι μήτε τὴν δύναμιν τοῦ φαρμάκου, [896] προσθεῖναί τε τῆς ῥητίνης μίξει τὸ δυσαπόπτωτον αὐτῇ, διὰ τὸ ψαθυρὸν γίνεσθαι τὸ φάρμακον, ἂν ἐν ἐλαίῳ τοσούτῳ τοσοῦτον ἕψηται τῆς λιθαργύρου τε καὶ τοῦ ψιμυθίου.
τινὲς δὲ κατὰ τὸν αὐτὸν λόγον ἐνέβαλον ἑψημένῳ τῷ φαρμάκῳ τὸν λευκὸν κηρόν.

τῇ μέντοι διπλάσιον ἐχούσῃ τὸ ἔλαιον λιθαργύρῳ, κᾂν μηδὲν ἐπεμβάλλῃς ῥητινῶδες ἢ κηρῶδες, ὑπάρξει τὸ ἐχέκολλον ἐκ τῆς ἑψήσεως, καὶ πολύ γε μᾶλλον, ἐὰν τριπλάσιον μίξῃς τὸ ἔλαιον τῇ λιθαργύρῳ, τουτέστιν ἐὰν τρεῖς μετρικὰς ἐλαίου μίξεις τρισὶ σταθμικαῖς τῆς λιθαργύρου.
εἰκὸς οὖν ἐστι τὸν Ἀνδρόμαχον θ΄.
τῶν μετρικῶν οὐγγιῶν ἀξιοῦν ἐμβάλλεσθαι τὸ κίκινον ἔλαιον, ὡς γίγνεσθαι τῶν ἕξ κοτυλῶν οὐγγίας νδ΄.
μετρικὰς, ὅπερ ἐστὶ ταὐτὸν λίτρας μετρικαῖς Ῥωμαϊκαῖς δ΄.
εὔδηλον δ’ ὅτι μὴ παρόντος ποτὲ ἡμῖν τοῦ κικίνου τὸ παλαιὸν ἔλαιον ἀντ’ αὐτοῦ παραληψόμεθα.
english_sentences: For this reason some have mixed in either terebinth resin or the transparent kind called colophony, trying, as far as possible, to harm neither the colour nor the power of the drug, [896] and to add to it, by the admixture of the resin, the property of not easily falling off, because the drug becomes crumbly if so much of the litharge and of the white lead is boiled in so much oil.
Others, on the same principle, added white wax to the drug once it had been boiled.

To litharge that has double the quantity of oil, however, even if you add nothing resinous or waxy, the adhesive quality will belong as a result of the boiling, and much more so if you mix in triple the oil to the litharge, that is, if you mix three measure-litrai of oil with three weight-litrai of litharge.

It is likely, then, that Andromachus wants the castor oil to be put in at nine metric ounces [per kotyle], so that the six kotylai come to fifty-four metric ounces, which is the same as four and a half Roman metric litrai.
And it is quite clear that, if at some time castor oil is not available to us, we shall take old oil in its place.

beads.greek: καὶ τὸ σικυώνιον δ’ ἐγὼ πολλάκις ἐνέβαλον εἰς τὰς διαφορητικὰς ἐμπλάστρους, κᾀκείνου μὴ παρόντος, ἕτερον ἔλαιον αὐτοσχεδιάσας, ὅμοιον ἐκείνοις εἰργασάμην, ἐναφεψήσας αὐτῷ ῥίζας σικύου ἀγρίου καὶ βρυωνίου [897] καὶ ἀλθαίας.
beads.english: And I myself have often put Sicyonian oil into the discutient plasters, and when that too was not available, I improvised another oil and made it similar to those, by boiling down in it roots of wild cucumber and bryony [897] and marshmallow.

beads.greek: ὅτι δὲ διαφορητικόν τε καὶ μαλακτικὸν εἶναι βούλεται τὸ προκείμενον φάρμακον ὁ Ἀνδρόμαχος εὔδηλον ἐκ τοῦ κίκινον ἔλαιον ἐμβάλλειν αὐτῷ καὶ πλεῖστον ἀμμωνιακὸν θυμίαμα.
beads.english: That Andromachus wants the drug before us to be both discutient and emollient is quite evident from his putting castor oil into it, and a very large amount of ammoniac incense.

beads.greek: τῇ γὰρ λιθαργύρῳ τὸν μὲν κηρὸν ἴσον εἶναι βούλεται τῷ σταθμῷ, τὸ δ’ ἀμμωνιακὸν S". καίτοι κατὰ πολλὰς τῶν ἐνδόξων ἐμπλάστρων οὐχ ἡμίσεος, ἀλλὰ δ΄.
beads.english: For he wants the wax to be equal to the litharge in weight, and the ammoniac a half; and yet in many of the renowned plasters this drug is put in not at a half, but at a fourth part or a fifth, and often a seventh and an eighth, and sometimes a tenth, by weight, in relation to the litharge.

beads.greek: μέρους ἢ ε΄. καὶ πολλάκις ἑβδόμου τε καὶ ὀγδόου καί ποτε δεκάτου βαλλομένου τοῦ φαρμάκου τούτου κατὰ τὸν σταθμὸν, ὡς πρὸς τὴν λιθάργυρον.
beads.english: Concerning wax we have learned that it holds the rank of material in the compositions of such drugs, not the contribution of an active power.

beads.greek: περὶ δὲ τοῦ κηροῦ μεμαθήκαμεν ὡς ὕλης ἔχει τάξιν ἐν ταῖς τῶν τοιούτων φαρμάκων συνθέσεσιν, οὐ δυνάμεως δραστηρίου συντέλειαν. ὑπάρχει δὲ καὶ αὐτῷ βραχεῖά τις δύναμις μαλακτικὴ, ἀλλ’ οὐ διὰ ταύτην ἐν τῷ προκειμένῳ φαρμάκῳ παρείληπται, καθάπερ οὐδ’ ἡ τερμινθίνη ῥητίνη, καίτοι πολὺ πλαστικωτέρα κατὰ δύναμιν οὖσα τοῦ κηροῦ.
beads.english: It too possesses some slight emollient power, but it has not been taken up into the drug before us on account of this, just as the terebinth resin has not either, although it is far more plastic (πλαστικωτέρα) in power than wax.

beads.greek: καὶ γὰρ μαλάττει μᾶλλον αὐτοῦ καὶ προσέτι θερμαίνει καὶ διαφορεῖ, τοῦ κηροῦ μηδ’ ἕτερον ἔχοντος τούτων.
beads.english: For indeed it softens more than wax does, and in addition it heats and disperses, whereas wax has neither of these.

beads.greek: ἀλλὰ τὸ ἀμμωνιακὸν θυμίαμα μόνον ἐμβληθὲν αὐχμηρὸν ἐργάσεται τὸ φάρμακον.
beads.english: But the ammoniac incense, if put in alone, will make the drug dry and crumbly (αὐχμηρόν).

greek_sentences: καὶ τὸ σικυώνιον δ’ ἐγὼ πολλάκις ἐνέβαλον εἰς τὰς διαφορητικὰς ἐμπλάστρους, κᾀκείνου μὴ παρόντος, ἕτερον ἔλαιον αὐτοσχεδιάσας, ὅμοιον ἐκείνοις εἰργασάμην, ἐναφεψήσας αὐτῷ ῥίζας σικύου ἀγρίου καὶ βρυωνίου [897] καὶ ἀλθαίας.
ὅτι δὲ διαφορητικόν τε καὶ μαλακτικὸν εἶναι βούλεται τὸ προκείμενον φάρμακον ὁ Ἀνδρόμαχος εὔδηλον ἐκ τοῦ κίκινον ἔλαιον ἐμβάλλειν αὐτῷ καὶ πλεῖστον ἀμμωνιακὸν θυμίαμα.
τῇ γὰρ λιθαργύρῳ τὸν μὲν κηρὸν ἴσον εἶναι βούλεται τῷ σταθμῷ, τὸ δ’ ἀμμωνιακὸν S".
καίτοι κατὰ πολλὰς τῶν ἐνδόξων ἐμπλάστρων οὐχ ἡμίσεος, ἀλλὰ δ΄.
καὶ πολλάκις ἑβδόμου τε καὶ ὀγδόου καί ποτε δεκάτου βαλλομένου τοῦ φαρμάκου τούτου κατὰ τὸν σταθμὸν, ὡς πρὸς τὴν λιθάργυρον.
περὶ δὲ τοῦ κηροῦ μεμαθήκαμεν ὡς ὕλης ἔχει τάξιν ἐν ταῖς τῶν τοιούτων φαρμάκων συνθέσεσιν, οὐ δυνάμεως δραστηρίου συντέλειαν.
ὑπάρχει δὲ καὶ αὐτῷ βραχεῖά τις δύναμις μαλακτικὴ, ἀλλ’ οὐ διὰ ταύτην ἐν τῷ προκειμένῳ φαρμάκῳ παρείληπται, καθάπερ οὐδ’ ἡ τερμινθίνη ῥητίνη, καίτοι πολὺ πλαστικωτέρα κατὰ δύναμιν οὖσα τοῦ κηροῦ.
καὶ γὰρ μαλάττει μᾶλλον αὐτοῦ καὶ προσέτι θερμαίνει καὶ διαφορεῖ, τοῦ κηροῦ μηδ’ ἕτερον ἔχοντος τούτων.
ἀλλὰ τὸ ἀμμωνιακὸν θυμίαμα μόνον ἐμβληθὲν αὐχμηρὸν ἐργάσεται τὸ φάρμακον.
english_sentences: And I myself have often put Sicyonian oil into the discutient plasters, and when that too was not available, I improvised another oil and made it similar to those, by boiling down in it roots of wild cucumber and bryony [897] and marshmallow.
That Andromachus wants the drug before us to be both discutient and emollient is quite evident from his putting castor oil into it, and a very large amount of ammoniac incense.

For he wants the wax to be equal to the litharge in weight, and the ammoniac a half; and yet in many of the renowned plasters this drug is put in not at a half, but at a fourth part or a fifth, and often a seventh and an eighth, and sometimes a tenth, by weight, in relation to the litharge.
Concerning wax we have learned that it holds the rank of material in the compositions of such drugs, not the contribution of an active power.

It too possesses some slight emollient power, but it has not been taken up into the drug before us on account of this, just as the terebinth resin has not either, although it is far more plastic (πλαστικωτέρα) in power than wax.
For indeed it softens more than wax does, and in addition it heats and disperses, whereas wax has neither of these.
But the ammoniac incense, if put in alone, will make the drug dry and crumbly (αὐχμηρόν).

beads.greek: ὡς δ’ εἰς [898] ἐμπλαστροποιΐαν, οὐδὲ γὰρ χεῖρον οὕτως ὀνομάσαι, χρήσιμός ἐστιν ὅ τε κηρὸς καὶ ἡ ῥητίνη.
beads.english: But for [898] plaster-making—for it is no worse to name it thus—both the wax and the resin are useful.

beads.greek: τὸ γάρ τοι μαλάττειν τε καὶ διαφορεῖν ὑπάρχει τῷ φαρ μάκῳ κᾀκ μόνου τοῦ ἀμμωνιακοῦ πρωτεύοντος μὲν ἐν τοῖς μαλακτικοῖς, ἐναμίλλου δὲ καὶ τοῖς διαφορητικοῖς ὄντος.
beads.english: For in fact softening and dispersing belong to the drug even from the ammoniac alone, which holds the first place among emollients and is a rival also to the discutients.

beads.greek: ἀναμνησθέντες δὲ τῶν ἐν τῷ ε΄. τῆς τῶν ἁπλῶν φαρμάκων δυνάμεως εἰρημένων, ὁποίαν τινὰ τὴν κρᾶσιν εἶναι χρὴ τοῖς τοιούτοις φαρμάκοις, οὐδὲν ἔτι δεηθήσεσθε νεωτέρας διδασκαλίας.
beads.english: And if you recall what was said in the fifth book of On the Powers of Simple Drugs, as to what sort of mixture such drugs must have, you will have no further need of fresh instruction.

beads.greek: αἱ μὲν γὰρ πρῶται δυνάμεις δραστικαὶ τοῖς φαρμάκοις εἰσὶν ἐν θερμότητι καὶ ψυχρότητι καὶ ὑγρότητι καὶ ξηρότητι· δεύτεραι δὲ αἵ τε μαλακτικαὶ καὶ διαφορητικαὶ καὶ ἀποκρουστικαὶ καὶ ἑλκτικαὶ καὶ πεπτικαί τε καὶ ῥυπτικαὶ καὶ σηπτικαὶ, καθάπερ γε καὶ τρίται κολλητικαὶ τραυμάτων, ἐπουλωτικαί τε καὶ σαρκωτικαί.
beads.english: For the primary active powers of drugs lie in heat and cold and moisture and dryness; the secondary are the emollient, the discutient, the repellent, the attractive, the concocting, the detergent and the septic, just as the tertiary are those agglutinative of wounds, the cicatrizing and the flesh-producing.

beads.greek: καὶ τὸ συγκείμενον οὖν ἐξ ἐλαίου κικίνου καὶ ἀμμωνιακοῦ θυμιάματος φάρμακον ἱκανόν ἐστι διαφορεῖν τε καὶ μαλάττειν καὶ δηλονότι καὶ ξηραίνειν, ὕλην ἐπιτηδείαν προσειληφὸς τὸν κηρόν τε καὶ τὴν ῥητίνην καὶ τὴν ἐπὶ τὸ πλέον ἑψημένην λιθάργυρον.
beads.english: And so the drug compounded from castor oil and ammoniac incense is sufficient to disperse and to soften and, evidently, also to dry, having taken on as suitable material the wax and the resin and the litharge that has been boiled for a longer time.

greek_sentences: ὡς δ’ εἰς [898] ἐμπλαστροποιΐαν, οὐδὲ γὰρ χεῖρον οὕτως ὀνομάσαι, χρήσιμός ἐστιν ὅ τε κηρὸς καὶ ἡ ῥητίνη.
τὸ γάρ τοι μαλάττειν τε καὶ διαφορεῖν ὑπάρχει τῷ φαρ μάκῳ κᾀκ μόνου τοῦ ἀμμωνιακοῦ πρωτεύοντος μὲν ἐν τοῖς μαλακτικοῖς, ἐναμίλλου δὲ καὶ τοῖς διαφορητικοῖς ὄντος.
ἀναμνησθέντες δὲ τῶν ἐν τῷ ε΄.
τῆς τῶν ἁπλῶν φαρμάκων δυνάμεως εἰρημένων, ὁποίαν τινὰ τὴν κρᾶσιν εἶναι χρὴ τοῖς τοιούτοις φαρμάκοις, οὐδὲν ἔτι δεηθήσεσθε νεωτέρας διδασκαλίας.

αἱ μὲν γὰρ πρῶται δυνάμεις δραστικαὶ τοῖς φαρμάκοις εἰσὶν ἐν θερμότητι καὶ ψυχρότητι καὶ ὑγρότητι καὶ ξηρότητι· δεύτεραι δὲ αἵ τε μαλακτικαὶ καὶ διαφορητικαὶ καὶ ἀποκρουστικαὶ καὶ ἑλκτικαὶ καὶ πεπτικαί τε καὶ ῥυπτικαὶ καὶ σηπτικαὶ, καθάπερ γε καὶ τρίται κολλητικαὶ τραυμάτων, ἐπουλωτικαί τε καὶ σαρκωτικαί.

καὶ τὸ συγκείμενον οὖν ἐξ ἐλαίου κικίνου καὶ ἀμμωνιακοῦ θυμιάματος φάρμακον ἱκανόν ἐστι διαφορεῖν τε καὶ μαλάττειν καὶ δηλονότι καὶ ξηραίνειν, ὕλην ἐπιτηδείαν προσειληφὸς τὸν κηρόν τε καὶ τὴν ῥητίνην καὶ τὴν ἐπὶ τὸ πλέον ἑψημένην λιθάργυρον.
english_sentences: But for [898] plaster-making—for it is no worse to name it thus—both the wax and the resin are useful.
For in fact softening and dispersing belong to the drug even from the ammoniac alone, which holds the first place among emollients and is a rival also to the discutients.
And if you recall what was said in the fifth book of On the Powers of Simple Drugs, as to what sort of mixture such drugs must have, you will have no further need of fresh instruction.

For the primary active powers of drugs lie in heat and cold and moisture and dryness; the secondary are the emollient, the discutient, the repellent, the attractive, the concocting, the detergent and the septic, just as the tertiary are those agglutinative of wounds, the cicatrizing and the flesh-producing.

And so the drug compounded from castor oil and ammoniac incense is sufficient to disperse and to soften and, evidently, also to dry, having taken on as suitable material the wax and the resin and the litharge that has been boiled for a longer time.

beads.greek: ἐπεμβάλλειν δ’ αὐτῷ κελεύει ﻿ [899] καὶ τῶν κεκαυμένων ἐρίων καὶ ἀριστολοχίας, διαφορητικωτάτων τε καὶ ξηραντικωτάτων φαρμάκων, ἐφ’ οἷς πεπτικοῦ καὶ παρηγορικοῦ φαρμάκου μνημονεύει τοῦ λιβανωτοῦ.
beads.english: And he orders that there be added to it [899] also some burnt wool and aristolochia, drugs that are most discutient and most desiccative; after these he mentions a concocting and soothing drug, frankincense.

beads.greek: εἰ δὲ καὶ τῆς σμύρνης ἐμβάλλοιμέν τι καὶ ὀποπάνακος, ἐνίους γάρ φησι καὶ τούτων τι μιγνύναι τῷ φαρμάκῳ, τὴν μὲν σμύρναν ἴσμεν οὐκ ἀγεννῶς θερμαίνουσάν τε καὶ ξηραίνουσαν, τὸν δὲ ὀποπάνακα καὶ γενναιότερον ἔτι ταῦτ’ ἄμφω δρῶντα καὶ προσέτι λεπτυντικῆς τε καὶ διαφορητικῆς ὄντα δυνάμεως.
beads.english: And if we should also put in some myrrh and opopanax—for he says that some people mix some of these too into the drug—we know that myrrh heats and dries in no ignoble fashion, while opopanax does both of these even more vigorously and is moreover of an attenuating and discutient faculty.

beads.greek: ἀλλὰ τούτου μὲν ὀλίγιστον ἐμβάλλεται, δεδιότος οἶμαι τοῦ προσθέντος αὐτὸ τὴν δριμύτητα τοῦ φαρμάκου καὶ βουλομένου μὴ μόνον διαφορητικήν τε καὶ μαλακτικὴν ἐργάσασθαι τὴν ἔμπλαστρον, ἀλλὰ καὶ τραύμασιν ἐπιτηδείαν.
beads.english: But of this only a very little is put in, since, I think, the one who added it feared the acridity of the drug and wished to make the plaster not only discutient and emollient but also suitable for wounds.

beads.greek: διὰ τοῦτο οὖν αὐτῷ καὶ τὴν λεπίδα τοῦ χαλκοῦ τε καὶ τοῦ στομώματος ἔμιξε, φάρμακα στυπτικὴν ἔχοντα δύναμιν ἅμα τῷ ξηραίνειν ἰσχυρῶς.
beads.english: For this reason, then, he also mixed into it the scale of copper and of steel (στομώματος), drugs that have an astringent faculty together with drying strongly.

beads.greek: διὰ γοῦν τὴν τούτων μίξιν ἐπί τε τῶν ἐναίμων τραυμάτων ἄλλων θ’ ἑλκῶν οὐκ ὀλίγων ἀγαθὸν γίγνεται φάρμακον ἡ προκειμένη κατὰ λόγον ἔμπλαστρος Αἰγυπτία.
beads.english: At any rate, on account of the admixture of these, the Egyptian plaster under discussion becomes a good drug for bleeding wounds and for not a few other ulcers.

greek_sentences: ἐπεμβάλλειν δ’ αὐτῷ κελεύει ﻿ [899] καὶ τῶν κεκαυμένων ἐρίων καὶ ἀριστολοχίας, διαφορητικωτάτων τε καὶ ξηραντικωτάτων φαρμάκων, ἐφ’ οἷς πεπτικοῦ καὶ παρηγορικοῦ φαρμάκου μνημονεύει τοῦ λιβανωτοῦ.

εἰ δὲ καὶ τῆς σμύρνης ἐμβάλλοιμέν τι καὶ ὀποπάνακος, ἐνίους γάρ φησι καὶ τούτων τι μιγνύναι τῷ φαρμάκῳ, τὴν μὲν σμύρναν ἴσμεν οὐκ ἀγεννῶς θερμαίνουσάν τε καὶ ξηραίνουσαν, τὸν δὲ ὀποπάνακα καὶ γενναιότερον ἔτι ταῦτ’ ἄμφω δρῶντα καὶ προσέτι λεπτυντικῆς τε καὶ διαφορητικῆς ὄντα δυνάμεως.

ἀλλὰ τούτου μὲν ὀλίγιστον ἐμβάλλεται, δεδιότος οἶμαι τοῦ προσθέντος αὐτὸ τὴν δριμύτητα τοῦ φαρμάκου καὶ βουλομένου μὴ μόνον διαφορητικήν τε καὶ μαλακτικὴν ἐργάσασθαι τὴν ἔμπλαστρον, ἀλλὰ καὶ τραύμασιν ἐπιτηδείαν.
διὰ τοῦτο οὖν αὐτῷ καὶ τὴν λεπίδα τοῦ χαλκοῦ τε καὶ τοῦ στομώματος ἔμιξε, φάρμακα στυπτικὴν ἔχοντα δύναμιν ἅμα τῷ ξηραίνειν ἰσχυρῶς.
διὰ γοῦν τὴν τούτων μίξιν ἐπί τε τῶν ἐναίμων τραυμάτων ἄλλων θ’ ἑλκῶν οὐκ ὀλίγων ἀγαθὸν γίγνεται φάρμακον ἡ προκειμένη κατὰ λόγον ἔμπλαστρος Αἰγυπτία.
english_sentences: And he orders that there be added to it [899] also some burnt wool and aristolochia, drugs that are most discutient and most desiccative; after these he mentions a concocting and soothing drug, frankincense.

And if we should also put in some myrrh and opopanax—for he says that some people mix some of these too into the drug—we know that myrrh heats and dries in no ignoble fashion, while opopanax does both of these even more vigorously and is moreover of an attenuating and discutient faculty.

But of this only a very little is put in, since, I think, the one who added it feared the acridity of the drug and wished to make the plaster not only discutient and emollient but also suitable for wounds.
For this reason, then, he also mixed into it the scale of copper and of steel (στομώματος), drugs that have an astringent faculty together with drying strongly.
At any rate, on account of the admixture of these, the Egyptian plaster under discussion becomes a good drug for bleeding wounds and for not a few other ulcers.

beads.greek: καὶ μέντοι καὶ πρὸς ἀποστήματα καὶ πάνθ’ [900] ὅσα διαφορεῖσθαι δεῖται, πολλάκις ἀκηκόατε τὰ μὲν ἅμα τοῖς διαφορητικοῖς φαρμάκοις ἔχοντά τι καὶ τῶν στυπτικῶν ἀσφαλέστερα γίγνεσθαι, τὰ δὲ χωρὶς τῶν στυφόντων δραστικώτερα μὲν, οὐκ ἀσφαλῆ δέ.
beads.english: And indeed also for abscesses and for all [900] such things as need to be dispersed, you have often heard that those remedies which, together with the discutient drugs, contain also something of the astringents become safer, whereas those without the astringent ingredients are more effective, but not safe.

beads.greek: πολλάκις γὰρ ἐπισπᾶται ῥεύματα πληθωρικοῦ τοῦ θεραπευομένου σώματος ὄντος ἢ κακοχύμου.
beads.english: For often such a remedy draws fluxes, when the body being treated is plethoric or full of bad humours.

beads.greek: κενὸν δ’ εἴπερ εἴη τὸ σῶμα καὶ ἀπέριττον, ἑτοιμότερον ἀφικνεῖται τοῦ τέλους τὰ διαφορητικώτερα φάρμακα μόνα παραλαμβανόμενα χωρὶς τῶν στυπτικῶν.
beads.english: But if the body is empty and free of superfluity, the more discutient drugs, taken by themselves without the astringents, reach their goal more readily.

beads.greek: ὀλίγοις δὲ προσφερόμενα ἐπὶ τοιούτοις σώμασι τὰ φάρμακα διὰ τοῦτο ἀσφαλέστερον ἔδοξεν εἶναι μιγνύναι τι καὶ τῶν ἀποκρουστικῶν.
beads.english: Since, however, the drugs are applied to such bodies only in few cases, for this reason it has seemed safer to mix in also something of the repellents.

beads.greek: οὕτω τοι καὶ τῇ διὰ τῶν ἁλῶν ἐμπλάστρῳ διαφορητικῇ προσέθεσάν τινες χαλκάνθου βραχὺ, καίτοι καὶ τῶν ἁλῶν αὐτῶν ἐχόντων τι στυπτικόν.
beads.english: Thus indeed some have added a little chalcanthum to the discutient plaster made with salts, although the salts themselves also have something astringent.

greek_sentences: καὶ μέντοι καὶ πρὸς ἀποστήματα καὶ πάνθ’ [900] ὅσα διαφορεῖσθαι δεῖται, πολλάκις ἀκηκόατε τὰ μὲν ἅμα τοῖς διαφορητικοῖς φαρμάκοις ἔχοντά τι καὶ τῶν στυπτικῶν ἀσφαλέστερα γίγνεσθαι, τὰ δὲ χωρὶς τῶν στυφόντων δραστικώτερα μὲν, οὐκ ἀσφαλῆ δέ.
πολλάκις γὰρ ἐπισπᾶται ῥεύματα πληθωρικοῦ τοῦ θεραπευομένου σώματος ὄντος ἢ κακοχύμου.
κενὸν δ’ εἴπερ εἴη τὸ σῶμα καὶ ἀπέριττον, ἑτοιμότερον ἀφικνεῖται τοῦ τέλους τὰ διαφορητικώτερα φάρμακα μόνα παραλαμβανόμενα χωρὶς τῶν στυπτικῶν.
ὀλίγοις δὲ προσφερόμενα ἐπὶ τοιούτοις σώμασι τὰ φάρμακα διὰ τοῦτο ἀσφαλέστερον ἔδοξεν εἶναι μιγνύναι τι καὶ τῶν ἀποκρουστικῶν.
οὕτω τοι καὶ τῇ διὰ τῶν ἁλῶν ἐμπλάστρῳ διαφορητικῇ προσέθεσάν τινες χαλκάνθου βραχὺ, καίτοι καὶ τῶν ἁλῶν αὐτῶν ἐχόντων τι στυπτικόν.
english_sentences: And indeed also for abscesses and for all [900] such things as need to be dispersed, you have often heard that those remedies which, together with the discutient drugs, contain also something of the astringents become safer, whereas those without the astringent ingredients are more effective, but not safe.
For often such a remedy draws fluxes, when the body being treated is plethoric or full of bad humours.
But if the body is empty and free of superfluity, the more discutient drugs, taken by themselves without the astringents, reach their goal more readily.
Since, however, the drugs are applied to such bodies only in few cases, for this reason it has seemed safer to mix in also something of the repellents.
Thus indeed some have added a little chalcanthum to the discutient plaster made with salts, although the salts themselves also have something astringent.

beads.greek: τὸ τοίνυν προκείμενον φάρμακον εὕρηται μὲν διαφορητικὸν ἰσχυρῶς, ὡς καὶ πῦον ἤδη τό γε μὴ πάνυ πολὺ, χωρὶς τοῦ διατρῆσαι τὸ δέρμα, διαφορεῖν δύνασθαι, μαλακτικὸν δὲ τῶν σκιῤῥουμένων τε καὶ ὁπωσοῦν σκληρυνομένων, κολλητικὸν δὲ μεγάλων τραυμάτων, ὥσπερ γε καὶ τῶν ἤδη κακοηθευομένων ἑλκῶν ἐπουλωτικὸν [901] ἁπάντων τε τῶν ἄλλων παθημάτων, ὅσα διαφορητικῆς τε ἅμα καὶ ἀποκρουστικῆς μετρεῖται δυνάμεως, ἐν οἷς ἐστι καὶ τὰ κατὰ τοῦ μετώπου ῥευματιζομένων ὀφθαλμῶν ἐπιτιθέμενα, καλούμενα δὲ ὑπὸ τῶν ἰατρῶν ἀνακολλήματα.
beads.english: The drug under discussion, then, has been found to be strongly discutient, so that it is able to disperse even pus already present—at least when it is not very abundant—without perforating the skin; emollient for parts that are becoming scirrhous or hardened in any way whatever; agglutinative of large wounds, just as it is also cicatrizing of ulcers that are already becoming malignant, [901] and of all the other affections that are apportioned (μετρεῖται) a power at once discutient and repellent, among which are also the things applied to the forehead for eyes affected by flux, which are called by physicians anakollēmata.

beads.greek: ταὐτὸν δὲ τοῦτο τὸ φάρμακον ἐπιτήδειον ἔσται καὶ τοῖς γεγυμνωμένοις νεύροις, εἰ καὶ τετμημένα κατά τι μέρος αὐτῶν τύχοι.
beads.english: This same drug will also be suitable for nerves that have been laid bare, even if they happen to have been cut in some part of them.

beads.greek: τὰ γάρ τοι διακεκομμένα τὸν ἐκ τῆς συμπαθείας οὐκ ἔχοντα κίν δυνον ἔτι καὶ τὴν αἴσθησιν ἀφαιρεῖται τῶν ὑποκειμένων ἑαυτῷ σωμάτων, εἰς ἃ κατίσχεται.
beads.english: For those that have been cut through, no longer having the danger that arises from sympathy, also take away the sensation of the bodies lying beneath it (ἑαυτῷ), into which it is held down (κατίσχεται).

beads.greek: δεῖταί γε μὴν καὶ ταῦτα τοιούτου φαρμάκου.
beads.english: Yet these too require such a drug.

beads.greek: τὰ γὰρ ὑγραίνοντα σήπει ῥᾳδίως αὐτὰ, διὰ τοῦτο καὶ οἱ ξηραντικοὶ κυκλίσκοι, καίτοι στύφοντες ἱκανῶς, ὅμως ἁρμόττουσι τοῖς γεγυμνωμένος νεύροις, ἅ γε μήπω φθάσαντα πρὸς τὴν ἀκμὴν τῆς φλεγμονῆς ἀφίκετο.
beads.english: For moistening agents easily putrefy them; for this reason the drying small disks too, although they are considerably astringent, are nevertheless suitable for nerves that have been laid bare—those, at least, which have not yet already arrived at the peak of inflammation.

beads.greek: ταῦτα γὰρ ἀγανακτεῖ καὶ παροξύνεται πρὸς τῶν τοιούτων φαρμάκων.
beads.english: For these are irritated and exacerbated by such drugs.

beads.greek: ἀλλὰ περὶ μὲν τούτων ἐπὶ προήκοντι τῷ λόγῳ ῥηθήσεται· περὶ δὲ τῆς προκειμένης ἐμπλάστρου τὰ λείποντα τῷ λόγῳ προσθῶμεν.
beads.english: But these matters will be spoken of as the discussion proceeds; concerning the plaster under discussion, let us add what is lacking to the account.

greek_sentences: τὸ τοίνυν προκείμενον φάρμακον εὕρηται μὲν διαφορητικὸν ἰσχυρῶς, ὡς καὶ πῦον ἤδη τό γε μὴ πάνυ πολὺ, χωρὶς τοῦ διατρῆσαι τὸ δέρμα, διαφορεῖν δύνασθαι, μαλακτικὸν δὲ τῶν σκιῤῥουμένων τε καὶ ὁπωσοῦν σκληρυνομένων, κολλητικὸν δὲ μεγάλων τραυμάτων, ὥσπερ γε καὶ τῶν ἤδη κακοηθευομένων ἑλκῶν ἐπουλωτικὸν [901] ἁπάντων τε τῶν ἄλλων παθημάτων, ὅσα διαφορητικῆς τε ἅμα καὶ ἀποκρουστικῆς μετρεῖται δυνάμεως, ἐν οἷς ἐστι καὶ τὰ κατὰ τοῦ μετώπου ῥευματιζομένων ὀφθαλμῶν ἐπιτιθέμενα, καλούμενα δὲ ὑπὸ τῶν ἰατρῶν ἀνακολλήματα.
ταὐτὸν δὲ τοῦτο τὸ φάρμακον ἐπιτήδειον ἔσται καὶ τοῖς γεγυμνωμένοις νεύροις, εἰ καὶ τετμημένα κατά τι μέρος αὐτῶν τύχοι.
τὰ γάρ τοι διακεκομμένα τὸν ἐκ τῆς συμπαθείας οὐκ ἔχοντα κίν δυνον ἔτι καὶ τὴν αἴσθησιν ἀφαιρεῖται τῶν ὑποκειμένων ἑαυτῷ σωμάτων, εἰς ἃ κατίσχεται.
δεῖταί γε μὴν καὶ ταῦτα τοιούτου φαρμάκου.

τὰ γὰρ ὑγραίνοντα σήπει ῥᾳδίως αὐτὰ, διὰ τοῦτο καὶ οἱ ξηραντικοὶ κυκλίσκοι, καίτοι στύφοντες ἱκανῶς, ὅμως ἁρμόττουσι τοῖς γεγυμνωμένος νεύροις, ἅ γε μήπω φθάσαντα πρὸς τὴν ἀκμὴν τῆς φλεγμονῆς ἀφίκετο.
ταῦτα γὰρ ἀγανακτεῖ καὶ παροξύνεται πρὸς τῶν τοιούτων φαρμάκων.
ἀλλὰ περὶ μὲν τούτων ἐπὶ προήκοντι τῷ λόγῳ ῥηθήσεται· περὶ δὲ τῆς προκειμένης ἐμπλάστρου τὰ λείποντα τῷ λόγῳ προσθῶμεν.
english_sentences: The drug under discussion, then, has been found to be strongly discutient, so that it is able to disperse even pus already present—at least when it is not very abundant—without perforating the skin; emollient for parts that are becoming scirrhous or hardened in any way whatever; agglutinative of large wounds, just as it is also cicatrizing of ulcers that are already becoming malignant, [901] and of all the other affections that are apportioned (μετρεῖται) a power at once discutient and repellent, among which are also the things applied to the forehead for eyes affected by flux, which are called by physicians anakollēmata.
This same drug will also be suitable for nerves that have been laid bare, even if they happen to have been cut in some part of them.

For those that have been cut through, no longer having the danger that arises from sympathy, also take away the sensation of the bodies lying beneath it (ἑαυτῷ), into which it is held down (κατίσχεται).
Yet these too require such a drug.

For moistening agents easily putrefy them; for this reason the drying small disks too, although they are considerably astringent, are nevertheless suitable for nerves that have been laid bare—those, at least, which have not yet already arrived at the peak of inflammation.
For these are irritated and exacerbated by such drugs.
But these matters will be spoken of as the discussion proceeds; concerning the plaster under discussion, let us add what is lacking to the account.

beads.greek: ἐπεὶ δὲ οἱ πολλοὶ τῶν ἰατρῶν ἀγνοοῦντες ἐπιτιθέασι τὰς τοιαύτας· ἐμπλάστρους σκληρὰς, ἄμεινον ἐμμότους ποιῆσαι τήξαντας [902] ἢ κατὰ τὴν σκευασίαν εὐθὺς ἐργάσασθαι μαλθακάς.
beads.english: But since most physicians, out of ignorance, apply such plasters in a hard state, it is better to make them into lint-dressings (ἐμμότους) by melting them, [902] or to work them soft straightaway in the course of preparation.

beads.greek: ἔπειτα δὲ ὅταν ἐπὶ μεγάλων διαιρέσεων, ἐν αἷς γεγύμνωται νεῦρα, πειραθῶσιν αὐτῶν, ἐλπίζουσιν ἐπὶ τῶν νυγμάτων ἔσεσθαι πολὺ μᾶλλον ὠφελίμους, ἀγνοοῦντες κᾀνταῦθα μέγιστόν τι θεώρημα, περὶ οὗ διελέχθην ἤδη διδάσκων ὑμᾶς ἐν τῷ λόγῳ μὲν πρῶτον ἐξεῦρον, εἶθ’ ὑπὸ τῆς πείρας ἔγνων βεβαιούμενα, διὰ τοῦτο καὶ νῦν ἀναμιμνήσκω.
beads.english: Then, when they have made trial of them on large divisions in which nerves have been laid bare, they expect that they will be much more beneficial in the case of punctures, being ignorant here too of a most important theorem, concerning which I have already discoursed when teaching you — things which I first discovered by reasoning and then recognised as confirmed by experience; for this reason I remind you of it now as well.

beads.greek: πολὺ γὰρ θερμοτέρων τε καὶ διαφορητικωτέρων δέονται φαρμάκων αἱ νύξεις τῶν νεύρων ἤπερ ὅταν ὅλον γυμνωθῇ, τραύματος ἀξιολόγου γενομένου.
beads.english: For punctures of nerves require drugs that are much hotter and more discutient than when a whole nerve has been laid bare, a considerable wound having occurred.

beads.greek: τὰ γάρ τοι γυμνωθέντα τὰς τῶν δριμέων τε καὶ θερμῶν πάνυ φαρμάκων ἐπιθέσεις οὐ φέρει διὰ τὴν δῆξιν, ἀλλὰ τῶν χαλαστικῶν καὶ διαφορητικῶν δεῖται μεμιγμένων συμμέτρως τοῖς στύφουσι φαρμάκοις.
beads.english: For those that have been laid bare do not tolerate the application of acrid and very hot drugs, because of the bitingness, but they need relaxing and discutient ones mixed in due proportion with the astringent drugs.

beads.greek: ἀλλὰ καὶ ὅτι βέλτιόν ἐστι τὰ πέριξ τοῦ τραύματος καταλαμβάνειν τοῖς δριμέσι τε καὶ λεπτομερέσι καὶ διαφορητικοῖς ἱκανῶς, ὁποῖόν ἐστι τὸ διὰ τοῦ εὐφορβίου.
beads.english: But also that it is better to take hold of the parts around the wound with drugs that are acrid, fine-particled and sufficiently discutient, such as the one made with euphorbium.

beads.greek: ἐγὼ μὲν οὖν ἐτεκμηράμην τὴν προκειμένην ἔμπλαστρον ἱκανὴν εἶναι ποιεῖν ἃ προείρηκα, καὶ σκευάσας ταύτην εὗρον τὴν πεῖραν μαρτυροῦσαν.
beads.english: I, then, inferred that the plaster under discussion was capable of doing what I have said before, and having prepared it I found experience bearing witness.

πολὺ γὰρ θερμοτέρων τε καὶ διαφορητικωτέρων δέονται φαρμάκων αἱ νύξεις τῶν νεύρων ἤπερ ὅταν ὅλον γυμνωθῇ, τραύματος ἀξιολόγου γενομένου.
τὰ γάρ τοι γυμνωθέντα τὰς τῶν δριμέων τε καὶ θερμῶν πάνυ φαρμάκων ἐπιθέσεις οὐ φέρει διὰ τὴν δῆξιν, ἀλλὰ τῶν χαλαστικῶν καὶ διαφορητικῶν δεῖται μεμιγμένων συμμέτρως τοῖς στύφουσι φαρμάκοις.
ἀλλὰ καὶ ὅτι βέλτιόν ἐστι τὰ πέριξ τοῦ τραύματος καταλαμβάνειν τοῖς δριμέσι τε καὶ λεπτομερέσι καὶ διαφορητικοῖς ἱκανῶς, ὁποῖόν ἐστι τὸ διὰ τοῦ εὐφορβίου.
ἐγὼ μὲν οὖν ἐτεκμηράμην τὴν προκειμένην ἔμπλαστρον ἱκανὴν εἶναι ποιεῖν ἃ προείρηκα, καὶ σκευάσας ταύτην εὗρον τὴν πεῖραν μαρτυροῦσαν.
english_sentences: But since most physicians, out of ignorance, apply such plasters in a hard state, it is better to make them into lint-dressings (ἐμμότους) by melting them, [902] or to work them soft straightaway in the course of preparation.

Then, when they have made trial of them on large divisions in which nerves have been laid bare, they expect that they will be much more beneficial in the case of punctures, being ignorant here too of a most important theorem, concerning which I have already discoursed when teaching you — things which I first discovered by reasoning and then recognised as confirmed by experience; for this reason I remind you of it now as well.
For punctures of nerves require drugs that are much hotter and more discutient than when a whole nerve has been laid bare, a considerable wound having occurred.

For those that have been laid bare do not tolerate the application of acrid and very hot drugs, because of the bitingness, but they need relaxing and discutient ones mixed in due proportion with the astringent drugs.
But also that it is better to take hold of the parts around the wound with drugs that are acrid, fine-particled and sufficiently discutient, such as the one made with euphorbium.
I, then, inferred that the plaster under discussion was capable of doing what I have said before, and having prepared it I found experience bearing witness.

beads.greek: ὕστερον [903] δέ ποτε καὶ ταῖς Ἀσκληπιάδου τε καὶ Κρίτωνος ἐντυγχάνων φαρμακίτισι βίβλοις ἔγνων αὐτοὺς γεγραφότας, οὐχ ὥσπερ καὶ Ἀνδρόμαχος ἀδιορίστως, ἀλλὰ μετὰ διορισμῶν σαφῶς ἥν τινα δύναμιν ἔχει. διά τε οὖν τοῦτο καὶ διότι διαφωνοῦσιν ἐν τῇ σκευασίᾳ, κατά τινα τῷ Ἀνδρομάχῳ, κάλλιον ἔδοξέ μοι προσγράψαι καὶ τὰς ἐκείνων αὐτῶν λέξεις, ἔπειθ’ οὕτως εἰπεῖν τι καὶ περὶ τῆς ἐν τῇ συνθέσει τοῦ φαρμάκου διαφωνίας αὐτῶν.
beads.english: But later [903] at some point, when I also came upon the pharmacological books of Asclepiades and Criton, I learned that they had written, not indefinitely as Andromachus too had done, but with distinctions, clearly, what power it has.

beads.greek: [Περὶ τῶν γεγραμμένων ὑπ’ Ἀσκληπιάδου καὶ Κρίτωνος περὶ τῆς προκειμένης ἐμπλάστρου.] Περὶ τῆς ὑπ’ Ἀνδρομάχου γεγραμμένης Αἰγυπτίας ἐμπλάστρου ὁ Ἀσκληπιάδης οὕτως ἔγραψεν. Ἀνδρομάχου Αἰγυπτία ἄναιμος, τραυματική.
beads.english: Both for this reason, then, and because they disagree in certain points with Andromachus regarding the preparation, it seemed better to me to append the very words of those authors as well, and then in this way to say something also about their disagreement regarding the composition of the drug.

beads.greek: ποιεῖ πρὸς νεύρων καὶ μυῶν διακοπὰς, ποιεῖ πρὸς νύγματα, περιθλάσεις, παρατρίματα, λυγίσματα. ἔστι δὲ καὶ ὀφθαλμιώντων παρακόλλημα.
beads.english: [On what has been written by Asclepiades and Criton about the plaster under discussion.] Concerning the Egyptian plaster written down by Andromachus, Asclepiades wrote as follows.

beads.greek: ποιεῖ κεφαλαλγικοῖς καὶ πρὸς πολλὰς διαθέσεις χρήσιμόν ἐστι τὸ φάρμακον.
beads.english: Andromachus' Egyptian, bloodless, wound-plaster.
It is effective for severings of nerves and muscles; it is effective for punctures, contusions, chafings, sprains.
It is also an adhesive application for those suffering from ophthalmia.
It works for those suffering from headache, and the drug is useful for many conditions. ♃ Of litharge, of wax, 144 drachms each; of ammoniac incense, 72 drachms; of terebinth resin, 36 drachms.

greek_sentences: ὕστερον [903] δέ ποτε καὶ ταῖς Ἀσκληπιάδου τε καὶ Κρίτωνος ἐντυγχάνων φαρμακίτισι βίβλοις ἔγνων αὐτοὺς γεγραφότας, οὐχ ὥσπερ καὶ Ἀνδρόμαχος ἀδιορίστως, ἀλλὰ μετὰ διορισμῶν σαφῶς ἥν τινα δύναμιν ἔχει.

διά τε οὖν τοῦτο καὶ διότι διαφωνοῦσιν ἐν τῇ σκευασίᾳ, κατά τινα τῷ Ἀνδρομάχῳ, κάλλιον ἔδοξέ μοι προσγράψαι καὶ τὰς ἐκείνων αὐτῶν λέξεις, ἔπειθ’ οὕτως εἰπεῖν τι καὶ περὶ τῆς ἐν τῇ συνθέσει τοῦ φαρμάκου διαφωνίας αὐτῶν.
[Περὶ τῶν γεγραμμένων ὑπ’ Ἀσκληπιάδου καὶ Κρίτωνος περὶ τῆς προκειμένης ἐμπλάστρου.] Περὶ τῆς ὑπ’ Ἀνδρομάχου γεγραμμένης Αἰγυπτίας ἐμπλάστρου ὁ Ἀσκληπιάδης οὕτως ἔγραψεν.

ποιεῖ κεφαλαλγικοῖς καὶ πρὸς πολλὰς διαθέσεις χρήσιμόν ἐστι τὸ φάρμακον.
english_sentences: But later [903] at some point, when I also came upon the pharmacological books of Asclepiades and Criton, I learned that they had written, not indefinitely as Andromachus too had done, but with distinctions, clearly, what power it has.

Both for this reason, then, and because they disagree in certain points with Andromachus regarding the preparation, it seemed better to me to append the very words of those authors as well, and then in this way to say something also about their disagreement regarding the composition of the drug.
[On what has been written by Asclepiades and Criton about the plaster under discussion.] Concerning the Egyptian plaster written down by Andromachus, Asclepiades wrote as follows.
Andromachus' Egyptian, bloodless, wound-plaster.
It is effective for severings of nerves and muscles; it is effective for punctures, contusions, chafings, sprains.
It is also an adhesive application for those suffering from ophthalmia.
It works for those suffering from headache, and the drug is useful for many conditions. ♃ Of litharge, of wax, 144 drachms each; of ammoniac incense, 72 drachms; of terebinth resin, 36 drachms.

beads.english: of greasy, oesypum-laden wool, burnt, [904] 18 drachmas; of scale of copper, 8 drachmas; of scale of steel (stomōma), 8 drachmas; of frankincense, 8 drachmas; of round aristolochia, 8 drachmas; of castor-oil (kiki), 3 cotylae.

Having first stated these things, Asclepiades next writes the manner of the boiling—Andromachus not having preserved even this part of the composition in the case of the plasters, for it has been omitted in almost all of them.

beads.greek: γ΄. ταῦτα προειπὼν ὁ Ἀσκληπιάδης ἐφεξῆς γράφει τὸν τρόπον τῆς ἑψήσεως, οὐδὲ τοῦτο τὸ μέρος τῆς συνθέσεως ἐπὶ τῶν ἐμπλάστρων φυλάξαντος τοῦ Ἀνδρομάχου, παραλέλειπται γὰρ ἐν ἁπάσαις σχεδόν.
beads.english: But concerning the boilings not a little has been said in the fourth book, and it will also be spoken of now, a little further on.

beads.greek: ἀλλὰ περὶ μὲν τῶν ἑψήσεων εἴρηται μὲν οὐκ ὀλίγα κατὰ τὸ δ΄. γράμμα καὶ νῦν εἰρήσεται μετ’ ὀλίγον.
beads.english: It is worth examining the matter of the disagreement which Asclepiades made with Andromachus in the quantity of the simple drugs.

beads.greek: ἄξιον δὲ ἐπισκέψασθαι τὸ τῆς διαφωνίας, ἣν ἐν τῇ ποσότητι τῶν ἁπλῶν φαρμάκων ἐποιήσατο πρὸς τὸν Ἀνδρόμαχον ὁ Ἀσκληπιάδης.

οὐ γὰρ ἓξ κοτύλας τοῦ κίκεως, ὥσπερ ὁ Ἀνδρόμαχος, ἀλλὰ τρεῖς ἐμβάλλειν ἀξιοῖ, κατὰ δὲ τὴν ἀριστολοχίαν οὐδὲν προδιορισαμένου τοῦ Ἀνδρομάχου, προσέθηκεν αὐτὸς τὸ στρογγύλην, ὥσπερ γε καὶ κατὰ τὸ κεκαυμένον ἔριον τὸ οἰσυπηρόν. τὸν μέντοι σταθμὸν ἴσον ἐμβάλλει τῷ Ἀνδρομάχῳ.
beads.english: For he thinks it right to put in not six cotylae of the castor-oil, as Andromachus does, but three; and in the case of the aristolochia, Andromachus having made no prior specification, he himself added 'round', just as also in the case of the burnt greasy wool.

beads.greek: γράφει γοῦν οὕτως. ♃ ἐρίων οἰσυπηρῶν κεκαυμένων δραχ.
beads.english: The weight, however, he puts in equal to that of Andromachus.
At any rate he writes thus: ♃ of greasy wool, burnt, 18 drachmas; of round aristolochia, 8 drachmas.

τὸν μέντοι σταθμὸν ἴσον ἐμβάλλει τῷ Ἀνδρομάχῳ.
