beads.greek: πάντα βαλὼν εἰς [819] ἄγγος χαλκοῦν ἕψε ἐπὶ τέφρας μαλακῆς, κινῶν ἕως ἂν ἀποσταζόμενον εἰς ὕδωρ ψυχρὸν πάχος ἔχῃ μέλιτος. μετὰ δὲ ταῦτα αἶρε κινῶν, τοῦτο ἐγχρίσας εἰς δερμάτιον, ἐπιτίθει καὶ λῦε χειμῶνος μὲν μετὰ τὴν ἑβδόμην ἡμέραν, θέρους δὲ μετὰ τὴν πέμπτην.
beads.english: Putting everything into [819] a bronze vessel, boil it over soft ashes, stirring, until a drop let fall into cold water has the thickness of honey.

beads.greek: [Ἄλλη, ἐκ τῶν Φιλοξένου.] ♃ Λιβάνου, σμύρνης, κρόκου, Ἰλλυρικῆς, βδελλίου, λεπίδος χαλκοῦ, χαλκάνθου, χαλκίτεως, στυπτηρίας στρογγύλης καὶ σχιστῆς, μίσυος ξενικοῦ, ἀμμωνιακοῦ θυμιάματος, προπόλεως, ἰξοῦ δρυΐνου, ὀποπάνακος, σιδίων μεμυκότων ἀνὰ δραχ. δ΄.
beads.english: After this, take it off while stirring; spread it on a small piece of leather, apply it, and undo it in winter after the seventh day, in summer after the fifth.

beads.greek: ἀριστολοχίας δραχμὰς η΄. κηροῦ, στέατος ταυρείου ἀνὰ δραχμὰς ρ΄.
beads.english: [Another, from the writings of Philoxenus.] ℞ Frankincense, myrrh, saffron, Illyrian [iris], bdellium, flake of copper, chalcanthum, chalcitis, round and split alum, foreign misy, ammoniac incense, propolis, oak birdlime, opopanax, closed pomegranate rinds, 4 dr. each; birthwort 8 dr.; wax, bull's suet, 100 dr. each, which he writes down as a mina; terebinth resin 15 dr., which he writes down as three quarters.

beads.greek: ἃ μνᾶν ἐπιγράφει. ῥητίνης τερμινθίνης δραχ.
beads.english: Putting the resin into an earthenware casserole, boil it until it becomes odourless; then grate the suet and the wax, add them and melt them.

beads.greek: ιε΄. ὃ τρία τέταρτα ἐπιγράφει, τὴν ῥητίνην βαλὼν εἰς λοπάδα ὀστρακίνην, ἕψε ἕως ἄνοσμα γένηται, εἶτα τὸ στέαρ καὶ τὸν κηρὸν κατακνήσας, ἐπέμβαλε καὶ τῆκε.
beads.english: Pound the dry ingredients and sift them through a very fine sieve; then, taking the meltable ingredients off the fire and letting them cool somewhat, sprinkle the dry ingredients over them and stir carefully.

beads.greek: τὰ δὲ ξηρὰ κόπτε καὶ σῆθε λεπτοτάτῳ κοσκίνῳ, ἔπειτα καθελὼν ἀπὸ τοῦ πυρὸς τὰ τηκτὰ καὶ ποσῶς ἐάσας ψυγῆναι τούτων κατάπασσε τὰ ξηρὰ καὶ κίνει ἐπιμελῶς.

greek_sentences: πάντα βαλὼν εἰς [819] ἄγγος χαλκοῦν ἕψε ἐπὶ τέφρας μαλακῆς, κινῶν ἕως ἂν ἀποσταζόμενον εἰς ὕδωρ ψυχρὸν πάχος ἔχῃ μέλιτος.
μετὰ δὲ ταῦτα αἶρε κινῶν, τοῦτο ἐγχρίσας εἰς δερμάτιον, ἐπιτίθει καὶ λῦε χειμῶνος μὲν μετὰ τὴν ἑβδόμην ἡμέραν, θέρους δὲ μετὰ τὴν πέμπτην.

[Ἄλλη, ἐκ τῶν Φιλοξένου.] ♃ Λιβάνου, σμύρνης, κρόκου, Ἰλλυρικῆς, βδελλίου, λεπίδος χαλκοῦ, χαλκάνθου, χαλκίτεως, στυπτηρίας στρογγύλης καὶ σχιστῆς, μίσυος ξενικοῦ, ἀμμωνιακοῦ θυμιάματος, προπόλεως, ἰξοῦ δρυΐνου, ὀποπάνακος, σιδίων μεμυκότων ἀνὰ δραχ.
κηροῦ, στέατος ταυρείου ἀνὰ δραχμὰς ρ΄.
ὃ τρία τέταρτα ἐπιγράφει, τὴν ῥητίνην βαλὼν εἰς λοπάδα ὀστρακίνην, ἕψε ἕως ἄνοσμα γένηται, εἶτα τὸ στέαρ καὶ τὸν κηρὸν κατακνήσας, ἐπέμβαλε καὶ τῆκε.
τὰ δὲ ξηρὰ κόπτε καὶ σῆθε λεπτοτάτῳ κοσκίνῳ, ἔπειτα καθελὼν ἀπὸ τοῦ πυρὸς τὰ τηκτὰ καὶ ποσῶς ἐάσας ψυγῆναι τούτων κατάπασσε τὰ ξηρὰ καὶ κίνει ἐπιμελῶς.
english_sentences: Putting everything into [819] a bronze vessel, boil it over soft ashes, stirring, until a drop let fall into cold water has the thickness of honey.
After this, take it off while stirring; spread it on a small piece of leather, apply it, and undo it in winter after the seventh day, in summer after the fifth.

[Another, from the writings of Philoxenus.] ℞ Frankincense, myrrh, saffron, Illyrian [iris], bdellium, flake of copper, chalcanthum, chalcitis, round and split alum, foreign misy, ammoniac incense, propolis, oak birdlime, opopanax, closed pomegranate rinds, 4 dr. each; birthwort 8 dr.; wax, bull's suet, 100 dr. each, which he writes down as a mina; terebinth resin 15 dr., which he writes down as three quarters.
Putting the resin into an earthenware casserole, boil it until it becomes odourless; then grate the suet and the wax, add them and melt them.

Pound the dry ingredients and sift them through a very fine sieve; then, taking the meltable ingredients off the fire and letting them cool somewhat, sprinkle the dry ingredients over them and stir carefully.

beads.greek: ἔχειν δὲ δεῖ μετ’ ὄξους τετριμμένα σμύρναν, λίβανον, [820] βδέλλιον, ὀποπάνακα.
τούτοις ἐπίβαλλε τὰ ἐν τῇ λοπάδι καὶ τρῖβε ὥστε ἐγκηρίδας μὴ γενέσθαι. ὅταν δὲ καλῶς ἔχῃ, ἀνελοῦ εἰς πυξίδα ξυλίνην, προσεγχρίσας ἰρίνῳ μύρῳ.
beads.english: You must have ready myrrh, frankincense, [820] bdellium and opopanax ground with vinegar.

beads.greek: [Ἡ διὰ δυοῖν ἀριστολοχιῶν, ὡς Ἀνδρόμαχος.] Περὶ ταύτης ὁ Ἀνδρόμαχος κατὰ λέξιν οὕτως γράφει. ἡ διὰ δυοῖν ἀριστολοχιῶν.
beads.english: Onto these put the contents of the earthenware pan, and grind so that no wax-lumps (enkērides) form.

beads.greek: ♃ ῥητίνης φρυκτῆς λίτραν α΄. κηροῦ λίτραν α΄.
beads.english: When it is in good condition, take it up into a wooden box, having first smeared the box with iris unguent.

beads.greek: πίσσης λίτραν α΄. κίκεως ἢ ἐλαίου παλαιοῦ κοτύλην μίαν, κυάθους δύο, ψιμυθίου οὐγγίας στ΄.
beads.english: [The plaster made with the two birthworts, as Andromachus gives it.] Concerning this plaster Andromachus writes word for word as follows: The plaster made with the two birthworts. ℞ Roasted resin, 1 litra; wax, 1 litra; pitch, 1 litra; kiki oil or old olive oil, one kotyle, two kyathoi; white lead, 6 ounces; verdigris, 6 ounces; chalcanthum, 4 ounces; manna, 6 ounces; long birthwort, 4 ounces, and round birthwort, 4 ounces;

beads.greek: ἰοῦ οὐγγίας στ΄. χαλκάνθου οὐγγίας δ΄.
beads.english: Eretrian earth, 6 ounces;

beads.greek: ἀριστολοχίας μακρᾶς οὐγγίας δ΄. καὶ στρογγύλης οὐγγίας δ΄.
beads.english: Illyrian iris, 4 ounces; oak-gall, 2 ounces; vinegar, 1 kotyle (I use more); pomegranate rinds, 2 ounces.

beads.greek: ὄξους κοτύλην α΄. ἐγὼ πλέον, σιδίων οὐγγίας β΄.
beads.english: Grind the dry ingredients smooth with the vinegar, then add the meltable ingredients.

beads.greek: λείου σὺν ὄξει τὰ ξηρὰ, εἶτα τὰ τηκτά. [Ἡ διὰ δικτάμνου ὡς Δαμοκράτης.] Εἴρηταί μοι πολλάκις ὡς οὐ μόνον εἰς μνήμην αἱ ἔμμετροι γραφαὶ χρησιμώτεροι τῶν πεζῇ γεγραμμένων εἰσὶν, ἀλλὰ καὶ εἰς τὴν τῆς συμμετρίας τῶν μιγνυμένων ἀκρίβειαν.
beads.english: [The plaster made with dittany, as Damocrates gives it.] I have often said that recipes written in verse are more useful than those written in prose not only for memory but also for exactness in the proportion of the ingredients mixed.

Onto these put the contents of the earthenware pan, and grind so that no wax-lumps (enkērides) form.
When it is in good condition, take it up into a wooden box, having first smeared the box with iris unguent.

Illyrian iris, 4 ounces; oak-gall, 2 ounces; vinegar, 1 kotyle (I use more); pomegranate rinds, 2 ounces.
Grind the dry ingredients smooth with the vinegar, then add the meltable ingredients.

beads.greek: διὰ τοῦτ’ [821] οὖν καὶ νῦν τὴν διὰ δικτάμνου προσέγραψε συμμετρίαν ἀκριβῆ διασώζουσαν ἐν τῇ Δαμοκράτου γραφῇ.
beads.english: For this reason, then, he has now also appended [821] the [plaster] made with dittany, which keeps its exact proportion in Damocrates' text.

beads.greek: Τῶν περιβοήτων δ’ ἐστὶν ἐμπλάστρων μία, Μόνη τ’ ἔχουσα Κρητικὸν τὸ καλούμενον Δίκταμνον, ἰᾶται δὲ τὰς τῶν ἑρπετῶν, Ἰοβόλων πληγάς τε καὶ τὰ δήγματα Πάντων τετραπόδων, κᾂν λελυσσήκῃ τινὰ, Τετυλωμένα θ’ ἕλκη, τάς τε τῶν νεύρων φθοράς.
beads.english: 'It is one of the celebrated plasters, and the only one that contains the so-called Cretan dittany. It heals the strikes of venomous reptiles and the bites of all quadrupeds, even if some of them have been rabid, and callused ulcers, and the corruptions of nerves, of muscles and of the cartilages that lie upon bones, when these already have corruption in depth.

beads.greek: Μυῶν τε καὶ τῶν ὀστέοις ἐπικειμένων Χόνδρων, ἐχόντων διὰ βάθους ἤδη φθοράν. Τά τε περὶ μαστοὺς καὶ τράχηλον καὶ ῥάχιν Ἕλκη θεραπεύει, κᾂν χρόνους πολλοὺς ἔχῃ· Καὶ πάνθ’ ὅς’ εἶπον τὴν καλουμένην ποιεῖν Αἰγυπτίαν ἔμπλαστρον ἔμπροσθεν βραχύ.
beads.english: It treats ulcers about the breasts, the neck and the spine, even if they are of long standing, and everything that I said a little earlier the plaster called the Egyptian does.

beads.greek: Ταύτην ἀγαθὴν σφόδρ’ οὖσαν ἔνιοι καὶ μόνην Δοκοῦσι πασῶν τῶν καλῶν βελτίονα, Πολλῶν διὰ πείρας οὐκ ἔχοντες φαρμάκων.
beads.english: Since it is very good, some think it the only one better than all the good ones, because they have no experience of many drugs.'

greek_sentences: διὰ τοῦτ’ [821] οὖν καὶ νῦν τὴν διὰ δικτάμνου προσέγραψε συμμετρίαν ἀκριβῆ διασώζουσαν ἐν τῇ Δαμοκράτου γραφῇ.

Τῶν περιβοήτων δ’ ἐστὶν ἐμπλάστρων μία, Μόνη τ’ ἔχουσα Κρητικὸν τὸ καλούμενον Δίκταμνον, ἰᾶται δὲ τὰς τῶν ἑρπετῶν, Ἰοβόλων πληγάς τε καὶ τὰ δήγματα Πάντων τετραπόδων, κᾂν λελυσσήκῃ τινὰ, Τετυλωμένα θ’ ἕλκη, τάς τε τῶν νεύρων φθοράς.
Μυῶν τε καὶ τῶν ὀστέοις ἐπικειμένων Χόνδρων, ἐχόντων διὰ βάθους ἤδη φθοράν.
Τά τε περὶ μαστοὺς καὶ τράχηλον καὶ ῥάχιν Ἕλκη θεραπεύει, κᾂν χρόνους πολλοὺς ἔχῃ· Καὶ πάνθ’ ὅς’ εἶπον τὴν καλουμένην ποιεῖν Αἰγυπτίαν ἔμπλαστρον ἔμπροσθεν βραχύ.
Ταύτην ἀγαθὴν σφόδρ’ οὖσαν ἔνιοι καὶ μόνην Δοκοῦσι πασῶν τῶν καλῶν βελτίονα, Πολλῶν διὰ πείρας οὐκ ἔχοντες φαρμάκων.
english_sentences: For this reason, then, he has now also appended [821] the [plaster] made with dittany, which keeps its exact proportion in Damocrates' text.
'It is one of the celebrated plasters, and the only one that contains the so-called Cretan dittany.

It heals the strikes of venomous reptiles and the bites of all quadrupeds, even if some of them have been rabid, and callused ulcers, and the corruptions of nerves, of muscles and of the cartilages that lie upon bones, when these already have corruption in depth.
It treats ulcers about the breasts, the neck and the spine, even if they are of long standing, and everything that I said a little earlier the plaster called the Egyptian does.
Since it is very good, some think it the only one better than all the good ones, because they have no experience of many drugs.'

beads.greek: Ἔχει δὲ λιθάργυρον δὶς ἑκατὸν δραχμὰς, [822] Λίτρας δ’ ἐλαίου τοῦ παλαιοῦ τέταρτον. Τινὲς δὲ κοτύλης φασὶ μᾶλλον τέταρτον.
beads.english: It contains litharge, twice a hundred drachmas, [822] and of old oil a fourth of a litra; but some say rather a fourth of a kotyle.

beads.greek: Δὶς δ’ εἴκοσι πέντε Ποντικοῦ κηροῦ δραχμὰς, Κολοφωνίας δὲ τῆς καλῆς, κηροῦ διπλοῦν, Τινὲς δὲ μᾶλλον, ταὐτὸ τῆς τερμινθίνης.
Ἰοῦ δὲ χαλκοῦ καὶ ἀλόης Ἰνδικῆς, Χαλκοῦ τε κεκαυμένου καὶ διφρυγοῦς καλοῦ Ἑκκαίδεχ’ ἥμισυ ἐξ ἑκάστου μίγματος, Εἴκοσι δραχμὰς δὲ χαλβάνης καὶ δ΄. Μάννης, λιβάνου τε τὰς ἴσας δὶς ιβ΄.
beads.english: Twice twenty-five drachmas of Pontic wax, and of fine Colophonian resin double the wax, but some say rather the same quantity of terebinth.

beads.greek: Ἑκκαίδεκα δραχμὰς προπόλεως τῆς Ἀττικῆς, Ἀριστολοχίας τῆς μακρᾶς δὶς ι΄. δραχμὰς Δὶς στ΄.
beads.english: Of verdigris and of Indian aloe, of burnt copper and of fine diphryges, sixteen and a half of each ingredient of the mixture; twenty drachmas and 4 of galbanum; of manna and of frankincense equal amounts, twice 12; of ammoniac twice 5 and twice 20; sixteen drachmas of Attic propolis; of long birthwort twice 10 drachmas; twice 6 drachmas of scale of Cyprian copper, and an equal amount of very dry gentian root.

beads.greek: λεπίδος, τοῦ Κυπρίου χαλκοῦ δραχμὰς Καὶ γεντιανῆς ξηροτάτης ῥίζης ἴσον.
Τούτοις προσαπόδος πᾶσι δικτάμνου πόας Ξηρᾶς ἐχούσης ἄνθος ὁλκὰς κ΄. Λείας.
beads.english: To all these add further, of the herb dittany, dry and bearing its flower, 20 holkai, ground smooth.

greek_sentences: Ἔχει δὲ λιθάργυρον δὶς ἑκατὸν δραχμὰς, [822] Λίτρας δ’ ἐλαίου τοῦ παλαιοῦ τέταρτον.
Τινὲς δὲ κοτύλης φασὶ μᾶλλον τέταρτον.
Δὶς δ’ εἴκοσι πέντε Ποντικοῦ κηροῦ δραχμὰς, Κολοφωνίας δὲ τῆς καλῆς, κηροῦ διπλοῦν, Τινὲς δὲ μᾶλλον, ταὐτὸ τῆς τερμινθίνης.

Μάννης, λιβάνου τε τὰς ἴσας δὶς ιβ΄.

Τούτοις προσαπόδος πᾶσι δικτάμνου πόας Ξηρᾶς ἐχούσης ἄνθος ὁλκὰς κ΄.
english_sentences: It contains litharge, twice a hundred drachmas, [822] and of old oil a fourth of a litra; but some say rather a fourth of a kotyle.
Twice twenty-five drachmas of Pontic wax, and of fine Colophonian resin double the wax, but some say rather the same quantity of terebinth.

Of verdigris and of Indian aloe, of burnt copper and of fine diphryges, sixteen and a half of each ingredient of the mixture; twenty drachmas and 4 of galbanum; of manna and of frankincense equal amounts, twice 12; of ammoniac twice 5 and twice 20; sixteen drachmas of Attic propolis; of long birthwort twice 10 drachmas; twice 6 drachmas of scale of Cyprian copper, and an equal amount of very dry gentian root.
To all these add further, of the herb dittany, dry and bearing its flower, 20 holkai, ground smooth.

beads.greek: λιθάργυρον δὲ μετ’ ἐλαίου βαλὼν, [823] Εἰς λοπάδα καινὴν κεραμίαν πλατύστομον, Ἕψε πυρὶ κούφῳ καὶ μαλακῷ, κινῶν σπάθῃ Ἕως γένηται μέλιτος Ἀττικοῦ πάχος.
beads.english: Putting the litharge with the oil [823] into a new, wide-mouthed earthenware dish, boil it over a light and gentle fire, stirring with a spatula, until it takes on the thickness of Attic honey.

beads.greek: Ἴσον δὲ καὶ τῆς λεπίδος προσβαλὼν πάλιν Ἕψε λαβρότερον, εἶτα κιῤῥοῦ γενομένου Τοῦ φαρμάκου, πρόσβαλε χαλκὸν καὶ διφρυγὲς, Ποιῶν τ’ ἀμόλυντον καὶ πεπηγὸς φάρμακον Πρόσβαλλε κηρὸν τήν τε ῥητίνην ἅμα.
beads.english: Then add an equal amount of the scale as well and boil again more vigorously; next, when the drug has become tawny, add the copper and the diphryges, and, to make the drug non-staining and set, add the wax and the resin together. When these have melted together and you see that the plaster is blended, take the pot off the fire, and add some propolis and the galbanum, ammoniac, manna and aloe.

beads.greek: Ὧν συντακέντων, ὅταν ἴδῃς κεκραμένην Ἔμπλαστρον, αἴρεις τὴν χύτραν ἀπὸ τοῦ πυρὸς Καὶ προσβαλὼν προπόλεώς τε καὶ χαλβάνην, Ἀμμωνιακὸν, μάνναν τε καὶ ἀλόην, τότε Ψύξας τὸ πυρῶδες καὶ ζέον τοῦ φαρμάκου, Ἀριστολοχίαν λειοτάτην προσεμπάσεις Καὶ γεντιανὴν, τήν τε δίκταμνον πόαν Καὶ προσανακόψας τῇ σπάθῃ τὸ φάρμακον Χερσὶ καὶ μαγδαλιὰς ποιῶν, ἔχε, Εἰς ἃς προεῖπον χρώμενος περιστάσεις.
beads.english: Then, having cooled the fiery and seething heat of the drug, sprinkle in the aristolochia ground very smooth, and the gentian and the dittany herb. Beat the drug up further with the spatula, make it into rolls with your hands, and keep it, using it for the conditions I mentioned before.

Ὧν συντακέντων, ὅταν ἴδῃς κεκραμένην Ἔμπλαστρον, αἴρεις τὴν χύτραν ἀπὸ τοῦ πυρὸς Καὶ προσβαλὼν προπόλεώς τε καὶ χαλβάνην, Ἀμμωνιακὸν, μάνναν τε καὶ ἀλόην, τότε Ψύξας τὸ πυρῶδες καὶ ζέον τοῦ φαρμάκου, Ἀριστολοχίαν λειοτάτην προσεμπάσεις Καὶ γεντιανὴν, τήν τε δίκταμνον πόαν Καὶ προσανακόψας τῇ σπάθῃ τὸ φάρμακον Χερσὶ καὶ μαγδαλιὰς ποιῶν, ἔχε, Εἰς ἃς προεῖπον χρώμενος περιστάσεις.
english_sentences: Putting the litharge with the oil [823] into a new, wide-mouthed earthenware dish, boil it over a light and gentle fire, stirring with a spatula, until it takes on the thickness of Attic honey.

Then add an equal amount of the scale as well and boil again more vigorously; next, when the drug has become tawny, add the copper and the diphryges, and, to make the drug non-staining and set, add the wax and the resin together.
When these have melted together and you see that the plaster is blended, take the pot off the fire, and add some propolis and the galbanum, ammoniac, manna and aloe.
Then, having cooled the fiery and seething heat of the drug, sprinkle in the aristolochia ground very smooth, and the gentian and the dittany herb.
Beat the drug up further with the spatula, make it into rolls with your hands, and keep it, using it for the conditions I mentioned before.

beads.greek: [824] [Περὶ τροχίσκων Ἀσκληπιάδου.] Ὥσπερ δ’ ἐμπλάστρους ἀπὸ τῆς χρόας, ἀλλ’ οὐκ ἀπὸ τῆς κατὰ δύναμιν ἐπαγγελίας, ὠνόμασαν ἔνιοι τῶν ἰατρῶν μηλίνας καὶ λευκὰς καὶ φαιὰς καὶ κιῤῥὰς, οὕτως ἀπὸ τοῦ κατὰ τὴν ἀνάπλασιν σχήματος ὀνομάζουσι τροχίσκους οὐ πρὸς ἓν πάθος, ἀλλὰ πρὸς πάνυ πολλὰ διαφέροντας.
beads.english: [824] [On the troches of Asclepiades.] Just as some of the physicians named plasters from their colour, and not from what they promise to do by their power, calling them quince-yellow, white, grey and tawny, so they name troches (trochiskoi) from the shape given them in the moulding, although these differ from one another and are not for one affection but for a great many.

beads.greek: ἀκολουθήσαντες οὖν αὐτοῖς καὶ ἡμεῖς ἐφεξῆς γράψομεν πάντας· τούς γε δοκίμους, εἴτε κυκλίσκους, εἴτε τροχίσκους, ἑκατέρως γὰρ αὐτοὺς ὀνομάζουσι.
beads.english: Following them, then, we too shall write all of them in order, at least the approved ones, whether they are called little discs (kykliskoi) or troches (trochiskoi), for they name them in both ways.

beads.greek: καλῶς δὲ ποιοῦντες ἐφ’ ἑκάστου τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν προέγραψαν, καὶ μάλιστα ὁ Ἀσκληπιάδης, οὗ καὶ πρώτου τὰ κατὰ τὸ τρίτον πρὸς τὰ ἐκτὸς γεγραμμένα φάρμακα παραθήσομαι.
beads.english: And they did well to write the promise above each one, especially Asclepiades, whose drugs written in the third book of his work on external [affections] I shall set out first.

greek_sentences: [824] [Περὶ τροχίσκων Ἀσκληπιάδου.] Ὥσπερ δ’ ἐμπλάστρους ἀπὸ τῆς χρόας, ἀλλ’ οὐκ ἀπὸ τῆς κατὰ δύναμιν ἐπαγγελίας, ὠνόμασαν ἔνιοι τῶν ἰατρῶν μηλίνας καὶ λευκὰς καὶ φαιὰς καὶ κιῤῥὰς, οὕτως ἀπὸ τοῦ κατὰ τὴν ἀνάπλασιν σχήματος ὀνομάζουσι τροχίσκους οὐ πρὸς ἓν πάθος, ἀλλὰ πρὸς πάνυ πολλὰ διαφέροντας.
ἀκολουθήσαντες οὖν αὐτοῖς καὶ ἡμεῖς ἐφεξῆς γράψομεν πάντας· τούς γε δοκίμους, εἴτε κυκλίσκους, εἴτε τροχίσκους, ἑκατέρως γὰρ αὐτοὺς ὀνομάζουσι.
καλῶς δὲ ποιοῦντες ἐφ’ ἑκάστου τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν προέγραψαν, καὶ μάλιστα ὁ Ἀσκληπιάδης, οὗ καὶ πρώτου τὰ κατὰ τὸ τρίτον πρὸς τὰ ἐκτὸς γεγραμμένα φάρμακα παραθήσομαι.
english_sentences: [824] [On the troches of Asclepiades.] Just as some of the physicians named plasters from their colour, and not from what they promise to do by their power, calling them quince-yellow, white, grey and tawny, so they name troches (trochiskoi) from the shape given them in the moulding, although these differ from one another and are not for one affection but for a great many.
Following them, then, we too shall write all of them in order, at least the approved ones, whether they are called little discs (kykliskoi) or troches (trochiskoi), for they name them in both ways.
And they did well to write the promise above each one, especially Asclepiades, whose drugs written in the third book of his work on external [affections] I shall set out first.

Take up with sweet wine; anoint continually.

beads.greek: ♃ ψιμυθίου δραχμὰς στ΄. μάννης, λιβάνου ἀνὰ δραχμὴν α΄.

Take up with sweet wine.
For fissures and condylomata.

beads.greek: πρὸς ῥαγάδας καὶ κονδυλώματα. Μενεσθέως πρὸς τὰς ἐν δακτυλίῳ ῥαγάδας, ποιεῖ πρὸς νομάς.

beads.greek: τῶν ἐκτὸς, ἃ Μαρκέλλας ἐπιγράφει.] Ὁ μὲν Ἀνδρόμαχος [844] ἀνέμιξε τὰ κατὰ πάθος ἁρμόττοντα ξηρὰ τοῖς κατὰ τὰ πεπονθότα.
beads.english: of the External [Remedies], which he entitles 'Marcellas'.] Andromachus [844] mixed together the dry [drugs] suited to an affection with those suited to the affected parts.

beads.greek: διωρισμένως δ’ ὑπ’ Ἀσκληπιάδου γέγραπται κατὰ τὸ ε΄. ἰδίαις μὲν προγραφαῖς δηλούμενα τὰ κατὰ πάθος, ἰδίαις δὲ καὶ τὰ μετὰ τόπου πεπονθότος.
beads.english: But in Asclepiades they have been written separately, in the fifth [book]: those for an affection are marked by headings of their own, and those that go with an affected place likewise by headings of their own.

beads.greek: ἄνευ μὲν γὰρ τόπου γέγραπται πρὸς αὐτοῦ τὰ ἐπουλωτικὰ καὶ τὰ ἐσχαρωτικὰ καὶ τὰ πρὸς νομὰς ἁρμόττοντα καὶ ἄνθρακας καὶ τὰ καλούμενα ἴσχαιμα.
beads.english: Without reference to place he has written the cicatrizing and the escharotic [drugs], those suited to spreading ulcers and carbuncles, and the so-called haemostatics.

beads.greek: μετὰ τόπου δὲ πεπονθότος, ὅσα πρὸς πολύποδα καὶ ὀζαίνας καὶ τὰς ἐκ μυκτήρων αἱμοῤῥαγίας καὶ τὰς ἐν στόματι νομὰς καὶ οὖλα πλαδῶντα καὶ τὰς ἐπὶ τῶν γενείων ὀχθώδεις ἐπαναστάσεις καὶ πρὸς παρωνυχίας καὶ πτερύγια καὶ πρὸς τὰς ἐν δακτυλίῳ ῥαγάδας καὶ πρὸς τὰς αἱμοῤῥοΐδας.
beads.english: With reference to an affected place, he has written those for polyp, ozaenae, haemorrhages from the nostrils, spreading ulcers in the mouth, sodden gums, the lumpy swellings on the chin, and those for paronychias, pterygia, fissures in the anus, and haemorrhoids.

beads.greek: ἔνια δὲ καὶ τὴν ὁμωνυμίαν ἔσχηκεν ἀπὸ τοῦ πεπονθότος.
beads.english: Some have also acquired their name from the affected part.

beads.greek: ἁρμόττει δὲ καὶ τοῖς ἄλλοις μέρεσιν, ὁποῖα καὶ τὰ κεφαλικὰ καλούμενα πρὸς τῶν ἰατρῶν ἐστιν, ἁρμόττοντα μὲν ἐξαιρέτως ἐν τοῖς ὀστοῖς, δυνάμενα δὲ καὶ τὰς ἐν ὅλῳ τῷ σώματι γιγνομένας ἑλκώσεις σαρκοῦν.
beads.english: Yet they suit other parts too. Such are the [drugs] called cephalic by the physicians: they are suited especially to the bones, but they are also able to incarn ulcerations arising in the whole body.

beads.greek: ἐπὶ γὰρ τῆς κεφαλῆς οὐχ ὡς κεφαλῆς ἁρμόττειν μάλιστα πέφυκεν.
beads.english: For it is not as the head that they are by nature particularly suited to the head.

greek_sentences: τῶν ἐκτὸς, ἃ Μαρκέλλας ἐπιγράφει.] Ὁ μὲν Ἀνδρόμαχος [844] ἀνέμιξε τὰ κατὰ πάθος ἁρμόττοντα ξηρὰ τοῖς κατὰ τὰ πεπονθότα.
διωρισμένως δ’ ὑπ’ Ἀσκληπιάδου γέγραπται κατὰ τὸ ε΄.
ἰδίαις μὲν προγραφαῖς δηλούμενα τὰ κατὰ πάθος, ἰδίαις δὲ καὶ τὰ μετὰ τόπου πεπονθότος.
ἄνευ μὲν γὰρ τόπου γέγραπται πρὸς αὐτοῦ τὰ ἐπουλωτικὰ καὶ τὰ ἐσχαρωτικὰ καὶ τὰ πρὸς νομὰς ἁρμόττοντα καὶ ἄνθρακας καὶ τὰ καλούμενα ἴσχαιμα.

μετὰ τόπου δὲ πεπονθότος, ὅσα πρὸς πολύποδα καὶ ὀζαίνας καὶ τὰς ἐκ μυκτήρων αἱμοῤῥαγίας καὶ τὰς ἐν στόματι νομὰς καὶ οὖλα πλαδῶντα καὶ τὰς ἐπὶ τῶν γενείων ὀχθώδεις ἐπαναστάσεις καὶ πρὸς παρωνυχίας καὶ πτερύγια καὶ πρὸς τὰς ἐν δακτυλίῳ ῥαγάδας καὶ πρὸς τὰς αἱμοῤῥοΐδας.
ἔνια δὲ καὶ τὴν ὁμωνυμίαν ἔσχηκεν ἀπὸ τοῦ πεπονθότος.
ἁρμόττει δὲ καὶ τοῖς ἄλλοις μέρεσιν, ὁποῖα καὶ τὰ κεφαλικὰ καλούμενα πρὸς τῶν ἰατρῶν ἐστιν, ἁρμόττοντα μὲν ἐξαιρέτως ἐν τοῖς ὀστοῖς, δυνάμενα δὲ καὶ τὰς ἐν ὅλῳ τῷ σώματι γιγνομένας ἑλκώσεις σαρκοῦν.
ἐπὶ γὰρ τῆς κεφαλῆς οὐχ ὡς κεφαλῆς ἁρμόττειν μάλιστα πέφυκεν.
english_sentences: of the External [Remedies], which he entitles 'Marcellas'.] Andromachus [844] mixed together the dry [drugs] suited to an affection with those suited to the affected parts.

But in Asclepiades they have been written separately, in the fifth [book]: those for an affection are marked by headings of their own, and those that go with an affected place likewise by headings of their own.
Without reference to place he has written the cicatrizing and the escharotic [drugs], those suited to spreading ulcers and carbuncles, and the so-called haemostatics.

With reference to an affected place, he has written those for polyp, ozaenae, haemorrhages from the nostrils, spreading ulcers in the mouth, sodden gums, the lumpy swellings on the chin, and those for paronychias, pterygia, fissures in the anus, and haemorrhoids.
Some have also acquired their name from the affected part.
Yet they suit other parts too.
Such are the [drugs] called cephalic by the physicians: they are suited especially to the bones, but they are also able to incarn ulcerations arising in the whole body.
For it is not as the head that they are by nature particularly suited to the head.

beads.greek: ἀμέλει καὶ χωρὶς τοῦ γεγυμνῶσθαι τὸ ὀστοῦν, οὐδὲν αὐτῶν χρῄζομεν, ἀλλ’ ἐπὶ τῶν γεγυμνωμένων, [845] ἐπειδὴ τὴν τῶν λιπαινόντων φαρμάκων χρῆσιν εὐλαβούμεθα, τοῖς ξηροῖς μόνοις χρώμεθα, φεύγοντες τὰ καλούμενα πρὸς τῶν ἰατρῶν ἔμμοτα, διὰ μοτῶν ἐγχριομένων προσφερόμενα.
beads.english: Indeed, when the bone has not been laid bare, we have no need of any of them; but in cases where it has been laid bare, [845] since we are wary of using greasy drugs, we use the dry ones alone, avoiding what physicians call emmota, that is, drugs applied by means of lint smeared with them.

beads.greek: καθάπερ δὲ ἐπὶ τῆς κεφαλῆς γεγυμνωμένων τῶν ὀστῶν ἡ χρῆσις αὐτῶν ἐπιτήδειός ἐστι μάλιστα, κατὰ τοῦτο κᾀπὶ τῶν ἄλλων ἁπάντων ὀστῶν τῶν γεγυμνωμένων εἴτε βραχίων εἴτε πῆχυς εἴτε κερκὶς εἴτε μηρὸς εἴτε κνήμη τύχοι.
beads.english: And just as their use is most suitable when the bones of the head have been laid bare, so it is likewise in all the other bones that have been laid bare, whether it be the upper arm, the ulna, the radius, the thigh or the shin.

beads.greek: διὸ κᾀγὼ τὰ ὑπ’ Ἀσκληπιάδου γεγραμμένα ξηρὰ μέλλων ἐφεξῆς γράφειν, εὑρὼν αὐτὸν ἁπάντων πρῶτα γεγραφότα τὰ κεφαλικὰ καὶ αὐτὸς γράψω πρῶτα διὰ τὸ μὴ μόνον ἐπὶ τῶν ἐν τῇ κεφαλῇ γεγυμνωμένων ὀστῶν, ἀλλὰ καὶ τῶν ἄλλων ἁπάντων ὁμοίως πεπονθότων, ὑπάρχειν αὐτὰ χρήσιμα.
beads.english: Therefore I too, being about to write out next the dry drugs written by Asclepiades, and having found that he wrote the cephalics first of all, will myself also write them first, because they are useful not only for laid-bare bones in the head but also for all the other bones affected in the same way.

beads.greek: δεύτερα δ’ ἐπ’ αὐτοῖς γράψω τὰ ἐπουλωτικὰ, τὰ μεταξὺ πάνθ’ ὑπερβὰς, ὅσα τόπου πεπονθότος ἐφάπτεται.
beads.english: Second after them I shall write the cicatrizing drugs, passing over all those in between that concern an affected place.

beads.greek: μετὰ δὲ τὰ ἐπουλωτικὰ τὰ ἐφεξῆς ἅπαντα κατὰ τὴν προειρημένην ἄρτι μοι τάξιν.
beads.english: And after the cicatrizing drugs, all the rest in turn, in the order I have just stated.

beads.greek: ἔνια μέντοι τῶν ξηρῶν τούτων φαρμάκων διττὴν ἔχει χρῆσιν, ὡς καὶ ξηροῖς αὐτοῖς δύνασθαι χρῆσθαι καὶ μιγνυμένοις ἑτέροις τισὶν, ὡς καὶ αὐτὸς Ἀσκληπιάδης ἐπισημαίνεται.
beads.english: Some of these dry drugs, however, have a twofold use, so that one can use them both dry and mixed with certain other things, as Asclepiades himself also points out.

english_sentences: Indeed, when the bone has not been laid bare, we have no need of any of them; but in cases where it has been laid bare, [845] since we are wary of using greasy drugs, we use the dry ones alone, avoiding what physicians call emmota, that is, drugs applied by means of lint smeared with them.

And just as their use is most suitable when the bones of the head have been laid bare, so it is likewise in all the other bones that have been laid bare, whether it be the upper arm, the ulna, the radius, the thigh or the shin.

Second after them I shall write the cicatrizing drugs, passing over all those in between that concern an affected place.
And after the cicatrizing drugs, all the rest in turn, in the order I have just stated.
Some of these dry drugs, however, have a twofold use, so that one can use them both dry and mixed with certain other things, as Asclepiades himself also points out.

beads.greek: [846] [Ξηρὰ κεφαλικά.] Ξηρὸν κεφαλικὸν ᾧ ἐχρήσατο Λεύκιος ὁ καθηγητής. ἀφίστησι λεπίδας, ἀνάγει ὀστᾶ ἐφθορότα καὶ τὰ κοῖλα σαρκοῖ.

beads.greek: τὸ φάρμακόν ἐστιν ἀλιπές. ♃ ἴρεως Ἰλλυρικῆς δραχ.
beads.english: It detaches scales, brings up corrupted bones and fills hollows with flesh.
The drug is without fat.
Take: Illyrian iris, 4 dr.; panax, 4 dr.; birthwort, 2 dr.; manna, 2 dr.
Others make it without birthwort.
Pound and sift everything; use it on its own and with honey.

beads.greek: ἅπαντα κόπτε καὶ σῆθε, χρῶ κατ’ ἰδίαν καὶ μετὰ μέλιτος. τὸ διὰ τοῦ σιλφίου.
beads.english: The one made with silphium.

beads.greek: τὰ τετυλωμένα ὑπεκτήκει καὶ τὰ ῥυπαρὰ ἀνακαθαίρει καὶ τὰ κοῖλα πληροῖ τῶν ἑλκῶν, τοὺς ὑπολειπομένους χιτωνίσκους ὑπεκτήκει. ♃ ῥητίνης πιτυΐνης ξηρᾶς δραχ.
beads.english: It melts away callused parts, cleans out foul parts and fills the hollows of ulcers; it melts away the little membranes (chitōniskoi) that remain behind.

Use it dry and with honey.

Take: meal of tawny bitter vetch, 8 dr.;

Use it finely ground, and also with honey.

[Use it] dry and with honey.

beads.english: book; and also in this treatise, in the earlier parts, where I showed that, of hollow ulcers without any complication at all, the flesh-producing drugs are of a [848] detergent, non-biting power; that the cicatrizing ones are more drying, together with being astringent without biting; and that those which remove overgrown flesh are hot and acrid.

beads.greek: καὶ μέντοι καὶ τίνα κάλλιστα νομίζω τῶν ἐπουλωτικῶν εἶναι, προείρηταί μοι διὰ τῆς θεραπευτικῆς μεθόδου, καθ’ ἣν ἁπάντων παθῶν τῆς ἰάσεως αἱ μέθοδοι δελήλωνται καὶ τῶν εἰς ἕλκη διαφερουσῶν ἔμπροσθεν ἐν τῇδε τῇ νῦν προκειμένῃ.
beads.english: Moreover, which of the cicatrizing drugs I consider the best has also been stated by me before, in the Therapeutic Method, in which the methods of cure of all affections have been set out, and of those pertaining to ulcers earlier in this present [treatise] now before us.

beads.greek: ὁ δ’ Ἀσκληπιάδης ἔγραψε φάρμακα, καθάπερ καὶ ὁ Ἀνδρόμαχος ἐπουλωτικὰ, μὴ προσδιορισάμενος πότερον ἀπεριστάτων ἑλκῶν ἢ τῶν ἰδίως δυσεπουλώτων λεγομένων, ἃ διαφέρειν ἀλλήλων ἐδείχθη πλείοσι διαφοραῖς, ἴδιον ἑκάστης ἐχούσης σκοπὸν τῆς θεραπείας.
beads.english: Asclepiades, however, wrote down drugs, as did Andromachus too, as cicatrizing, without further specifying whether they are for uncomplicated ulcers or for those properly called hard to cicatrize, which were shown to differ from one another by a number of differences, each having its own aim of treatment.

beads.greek: ἔν τισι μέντοι προσγεγράφασιν ὅτι καὶ πρὸς κακοήθη, ἢ πάλιν, ὅτι πρὸς κονδυλώματα καὶ ῥαγάδας.
beads.english: In some cases, however, they have added in writing that it is also for malignant ones, or again, that it is for condylomata and fissures.

beads.greek: ὁ δ’ Ἀσκληπιάδης καίτοι μᾶλλον τοῦ Ἀνδρομάχου τοὺς ὁρισμοὺς εἰωθὼς προστιθέναι, παρέλιπεν ἐπὶ τῶν ἐπουλωτικῶν.
beads.english: And Asclepiades, although he is more accustomed than Andromachus to add the specifications, omitted them in the case of the cicatrizing drugs.

beads.greek: ἀλλ’ ἐξ ὧν ἐγὼ διῆλθον, ἔν τε τῇ θεραπευτικῇ πραγματείᾳ καὶ τῇ νῦν ἐνεστώσῃ δῆλον ἔσται τοῖς προσέχουσι τὸν νοῦν, ὅπως ἑκάστῳ τῶν γεγραμμένων χρηστέον.
beads.english: But from what I have set out, both in the therapeutic treatise and in the present one, it will be clear to those who pay attention how each of the recorded drugs is to be used.

ὁ δ’ Ἀσκληπιάδης ἔγραψε φάρμακα, καθάπερ καὶ ὁ Ἀνδρόμαχος ἐπουλωτικὰ, μὴ προσδιορισάμενος πότερον ἀπεριστάτων ἑλκῶν ἢ τῶν ἰδίως δυσεπουλώτων λεγομένων, ἃ διαφέρειν ἀλλήλων ἐδείχθη πλείοσι διαφοραῖς, ἴδιον ἑκάστης ἐχούσης σκοπὸν τῆς θεραπείας.
ἔν τισι μέντοι προσγεγράφασιν ὅτι καὶ πρὸς κακοήθη, ἢ πάλιν, ὅτι πρὸς κονδυλώματα καὶ ῥαγάδας.
ὁ δ’ Ἀσκληπιάδης καίτοι μᾶλλον τοῦ Ἀνδρομάχου τοὺς ὁρισμοὺς εἰωθὼς προστιθέναι, παρέλιπεν ἐπὶ τῶν ἐπουλωτικῶν.
ἀλλ’ ἐξ ὧν ἐγὼ διῆλθον, ἔν τε τῇ θεραπευτικῇ πραγματείᾳ καὶ τῇ νῦν ἐνεστώσῃ δῆλον ἔσται τοῖς προσέχουσι τὸν νοῦν, ὅπως ἑκάστῳ τῶν γεγραμμένων χρηστέον.
english_sentences: book; and also in this treatise, in the earlier parts, where I showed that, of hollow ulcers without any complication at all, the flesh-producing drugs are of a [848] detergent, non-biting power; that the cicatrizing ones are more drying, together with being astringent without biting; and that those which remove overgrown flesh are hot and acrid.

Moreover, which of the cicatrizing drugs I consider the best has also been stated by me before, in the Therapeutic Method, in which the methods of cure of all affections have been set out, and of those pertaining to ulcers earlier in this present [treatise] now before us.

Asclepiades, however, wrote down drugs, as did Andromachus too, as cicatrizing, without further specifying whether they are for uncomplicated ulcers or for those properly called hard to cicatrize, which were shown to differ from one another by a number of differences, each having its own aim of treatment.
In some cases, however, they have added in writing that it is also for malignant ones, or again, that it is for condylomata and fissures.
And Asclepiades, although he is more accustomed than Andromachus to add the specifications, omitted them in the case of the cicatrizing drugs.
But from what I have set out, both in the therapeutic treatise and in the present one, it will be clear to those who pay attention how each of the recorded drugs is to be used.

τὰ δὲ τῆς συνθέσεως ἔχει οὕτως.

♃ χάρτου κεκαυμένου, μολύβδου κεκαυμένου καὶ χαλκοῦ κεκαυμένου καὶ πεπλυμένου, ἀρσενικοῦ, λεπίδος στομώματος ἑκάστου ἴσον, θείου ἀπύρου τὸ ἥμισυ, λείοις χρῶ ἢ μετὰ μέλιτος ἢ ῥοδίνου Μοσχίωνος πρὸς νομάς.
λεπίδος χαλκοῦ δραχμὰς δύο, ἀρσενικοῦ δραχμὰς δ΄.
ἁλὸς ἀμμωνιακοῦ δραχμὴν μίαν, λείοις χρῶ μετὰ ῥοδίνου.
english_sentences: As [853] Ptolemy used it: ℞ burnt lead, orpiment, flake, burnt papyrus, 4 dr. of each; sulphur untouched by fire, 2 dr.
Use finely ground.
As Apelles used it: a successful drug, entitled 'the one with papyrus', for spreading ulcers.
It not only arrests the spreading ulcer but also prevents it when it is beginning.
It is also effective for dysenteric patients when infused with rose oil.
But when, he says, on being infused in dysenteric patients it produces a biting sensation, the spreading ulcer is to be suspected.
The composition is as follows. ℞ burnt papyrus, burnt lead, and burnt and washed copper, orpiment, flake of steel, an equal amount of each; sulphur untouched by fire, half that amount.
Use finely ground, either with honey or with rose oil.
Moschion's, for spreading ulcers. ℞ elaterium, 2 drachms; burnt papyrus, 2 drachms; copper flake, two drachms; orpiment, 4 drachms; worm verdigris, 1 drachm; ammoniac salt, one drachm.
Use finely ground with rose oil.
[The fragrant remedy of Lucius the teacher.] ℞ flake, 4 dr.; oak gall, 4 drachms; sandarach, 2 dr.; orpiment, 2 drachms; myrrh, 1 drachm; chalcanthum, 1 drachm.

beads.greek: χάρτου κεκαυμένου ὥστε χρῶσαι. ὡς δὲ ἡμεῖς.
beads.english: of frankincense [854] 2 dr., of elaterium 1 dr., of burnt papyrus enough to colour it.

beads.greek: χάρτου ὥστε χρῶσαι. ὡς δὲ Πρασίων.
beads.english: As we ourselves make it: ℞ of flake 8 dr., of oak-gall 8 dr., of myrrh 8 dr., of realgar 4 dr., of orpiment 4 dr., of elaterium 4 dr., of frankincense 3 dr., of chalcanthum 3 dr., of papyrus enough to colour it.
As Prasion makes it: ℞ of orpiment 2 dr., of flake 2 dr., of chalcanthum 1 drachm, of realgar 2 dr., of myrrh 1 drachm, of frankincense 1 dr., of oak-galls 1 drachm, of papyrus 4 dr.;
[use it] ground very fine, and also with rose oil.

beads.greek: λείοις καὶ μετὰ ῥοδίνου. Ἡρακλείδης δὲ ταύτην εἶχε τὴν γραφήν.
beads.english: Heracleides had this formula: ℞ of oak-galls 6 dr., of orpiment 4 dr., of realgar 4 dr., of flake 4 dr., of frankincense 3 dr., of chalcanthum 3 dr., of Minaean myrrh 2 dr., of papyrus 8 dr.

beads.greek: λιβάνου δραχμὴν α΄. χαλκάνθου δραχμὴν α΄.
beads.english: As Cleobulus makes it: ℞ of flake 2 dr., of realgar 2 dr., of orpiment 2 dr., of myrrh 1 drachm, of frankincense 1 drachm, of chalcanthum 1 drachm, of oak-gall 1 dr., of papyrus enough to colour it.

greek_sentences: Ἡρακλείδης δὲ ταύτην εἶχε τὴν γραφήν.
english_sentences: of frankincense [854] 2 dr., of elaterium 1 dr., of burnt papyrus enough to colour it.

As we ourselves make it: ℞ of flake 8 dr., of oak-gall 8 dr., of myrrh 8 dr., of realgar 4 dr., of orpiment 4 dr., of elaterium 4 dr., of frankincense 3 dr., of chalcanthum 3 dr., of papyrus enough to colour it.
As Prasion makes it: ℞ of orpiment 2 dr., of flake 2 dr., of chalcanthum 1 drachm, of realgar 2 dr., of myrrh 1 drachm, of frankincense 1 dr., of oak-galls 1 drachm, of papyrus 4 dr.;
[use it] ground very fine, and also with rose oil.
Heracleides had this formula: ℞ of oak-galls 6 dr., of orpiment 4 dr., of realgar 4 dr., of flake 4 dr., of frankincense 3 dr., of chalcanthum 3 dr., of Minaean myrrh 2 dr., of papyrus 8 dr.
As Cleobulus makes it: ℞ of flake 2 dr., of realgar 2 dr., of orpiment 2 dr., of myrrh 1 drachm, of frankincense 1 drachm, of chalcanthum 1 drachm, of oak-gall 1 dr., of papyrus enough to colour it.

beads.greek: [Πρὸς ἄνθρακας.] Ὁ ἄνθραξ ἕλκος ἐστὶν, ἐσχάραν ταχὺ ποιοῦν, μετὰ φλεγμονῆς ἰσχυρᾶς τοῦ πέριξ μορίου παντὸς, ὥστε καὶ πυρετοὺς ἐπιφέρεσθαι σφοδροὺς [855] καὶ κινδύνους ἐσχάτους, ὥστε χρὴ κατ’ αὐτῆς μὲν τῆς ἐσχάρας ἰσχυρὸν τιθέναι φάρμακον, καὶ τούτων γε ὁποῖα πρὸς νομὰς ἁρμόζειν εἴρηται, τὰ δὲ πέριξ καταπλάσσειν καταπλάσμασιν ὁμαλὴν ἔχουσι δύναμιν, ὡς ἀποκρούεσθαί τε καὶ μετρίως ἐμψύχειν καὶ διαφορεῖν.
ἀλλὰ περὶ μὲν τῶν καταπλασμάτων ἐν τῇ περὶ τούτων πραγματείᾳ λέλεκται· νυνὶ δὲ τῶν ὑπ’ Ἀσκληπιάδου γεγραμμένων μνημονεύσομεν. πρὸς ἄνθρακας τὰ ὑπ’ Ἀσκληπιάδου.
beads.english: [For carbuncles.] The carbuncle is an ulcer that quickly produces an eschar, with strong inflammation of the whole surrounding part, so that violent fevers also supervene [855] and extreme dangers.

beads.greek: ἡ τοῦ Μασσαλιώτου. ταύτην ἐξέθηκε τῇ πόλει πρὸς τὴν δύναμιν, διὰ τὸ τοὺς ἄνθρακας ἐπιπολάζειν καὶ πολλοὺς ἀφαιρεῖσθαι.
beads.english: Hence one must place a strong drug on the eschar itself, and indeed of these drugs such as have been said to suit spreading ulcers, and plaster the surrounding parts with poultices having an even power, so as both to repel and moderately to cool and to disperse.
But concerning poultices it has been said in the treatise on them; now we shall record those written by Asclepiades.
For carbuncles, those of Asclepiades.
That of the Massiliote.

He set this one out publicly for the city, in proportion to its power (?), because carbuncles were rife and carried off many. ♃ Chrysocolla 4 dr., roasted nitre 4 dr., Assian stone 4 dr., arsenikon 4 dr., sandarach 4 dr., roasted misy 4 dr., chalcitis 4 dr., split alum 4 dr., diphryges 4 dr.

beads.greek: δ΄. τρίψαντες καθ’ ἓν καὶ ὁμοῦ ἀποτιθέμεθα εἰς ἀγγεῖον χαλκοῦν Κύπριον.
beads.english: Having ground them separately and together, we store them in a Cyprian copper vessel.

beads.greek: ἐπὶ δὲ τῆς χρήσεως ἐπιτίθεμεν προσθλίβοντες τῷ πλάτει τῆς μήλης, ἕως μελανθῇ ὁ ἄνθραξ, εἶτ’ ἐπιτίθεμεν ἐπάνω τὴν ὑπογεγραμμένην χλωράν. ἔστι δὲ αὕτη.
beads.english: At the time of use we apply it, pressing it on with the flat of the probe, until the carbuncle turns black; then we put on top the green salve written below.
It is this: ♃ frankincense 1 dr., scraped verdigris 1 dr.

Hence one must place a strong drug on the eschar itself, and indeed of these drugs such as have been said to suit spreading ulcers, and plaster the surrounding parts with poultices having an even power, so as both to repel and moderately to cool and to disperse.
But concerning poultices it has been said in the treatise on them; now we shall record those written by Asclepiades.
For carbuncles, those of Asclepiades.
That of the Massiliote.

He set this one out publicly for the city, in proportion to its power (?), because carbuncles were rife and carried off many. ♃ Chrysocolla 4 dr., roasted nitre 4 dr., Assian stone 4 dr., arsenikon 4 dr., sandarach 4 dr., roasted misy 4 dr., chalcitis 4 dr., split alum 4 dr., diphryges 4 dr.
Having ground them separately and together, we store them in a Cyprian copper vessel.
At the time of use we apply it, pressing it on with the flat of the probe, until the carbuncle turns black; then we put on top the green salve written below.
It is this: ♃ frankincense 1 dr., scraped verdigris 1 dr.

beads.greek: λεπίδος χαλκοῦ δραχμὴν [856] μίαν, στυπτηρίας σχιστῆς ὀβολοὺς τέσσαρας, ἁλὸς ἀμμωνιακοῦ ὀβολοὺς τέσσαρας, κηροῦ δραχμὰς ζ΄. ὀβολοὺς τρεῖς, ῥητίνης πιτυΐνης ξηρᾶς δραχμὰς ιε΄.
beads.english: one drachm [856] of copper flake, four obols of split alum, four obols of ammoniac salt, 7 drachms 3 obols of wax, 15 drachms of dry pine resin, 1 kotyle of old oil.

beads.greek: ἐλαίου παλαιοῦ κοτύλην α΄. τὰ ξηρὰ τρῖβε ἐν ἡλίῳ μετὰ ὄξους.
beads.english: Grind the dry ingredients in the sun with vinegar.

beads.greek: τὰ δὲ τηκτὰ τῆκε καὶ κατέρα καὶ ἀνακόψας ἀνελόμενος χρῶ. παρὰ Δημοσθένει τῷ Μασσαλιώτῃ τῷ τε φάρμακον συντιθέντι ἐλαίου ἔχει κοτύλας δύο.
beads.english: Melt the meltable ones, pour them in, and when you have beaten it up and taken it out, use it.

beads.greek: [Ἀπίωνος πρὸς ἄνθρακας.] ♃ Νίτρου ἐρυθροῦ, ἀρσενικοῦ, σανδαράχης, χαλκίτεως, χαλκάνθου, διφρυγοῦς, ἑκάστου τὸ ἴσον, ὄξει λειοτριβῶν καὶ ξηράνας καὶ πάλιν τρίψας χρῶ.
Ἀπολλωνίου ὀργανικοῦ. ♃ χρυσοκόλλης δραχμὴν μίαν, στυπτηρίας σχιστῆς δραχμὴν α΄.
beads.english: In Demosthenes of Massalia, who also compounded the drug, it has two kotylai of oil.

beads.greek: καὶ στρογγύλης δραχμὴν μίαν, σανδαράχης δραχμὴν μίαν, ὤχρας δραχμὴν α΄. μίσυος ὠμοῦ δραχμὴν α΄.
beads.english: [Apion's, for carbuncles.] Take red natron, arsenic, sandarach, chalcitis, chalcanthum, diphryges, an equal amount of each; grind smooth with vinegar, dry, grind again, and use.
Of Apollonius Organicus.

beads.greek: ἡ ἀνθίζουσα Μάγνου πρὸς σηπεδόνας, νομὰς, ἄνθρακας, πτερύγια, ὦτα πυοῤῥοοῦντα, ποιεῖ καὶ πρὸς τὰς ἐν τῷ στόματι νομάς. ♃ στυπτηρίας σχιστῆς δραχ.
beads.english: Take 1 drachm of chrysocolla, 1 drachm of split alum and 1 drachm of round alum, 1 drachm of sandarach, 1 drachm of ochre, 1 drachm of raw misy, 1 drachm of chalcanthum.
Use them finely ground.
The 'flowering' remedy of Magnus, for putrefactions, spreading ulcers, carbuncles, pterygia and ears running with pus; it is also effective against spreading ulcers in the mouth.
Take 8 drachms of split alum, 6 drachms of chalcitis, 3 drachms of sandarach, 2 drachms of dried pomegranate rinds, 1 drachm of chalcanthum.

greek_sentences: λεπίδος χαλκοῦ δραχμὴν [856] μίαν, στυπτηρίας σχιστῆς ὀβολοὺς τέσσαρας, ἁλὸς ἀμμωνιακοῦ ὀβολοὺς τέσσαρας, κηροῦ δραχμὰς ζ΄.
ὀβολοὺς τρεῖς, ῥητίνης πιτυΐνης ξηρᾶς δραχμὰς ιε΄.

beads.greek: χρῶ ξηρῷ καὶ μετὰ μέλιτος. ἄλλο Διοδώρου.
beads.english: [857] of misy, 2 dr.; of nitre, 2 dr.; of dry omphacine, 2 dr.
Use it dry, and also with honey.

beads.greek: στυπτηρίας σχιστῆς, χαλκάνθου, λίθου Ἀσίου, διφρυγοῦς, νίτρου ἐρυθροῦ ἀνὰ δραχ. α΄.
beads.english: Another, of Diodorus. ℞ Omphacine oak-gall, 4 dr.; misy, 2 dr.; chalcitis, 2 dr.; arsenikon, 2 dr.; sandarach, 2 dr.; split alum, chalcanthum, Assian stone, diphryges, red nitre, 1 dr. of each.

beads.greek: λείοις κατάπασσε παραπτόμενος πυρῆνι μήλῃ. ἴσχαιμος Ἀσκληπιάδου.
beads.english: Sprinkle on in powdered form, touching the place with the knob (pyrēn) of a probe.

beads.greek: Λευκίου καθηγητοῦ φάρμακον ἐπιτετευγμένον. ♃ χαλκίτεως δραχ.
beads.english: The blood-staunching remedy of Asclepiades; a successful drug of Lucius the teacher. ℞ Chalcitis, 16 dr.; manna, 12 dr.; terebinth kneaded with vinegar [no quantity given].

beads.greek: ιβ΄. τερμινθίνης ὄξει πεφυρμένης, ξηροῖς κατάπασσε τοὺς αἱμοῤῥαγοῦντας τόπους.
beads.english: Sprinkle the bleeding places with the dry ingredients.

beads.greek: ἐν ἄλλαις δύο εὑρήκαμεν γραφαῖς μᾶλλον. ♃ χαλκίτεως δραχ.
beads.english: In two other copies we have found instead (?): ℞ chalcitis, 8 dr.; manna, 16 dr.; roasted terebinth, 16 dr.

beads.greek: ὡς δὲ Διοσκορίδης ὁ Ταρσεὺς ἔδωκεν Ἀρείῳ τῷ Ἀσκληπιαδείῳ θαυμαστῶς κατέχον τὰς αἱμοῤῥαγίας. ♃ χαλκίτεως δραχ.
beads.english: And as Dioscorides of Tarsus gave it to Areius the Asclepiadean, wonderfully checking haemorrhages: ℞ Chalcitis, 8 dr.; manna, 16 dr.; dry resin, 8 dr.; gypsum, 8 dr.

beads.greek: η΄. τὰ μὲν ἄλλα κόπτεται καὶ σήθεται καὶ μίγνυται καὶ ἀποτίθεται εἰς χαλκῆν πυξίδα.
beads.english: The other ingredients are pounded, sifted, mixed and stored in a bronze box; at the time of use an equal amount of the drug is mixed with the gypsum.

beads.greek: ἐπὶ δὲ τῆς χρήσεως ἴσον τοῦ φαρμάκου τῇ γύψῳ μίγνυται. ἐκ τῶν Ἡρακλείδου πρὸς αἱμοῤῥοΐδας.
beads.english: From the writings of Heraclides, for haemorrhoids.

greek_sentences: στυπτηρίας σχιστῆς, χαλκάνθου, λίθου Ἀσίου, διφρυγοῦς, νίτρου ἐρυθροῦ ἀνὰ δραχ.
τερμινθίνης ὄξει πεφυρμένης, ξηροῖς κατάπασσε τοὺς αἱμοῤῥαγοῦντας τόπους.
ἐν ἄλλαις δύο εὑρήκαμεν γραφαῖς μᾶλλον.
ὡς δὲ Διοσκορίδης ὁ Ταρσεὺς ἔδωκεν Ἀρείῳ τῷ Ἀσκληπιαδείῳ θαυμαστῶς κατέχον τὰς αἱμοῤῥαγίας.
τὰ μὲν ἄλλα κόπτεται καὶ σήθεται καὶ μίγνυται καὶ ἀποτίθεται εἰς χαλκῆν πυξίδα.
ἐπὶ δὲ τῆς χρήσεως ἴσον τοῦ φαρμάκου τῇ γύψῳ μίγνυται.

beads.greek: τούτῳ ἐχρήσατο πρὸς [858] τὰς τῶν μυκτήρων αἱμοῤῥαγίας, ἔριον καταβάπτων καὶ συστρέφων ὥσπερ ἐλλύχνιον. ♃ σιδίων ὀξείας ῥοιᾶς οὐγγίας γ΄.
beads.english: He used this for [858] haemorrhages of the nostrils, dipping wool into it and twisting it like a lamp-wick.

beads.greek: στυπτηρίας Αἰγυπτίας οὐγγίας δ΄. χαλκίτεως γο α΄.
beads.english: Rx: rinds of sour pomegranate, 3 ounces;

beads.greek: λείοις χρῶ. ἐπὶ δὲ τῶν μυκτήρων ἔριον πληρώσας τοῦ φαρμάκου ἐντίθει.
beads.english: Egyptian alum, 4 ounces; chalcitis, 1 ounce.

beads.greek: τούτῳ ἀντὶ καυτηρίου ἐχρήσατο, ἔστι δὲ ἐσχαρωτικόν.
ποιεῖ καὶ πρὸς πτερύγια, καταστέλλει πᾶσαν ἐξοχὴν, ὀστᾶ ἀνάγει, ἀφίστησι λεπίδας.

beads.english: Use ground fine.
For the nostrils, fill wool with the drug and insert it.
The so-called 'Heracles', for haemorrhages.
He used this in place of a cautery, and it is escharotic.
It is also effective for pterygia, reduces every excrescence, brings up bones, and detaches scales.
Rx: sory, 4 drachms; chalcanthum, 4 drachms; burnt chalcitis, 4 drachms; tanners' sumach, 4 drachms.
Use ground fine.
A successful blood-staunching drug.

beads.greek: ♃ λιβάνου γο α΄. μίσυος ξενικοῦ δραχ.
beads.english: Rx: foreign misy, 6 drachms; chalcanthum, 6 drachms; pine bark, 4 drachms; chalcitis, 4 drachms; manna, 4 drachms (others: 20); gypsum, 4 drachms.
Use ground fine.
Another.
Rx: frankincense, 1 ounce; foreign misy, 4 drachms; unripe oak-galls, 4 drachms; chalcitis, 4 drachms; burnt cork, 8 drachms; tanners' sumach, 4 drachms.
Use ground fine.

greek_sentences: τούτῳ ἐχρήσατο πρὸς [858] τὰς τῶν μυκτήρων αἱμοῤῥαγίας, ἔριον καταβάπτων καὶ συστρέφων ὥσπερ ἐλλύχνιον.
ἐπὶ δὲ τῶν μυκτήρων ἔριον πληρώσας τοῦ φαρμάκου ἐντίθει.
τούτῳ ἀντὶ καυτηρίου ἐχρήσατο, ἔστι δὲ ἐσχαρωτικόν.
ποιεῖ καὶ πρὸς πτερύγια, καταστέλλει πᾶσαν ἐξοχὴν, ὀστᾶ ἀνάγει, ἀφίστησι λεπίδας.

Rx: rinds of sour pomegranate, 3 ounces;
Egyptian alum, 4 ounces; chalcitis, 1 ounce.
Use ground fine.
For the nostrils, fill wool with the drug and insert it.
The so-called 'Heracles', for haemorrhages.
He used this in place of a cautery, and it is escharotic.
It is also effective for pterygia, reduces every excrescence, brings up bones, and detaches scales.
Rx: sory, 4 drachms; chalcanthum, 4 drachms; burnt chalcitis, 4 drachms; tanners' sumach, 4 drachms.
Use ground fine.
A successful blood-staunching drug.

Use ground fine.
